documents.title: Carbon reference adoption review
documents.markdown:
# Carbon reference adoption review

Reviewed: 2026-10-12. **Draft: official reference/source comparison and proposals**.
This is not a record of completed app comparison, Core adoption or full Storybook review.
Follow the [review order](review.md): Button → Field → Toolbar → Table → App Dialog.
Official code was checked at Carbon commit `47ab67155b185d56bf147b33cd9536e479ab0203`.

## Buttons and icons: values and roles

| Subject          | Official Carbon basis                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Geul choice and review                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command default  | React Button uses kind=primary. [Source](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/blob/47ab67155b185d56bf147b33cd9536e479ab0203/packages/react/src/components/Button/Button.tsx)                                            | Retain neutral/medium, IconButton neutral/low and the existing palette. Carbon primary does not become the ordinary app-command default.                          |
| Label↔icon       | Ghost uses 8px (`spacing-03`), distinct from ordinary button examples with 16px or more/32px. [Specifications](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/button/specifications)                          | Compare shared 8px gap and the existing compact-header 4px gap. Do not copy 32px into unfilled commands.                                                          |
| Glyph            | Ordinary buttons use 16×16; expressive uses 20×20. Same specifications.                                                                                                                                                           | Retain `chrome-icon-size` 16px. Larger button heights do not automatically enlarge the glyph.                                                                     |
| Icon-only box    | SCSS uses padding=0, width/height=layout height and ghost icon margin=0. [SCSS](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/blob/47ab67155b185d56bf147b33cd9536e479ab0203/packages/styles/scss/components/button/_button.scss) | Geul also uses padding=0. Do not add the documented icon-only 16px clearance as padding to every size. Separate square target, viewBox clearance and wrapper gap. |
| Control height   | Carbon xs/sm/md/lg=24/32/40/48px; full-bleed xl/2xl=64/80px. [Specifications](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/button/specifications)                                                           | Retain Geul xs/sm/md/lg/xl=30/36/42/50/60px, compact=28, chrome=32px and compare actual consumers first. Matching size names do not imply matching values.        |
| Between commands | Carbon fixed button-group spacing of 16px is composition guidance, not a value built into each button. Same specifications.                                                                                                       | Separate internal command gap from external action-row gap. Do not set every toolbar/table control gap to 16px.                                                   |

IBM artboard padding is **clearance inside the glyph frame**. Optical path bounds do not always fill the live area.
[IBM UI icon usage](https://www.ibm.com/design/language/iconography/ui-icons/usage/).

| Artboard | Internal padding | Live area | Official SVG viewBox example                                                                                                                         |
| -------- | ---------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 16px     | 1px              | 14px      | [0 0 16 16](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/blob/47ab67155b185d56bf147b33cd9536e479ab0203/packages/icons/src/svg/16/arrow--right.svg) |
| 20px     | 1.25px           | 17.5px    | [0 0 20 20](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/blob/47ab67155b185d56bf147b33cd9536e479ab0203/packages/icons/src/svg/20/arrow--right.svg) |
| 24px     | 1.5px            | 21px      | [0 0 24 24](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/blob/47ab67155b185d56bf147b33cd9536e479ab0203/packages/icons/src/svg/24/arrow--right.svg) |
| 32px     | 2px              | 28px      | [0 0 32 32](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/blob/47ab67155b185d56bf147b33cd9536e479ab0203/packages/icons/src/svg/32/arrow--right.svg) |

IBM documents a 32px production grid and optical centering in its [design guidance](https://www.ibm.com/design/language/iconography/ui-icons/design/).
Geul's [IconButton](../../components/core/IconButton/IconButton.tsx) displays Tabler viewBox24 glyphs in a 16px box.
Do not apply IBM's filled glyph/stroke/Plex combination directly to Tabler/Noto or crop paths to fill the frame.
Compare original proportions, optical alignment and stroke weight; record glyph clearance, CSS padding and target size separately.

IBM's touch guidance requires at least 44px and can use CSS clearance around a small glyph.
[IBM clearance](https://www.ibm.com/design/language/iconography/ui-icons/usage/).
Retain Geul's coarse-pointer 44px minimum and 16px input text.
This does not require every fine-pointer icon target or glyph to become 44px.
Do not equate this value with WCAG AA's minimum target criterion. See the [Geul density contract](size-density-contract.md).

## Spacing proposals and actual comparison

Carbon distinguishes small internal spacing from larger grouping in its 2/4/8px-based scale;
Stack owns spacing between children. Token values themselves do not vary with screen width.
[Spacing](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/foundations/spacing/overview).
Geul's [token owner](../../@echovisionlab/design-system/tokens) uses 4/8/10/12/16/24px.
Do not remove 10px simply because it is absent from Carbon.

Define glyph size, label-icon gap, control inline padding, action-row gap and section spacing as shared roles that reference the existing scale.
Keep meaning distinct even when values match. [Control CSS](../../components/core/Control.module.css) owns button/icon internals;
[control-context](../../components/core/control-context.tsx) owns size inheritance; Core Layout/Toolbar owns external composition.

When icon clearance looks excessive, measure computed control box, glyph frame/path bounds, actual padding, parent gap and
ActionRowSizeProvider/ToolbarDensityProvider inheritance first.
Fix unnecessary wrapper space or incorrect density inheritance at the shared owner.
Compact HeaderDensity uses the existing 4px internal gap; compact control size is 28px.
Compact size alone retains the ordinary 8px label gap. Coarse targets occupy at least 44px without overlap.
Do not uniformly reduce height/width, SVG proportions or outlines without measurements.

Compare actual consumers across valid Button APIs, default/hover/pressed/focus/disabled/pending, Light/Dark,
long Korean/English, RTL, labelWrap and sections/indicator.
390/834/1440px are representative mobile/tablet/desktop widths; include 320px and Geul breakpoint boundaries.
Verify Tab, Space/Enter, names, toggle state and pending locks through actual behavior.
Carbon covers icon-only hover/focus names separately from toggle semantics in [Button accessibility](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/button/accessibility).
Geul href retains navigation-link semantics. Do not apply Carbon's button-role link policy to every link.
Review tooltip visibility, accessible names and touch separately; Carbon's accessibility results are not Geul evidence.

## Storybook documentation and example standards

Carbon 2x Grid describes product-screen structure: an 8px mini unit, fixed padding 16px,
32px gutters when needed and 4/8/16 columns by breakpoint.
[2x Grid](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/foundations/2x-grid/overview).
Geul retains its existing breakpoint/content-width owners.

Use the same document order: purpose, anatomy, public API, geometry, states, content, responsive behavior,
accessibility, consumers and verification scope.
Examples use production Core and link to the contract/source owner.
Documentation specimen padding and maximum widths are not product specifications.

Core examples isolate component geometry and states. Composition examples review parent gaps and reading order.
Pages examples review actual View tasks and failure/recovery. Distinguish fixed-state specimens from actual interactions.
Document headless providers and hooks by responsibility and behavior.

Compare the same source, args, theme and locale at 390/834/1440px.
Record actual iframe CSS viewport, wrapper/product surface widths and pointer conditions.
Review long content, resizing, Light/Dark and keyboard states in the browser; retain unexecuted checks as pending.
Follow shared preview and toolbar ownership in the [Storybook guide](../ui-kit.md).

documents.title: Geul design system writing criteria based on Carbon
documents.markdown:
# Geul design system writing criteria based on Carbon

Updated: 2026-10-12. This is a writing and review policy, not a report that every criterion has passed.

Use Carbon's approach to specifications. Current Geul tokens, theme and Core own color, typography, geometry and interaction.
Keep documentation and actual running examples together in Storybook, and review changes in actual consumers.

## 1. References and application scope

| Subject                  | Official Carbon reference                                                                                                                                                                    | Geul policy                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tokens and themes        | Names and meaning remain stable while theme values change. [Themes](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/foundations/themes/overview)                                          | The same Core consumes the same semantic roles in Light/Dark.                                                                           |
| Role boundaries          | Shared roles are distinct from component roles. [Color overview](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/foundations/color/overview)                                              | Distinguish primitive, semantic, invariant and derived roles. Equal values do not imply equal meaning.                                  |
| Typography               | Size, weight and line height form roles. [Typography](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/foundations/typography/overview)                                                    | Document body, heading, command, supporting text and locale-specific fonts.                                                             |
| Spacing                  | Internal and external spacing have separate owners. [Spacing](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/foundations/spacing/overview)                                               | Core owns internal padding/gap; compositions consume Core Layout for external spacing.                                                  |
| Responsive layout        | Screen structure and breakpoint-specific design. [2x Grid](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/foundations/2x-grid/overview)                                                  | Review mobile, tablet, desktop and Geul breakpoint boundaries.                                                                          |
| Component specifications | Anatomy, geometry, states, content and overflow accompany code and documentation. [Component checklist](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/getting-started/contributing/component-checklist) | Connect public API, tokens, running examples, consumers and verification scope.                                                         |
| Content                  | Terminology and input/error/context guidance. [Content](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/foundations/content)                                                              | State conditions, actions and results precisely. Exclude unmeasurable praise from specifications.                                       |
| Accessibility            | Names, descriptions, errors, keyboard and automatic/manual checks. [Text input accessibility](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/text-input/accessibility)   | Review actual DOM semantics, keyboard, focus, contrast and recovery. Record automatic and actual assistive technology scope separately. |

Do not adopt IBM Blue, IBM Plex, Carbon's primary button default, padding or grid values as Geul defaults.
Distinguish [Carbon Button](https://carbondesignsystem.com/components/button/usage/) from Geul's neutral/medium and neutral/low contracts.
This policy does not require installing Carbon or replacing components.

## 2. Owners and Storybook representation

| Decision                                             | Source owner/document                                     | Storybook evidence                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Palette, spacing, size, boundary, opacity and motion | `@echovisionlab/design-system/tokens` → `primitiveTokens` | Roles, units, values and actual consumption examples                    |
| Light/Dark semantic colors                           | Same module → `semanticThemes`                            | Theme values under the same roles and rendering of the same Core        |
| Image overlays, canvases and print                   | Same module → `invariantTokens`                           | Theme-independent meaning and use context                               |
| Derived roles                                        | `derivedTokenRoles`; [token contract](token-contract.md)  | Source aliases and consumers; do not flatten aliases into copied values |
| Locale and fonts                                     | `lib/styles/font-assignment.css`                          | Actual locale fonts, direction and long translations                    |
| Runtime and preview theme                            | `theme.ts`, `.storybook/preview.tsx`                      | Shared app provider and CSS baseline                                    |
| Anatomy, states and closed API                       | `components/core/**`; [ownership](ownership-contract.md)  | Purpose, anatomy, props, supported states and accepted/rejected usage   |
| Layout and responsive composition                    | Core Layout; [density contract](size-density-contract.md) | Parent width, gap, wrapping, overflow and state preservation            |
| Input semantics and validation                       | Core Input; [input contract](input-contract.md)           | Label/value/description/error/actions relationships and actual input    |
| Consumers and previews                               | [Generated inventory](generated-inventory.md)             | Source owner, story, route/View mapping and inclusion boundaries        |

Follow [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) and the [design system](../design-system.md).
Do not bypass Core through Feature CSS or arbitrary presentation props.

## 3. Writing order and deliverables

| Order | Subject               | Deliverable                                                                                                          |
| ----- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1     | Foundations           | Token intent, values, aliases, themes, typography, spacing, icons, motion and responsive rules with examples         |
| 2     | Core components       | Purpose, anatomy, closed API, geometry, states, content, accessibility, consumers and running examples               |
| 3     | Repeated compositions | Parent layout and behavior of Field, ActionRow, Toolbar, Section, Navigation and Dialog                              |
| 4     | Pages                 | Actual Views, fixture data, tasks, failure/recovery, route and service boundaries                                    |
| 5     | Verification          | Accepted/rejected types, behavior regressions, story play, browser measurements, manual results and unresolved items |

Readers must be able to read Docs and exercise the relevant implementation in Canvas.
Do not substitute whole-screen images or imitation components with different source for actual examples.
Document provider, hook and controller responsibilities through code contracts and consuming compositions.

## 4. Component specification format

| Field                     | Required content                                                                              |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Purpose                   | Function, use conditions and selection between similar parts                                  |
| Anatomy                   | Order and owners of root, label, icon, value, description, error and actions                  |
| API                       | Public props, allowed values, defaults, required relationships and source owner               |
| Geometry                  | Owned tokens for height, target, padding, gap, boundary, text and icon                        |
| States                    | Actual default/hover/focus/pressed/selected/disabled/pending/readOnly/invalid support         |
| Combinations              | Visual precedence of valid states such as focus+invalid, unsupported combinations and reasons |
| Content                   | Short/long/empty values, multiline content, icons, locale, RTL, overflow, wrap and ellipsis   |
| Layout                    | Content/full/fixed width, min/max, parent resizing and breakpoint changes                     |
| Interaction/accessibility | Names, descriptions, relationships, state, keyboard, focus and error recovery                 |
| Usage                     | Actual consumers, accepted usage, rejected bypasses and related running stories               |
| Verification              | Executed environment, evidence, unresolved items, owner and change date                       |

Use the shared [component documentation](component-documentation.md) and [page documentation](page-documentation.md) formats.
Write a specification as `condition → behavior → verification`. For example: a coarse pointer requires a minimum
44px command height occupying actual layout space; check that adjacent targets do not overlap.

Define valid APIs and important combinations before adding a Cartesian specimen matrix.
Supported contract, example list and executed checks are separate information. Example counts are not complete verification.

## 5. Mobile, tablet and desktop review

Representative CSS viewports are 390×844, 834×1112 and 1440×900px.
Geul xs/sm/md/lg/xl breakpoints are 576/768/992/1200/1408px.
Form/compact/standard/wide maximum content widths are 448/768/992/1200px and serve a different purpose from transition boundaries.
Values assume the default 16px root.

| Environment | Required review                                                                                           |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mobile      | Single flow, navigation changes, command labels, keyboard, safe-area, dialogs/scroll and long input       |
| Tablet      | Split/merge boundaries, portrait/landscape and simultaneous touch/pointer use                             |
| Desktop     | Maximum content width, columns, toolbar/table density, keyboard movement and hierarchy                    |
| Shared      | Focus, selection, errors, readOnly, pending, Light/Dark, long translations, RTL, text zoom and low height |

Also inspect 320px and just below/at/above relevant breakpoints. Record actual iframe viewport, wrapper and product surface widths.
A viewport name does not establish touch/coarse verification. Review whether resizing loses input, selection or focus,
and whether toolbar wrapping/scrolling, fields and dialogs keep primary commands accessible.

Fine-pointer general controls use 30/36/42/50/60px, compact 28px and chrome 32px.
Coarse-pointer minimum is 44px; text inputs use at least 16px text.
Small glyphs and large targets are [separate roles](spacing-icon-contract.md).

## 6. Completion criteria and review

Using Carbon's [completion checklist](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/getting-started/contributing/component-checklist) as a reference,
record completion only for the supported scope with all relevant evidence below.

- Token roles, values, units, aliases and themes correspond to actual Core consumption.
- Documented API, defaults, states and anatomy match current source and running examples.
- Review the same Core in Light/Dark, long content, locales, parent widths and supported states in the browser.
- Review names, relationships, keyboard, focus and recovery through actual interaction; separate automatic and assistive technology results.
- Implement changes in token/Core owners and check consumers, accepted/rejected types and relevant regressions.
- Document page-fixture data, authorization, service and shell boundaries; retain actual-route checks where required.
- Evidence identifies source/build, story ID, args, viewport, pointer, theme, locale, observations and unresolved scope.

Review tables use `item / status / evidence / unresolved / next owner`.
Statuses are `not written`, `in review`, `adopted` and `deferred`.
Judge tokens, types, behavior, visuals, accessibility and consumers separately.
Automatic counts and documentation/preview presence do not establish complete design approval.

documents.title: Design system changes
documents.markdown:
# Design system changes

## 2026-11-03 — shared loading surfaces and command pending (unreleased)

Site `PageLoader` displays localized default text for omitted, empty or whitespace messages and retains
explicit phase text. Core `PageLoaderView.message` is now required and rejects blank strings; `imageAlt`
continues to name the image/status separately. Missing or failed images leave visible text. Configured
image selection, CDN resolution and GIF/SVG delivery remain site-owned. Catalogue bootstrap supplies
the same visible text directly to Core using its root-resolved image before ManifestProvider exists.

Core and site loaders add closed `contrast="standard" | "inverse"`, defaulting to standard theme
text. The standalone public form and embedded form block select inverse on their submission scrims
through their shared submission state; callers that omit contrast retain standard. Core uses existing
full-strength `text-on-image` on the scrim:
5.01:1 over the Light form overlay, where 88% inverse text would reach only 4.31:1. The form keeps
its overlay layout, interaction and admitted fields. No feature color override or new token is added.

`placement="flow"` adds a normal-flow region; existing `fill` remains the default positioned-parent
contract. Page blocks, editor preparation, initial lists, previews and modal/drawer bodies consume the
shared surface through their owning controllers. Consumers must retain loaded content during background
and incremental requests. Buttons, fields, upload/processing progress, playback buffering and route
progress keep their granular feedback.

Core [MediaVideoFrame](../../components/core/MediaControls/MediaVideoFrame.tsx) adds optional
`preparing` (default `false`). Core reserves initial 16:9 space while preparing or processing only
when no `video` or `.video-js` descendant is present to supply sizing; standard loaded-media sizing
remains runtime-owned. [VideoPlayerView](../../features/media/ui/VideoPlayerView.tsx) forwards `preparing`,
sets mount `aria-busy` from it and gives processing priority over preparation loading. The
[controller](../../features/media/VideoPlayer.tsx) supplies an inverse common loader over Core's
fixed black frame until runtime or native fallback mounting completes. Playback buffering and
processing retain their existing feedback.

TextButton adds command-only `loading`/`loadingLabel`. TableRowMenu tracks returned action Promises
and accepts `onError` for domain feedback. EditorHeader Back, ErrorPage command actions and
ImageUploadField removal track their returned Promises; MenuToggle forwards controlled `loading`.
SearchCombobox suppresses minimum-query/no-results copy while loading. MultiSelect adds optional
`isLoading`/`loadingLabel` using the shared checking glyph and suppresses pending empty copy.
MultiSelectComboboxView gates creation and suppresses empty results while querying or creating;
existing selections/options remain available. The post taxonomy wrapper supplies localized loading copy.
The shared pending-action helper preserves Promise values and original rejections while clearing
pending; domain feedback remains caller-owned.

Core adds `useOnDemandModuleState(module, needed, request?)` with `module`, `status`, `error` and
`retry`; `useOnDemandModule` keeps its module-only return. ConfirmDialogHost now requires localized
`loadError: { message, retryLabel }` for both default on-demand and eager loading. Exhausted renderer
retries end progress and show shared cancel/retry recovery while preserving queued intent and focus
restoration. A chunk failure never invokes confirmation.

ServerDataTableContent now retains loaded rows by default: `showPendingLoader` defaults to
`result.data.length === 0`, so initial empty navigation can still show PageLoader. Login and email
verification submission retain the disabled PIN and supply the common loader; explicit authority
rechecks retain their result region/focus. Actual PageContentView/EmbedFrame/ToolModule stories cover
mount pending, failed and ready, including a 320px region and the site loader. Their external module
fixtures do not exercise stalled downloads or real tool service requests. See the
[loading contract](loading-surface-contract.md) and [migration with consumer links](migrations/loading-commonization.md).

All 54 feature domains received source audit, alongside platform and support owners. Static candidates
are review evidence, not defect counts or complete semantic proof. The coordinator reports direct
visual inspection of the Works GIF and live PortaDJ ready state, plus Storybook common-loader GIF
phase/generic, no-image/failed-image, tool pending/failed/ready/320px and avatar `33steps`/hover states.
Most other production/Storybook states, physical coarse-pointer input and actual assistive-technology
checks remain unverified. No released web version or blanket visual approval is recorded.

## 2026-11-03 — smaller avatar removal visual (unreleased)

Core IconButton adds `appearance="media-overlay"` for inside media-corner commands: a 16px circle and 12px
glyph/spinner within a rectangular 24px fine-pointer / 44px coarse-pointer target. It rejects local size/shape, links,
toggles, count and contrast overrides. Existing icon-size, control-height and interaction roles own the geometry.
ImageUploadField exposes `removeButtonAppearance="avatar"`, requiring a circle preview and inside placement.
ProfileAvatarControl opts in for UserAvatarUploader's 56px admin and 80px default profile images.
The previous 24px filled removal circle shrinks visually while its target, keyboard focus, disabled and pending
behavior remain available. The rectangular hit area includes the painted badge edges; separate hover and active
selectors also preserve the small visual in Storybook's forced pseudo previews.
Other image actions and global control sizes retain their existing treatment.
See [image upload contract and migration](image-upload-contract.md). The coordinator reports inspecting
the `33steps` avatar and its hover state in Storybook; physical coarse-pointer input and actual
assistive-technology checks remain unverified. This observation does not approve every avatar state.

## 2026-10-28 — site logos sized by the uploaded file; search dialog copy (unreleased)

The public header, expanded admin navigation and form pages draw the full site logo at the size its SVG
declares (`SITE_LOGO_HEIGHT` `{ min }`) instead of fixed 28/36/24px heights; those heights remain the minimum
for files that declare a smaller size or none. Core `SiteHeader` exposes `--_site-header-brand-max-height`
(header height less `--geul-spacing-xxs` on each side) and `SiteLogoView` caps sized logos at it, or at
`--geul-chrome-header-height-sm` outside the header. `SiteLogoView` `height` also accepts `{ min }`; `'intrinsic'`
uses the `size` icon height as its minimum. The print watermark uses the symbol.
See [Site branding](site-branding.md); review `Pages/Application/Frames/StackedBrand*` in light/dark and on phones.

The post search dialog no longer repeats "Search posts…" as its title, field hint and empty state. The title
is the header's search action name, the field keeps the hint, and the empty state asks for two characters.
The `Frames` stories open the same Core `CommandPalette` with the same copy roles instead of a text-field modal.

## 2026-10-27 — video start control (unreleased)

The Core Video.js adapter includes the SDK's standalone big play button, which lacks the regular `vjs-button` class.
It uses the existing inverse, low-emphasis `lg` icon control with shared hover and keyboard focus states.
Centering follows the rendered hit area and preserves the shared minimum target on touch devices.
The SDK's oversized filled border is removed for video blocks, file previews and other `VideoPlayer` consumers.
Review `Feature/Media/Video Player/SmallPreview` at the 288px media width alongside the normal playback story.

## 2026-10-27 — embedded map width and startup recovery (unreleased)

`MapViewEmbedded` now applies display size to the parent width independently of its height cap.
A 100% map fills the content column even on wide screens; smaller authored widths and mobile stretching remain supported.
The shared `MapLibreMap` controller shows the map on its first load without waiting for an idle camera.
Constructor failures and startup exceeding 20 seconds reach the existing route error boundary and shared application error page.
Theme lookup failures preserve their original status for the same boundary. Recoverable tile errors retain the map.
Consumers include the public work/post maps and authored map blocks. Review `Feature/Map/Embedded/FullWidth`
and `Feature/Application Error/ErrorPage/GeneralError` in Storybook; the embedded fixture uses real browser graphics support.

## 2026-10-21 — phone navigation fills the screen below the header (unreleased)

Core `ApplicationFrame kind="site"` replaces the phone navigation drawer with a full-screen panel below
the header. The drawer covered nearly the whole width yet left a sliver of the page, and repeated the
logo at its top left while the header showed it in the center. The header now stays in place: the
brand keeps its position and the menu toggle turns into the close control. The panel is a disclosure
region (`nav`), not a modal: the page behind is inert and does not scroll, Escape closes it and
returns focus to the toggle, and it covers the consent banner while open. `navigationTitle` and the
site frame's `closeLabel` are removed. See [Site branding](site-branding.md).

## 2026-10-19 — outline rail at every width (unreleased)

Core `TableOfContentsView` uses the quiet rail at every width. The persistent outline column from `lg` is
removed: a long outline gave it a second scroll area beside the document. Wide documents now reserve only
the rail width at the inline end instead of 15rem plus the `xl` gap, and the document box gains that space. The `outlinePresentation` prop is removed from Core and from the navigation Feature; no
consumer passed it. The rail also keeps a preview started as the outline appears, ends a hover preview when
the pointer leaves the outline from the list, and keeps a previewed row whole at the list's edges. See
[Table of contents](table-of-contents.md).

## 2026-10-18 — self-hosted Geul fonts (unreleased)

The shared sans/mono assignments now use the Noto-backed Geul families. Korean Hanja and
Traditional Chinese use Han TC; Japanese uses Han JP and Simplified Chinese uses Han SC.
The app resolves a generated hashed stylesheet from `PUBLIC_FONT_BASE_URL` (default
`https://static.rawsector.com/fonts`) instead of constructing a Google Fonts proxy query.
Storybook consumes the same complete local output when present and falls back to the static
host without requiring font artifacts in CI. Its former Regular/Bold TTF declarations are removed;
Geul provides normal 400/500/600. Existing Core/theme font variables remain the consumer API.

Upload the matching artifacts before switching production. See [font migration and deployment](../fonts.md).
Browser rendering remains unverified because the computer-use tool denied Chrome access.

## 2026-10-18 — Braun palette, hairline geometry and quiet weights (unreleased)

Neutral and graphite move to Braun light grey (background #efeeea, surface #f8f7f4, text #1b1b19) and a
green-free anthracite (#141413, text #eceae5); secondary and muted ink step away from primary so labels
recede. A new `signal` family replaces blue as `action-accent`, `status-accent` and the lead chart
series (#9c3d18 light, #f28c52 dark); Ocean presets keep their blue accent. Every role pair still meets
the theme contrast gates.

Control heights move to 24/28/32/40/48px (compact 24, chrome 28; coarse pointers keep 44px). Line icons
draw `icon-stroke` 1.5 instead of Tabler's 2. `font-weight-medium` resolves to 400 and `strong` to 500,
so labels and selection read by ink and position. Field labels take secondary ink. Chrome commands
(header, language and mobile navigation) no longer fill on hover or selection: secondary ink at rest,
a 1px underline under the current item. The table-of-contents marker is 1px. Inline links (prose and
`NavigationLink`) take `action-accent` whether visited or not; an authored text colour still wins.
Chart guides run across the value axis only, categorical bars are at most 12px wide, histogram bins
touch, and area fills are the accent at 12%.

## 2026-10-18 — small, even type scale (unreleased)

The text scale moves to 10/11/12/13/14px (`xs`–`xl`, was 12/14/16/18/20px), one pixel per step: running
text, the editor body and interface text are 12px, metadata, supporting text and chrome 11px, captions,
badges and field help 10px. Chrome roles now alias `font-size-sm` instead of `font-size-xs`. Document leading moves to
1.6 (was 1.7). Headings follow: title 20/24px (was 32/40px), body h1–h3 16/15/14px below `sm` and
18/16/14px from `sm` (was 28/24/20 and 34/26/22px), and every heading, in Core and in published and
editor documents, uses the new `heading-weight` role (500) instead of `font-weight-strong` (600). Paper
moves to 9pt running text with 15/12/11/10pt headings (was 10.5pt and 22/18/15.5/13.5pt). The reading measure narrows from 44rem to 32rem so lines
stay near 85 Latin or 55 Hangul characters.

New `icon-size` roles carry the previous 12–20px geometry: social icons and the site logo image no longer
follow the text scale. Coarse-pointer text inputs keep 16px through the new `interaction-text-minimum`
role instead of `font-size-md`. Work client logos are sized from a smaller optical area to sit with 11px
metadata.

## 2026-10-18 — document visibility options and entity bodies (unreleased)

Page and Post authors can hide their table of contents through the shared layout field. Existing
layouts retain the outline by default. Page language controls stay at the frame’s inline end.
Post's Allow comments checkbox becomes the existing Core Switch; disabled comments no longer mount
the thread or issue read requests. Pages gain no comment setting.

`EntityDetailLayout` becomes overview → body → related collections, with a `listing` slot that completes
the overview beside the media; releases put their numbered tracklist there. Work, Event, Artist, Label and
Release move authored descriptions/biographies into `body`, remove the synthetic section heading and render
authored H1 as h2 under the entity title; the content language control stays at the title row's end.
Migrate running content from `children` into `body`; `children` always follow the body across the page
width, including on Series and Event series details.

Credits and clients become metadata rows on Work, Event and Release. `PublicCreditList` replaces
`CreditList` and `ReleaseCreditsList`: roles align as nested labels, shared roles share a row, avatars
and "Unknown" placeholders are gone. `PublicNameList` gives artists, labels and clients one slash grammar.
Work client logos stay, sized by area and greyscale until their link is engaged. Label artists use an
extra-small roster grid. Event dates read as one range phrase, Work's
updated date drops its time, long addresses show their host, Tech values use slashes, location rows omit
coordinates and a label's catalog number is not repeated when it equals the release's.

## 2026-10-18 — start-edge documents and one media scale per item size (unreleased)

Posts, legal documents and the changelog start at the start edge like entity details and pages: title, hero
text and running text share that edge and the outline sits at the inline end. Core `TableOfContentsView`
loses `contentPlacement` (the `center` placement and `--_table-of-contents-inset-start` are removed); Core
`LayoutContainer` gains `placement="start"`. The persistent outline column's rows move from `sm` to `xs`.
Core Collection has five item sizes (XS–XL, contracts 0.11.0 appends `xs`/`xl`) and Core `LayoutGrid` five
minimum column widths (7/10/14/20/28rem, a √2 scale). A collection thumbnail takes the minimum grid card width of its size (at
most 40% of a narrow row), so list and grid blocks of one size show images at the same scale and a 16:9 thumbnail
is no longer shorter than its title and metadata. New semantic token `text-hover` is the one hover ink of quiet
navigation (NavigationLink secondary/muted tones, Tabs, SideNavigation, outline rows). Outline column rows rest in `text-muted` and show `text-hover` on `surface-hover`
with a `border-strong` rule segment under a pointer; the current row also takes medium weight. Root `word-break:
keep-all` now applies in every interface language (Japanese and Chinese opt out), so Korean titles on English pages
no longer break inside words. Collection grids keep exact track widths from `md` (`LayoutGrid columnGrowth`), and
phone list thumbnails are square.

## 2026-10-17 — authoring settings column (unreleased)

`DocumentEditorPanels` puts the settings in a sticky, independently scrolling column beside the body from
`lg` (tabs below `lg`; the body bleeds to the edge on phones only). Event, Release and Series adopt it with
Post, Page and Work. New Feature `EditorSettingsSection` is the settings card; all editors order their cards
URL → details → classification/related → credits → options → summary → images → metadata → sharing →
translations. Release's bordered "Basic Information" box, Event's bordered "Body" box and untitled relation
card, and Work's loose location/image grid become standard cards; Work's type-specific group labels move
from `xs` to `sm` so they no longer read smaller than the fields they group.

## 2026-10-17 — public details, fluid collections and continued lists (unreleased)

New Feature `EntityDetailLayout` / `EntityDetailSection` / `EntityDetailImage` (document-layout) give every
public entity detail one full-width composition: media in the start third from `md` (sticky), title, metadata
and h2 sections beside it, stacked below `md`. Event, Work, Release, Artist, Label, Series and Event series
adopt it; their ad hoc `role="heading"` labels, Work's `WorkPublicHeaderLayout` and Release's fixed 280px
artwork column are removed. Work keeps its paper overlay header through `printMedia="overlay"`. `CreditList`
no longer prints its own title.

Core `LayoutGrid` adds `minColumnWidth` (`sm`/`md`/`lg`, responsive): a fluid grid of equal columns at least
that wide. Page collection blocks size columns from the item size instead of the authored count, which now
applies to carousels only (the editor shows "Slides to show" for carousels and no column control otherwise).
Stacked page sections now share the `xl` rhythm on screen as on paper, so a heading block no longer sits
flush against the collection before it; adjacent sections with a background colour stay joined.
Core `TableOfContentsView` adds `outlinePresentation="rail"` for documents sharing the page width. Core
`Pagination` and server table pagination render nothing for a single page. Collection blocks with pagination
on continue in place (`InfiniteItems`, Load more / retry) instead of page links.

## 2026-10-17 — admin page outline (unreleased)

Every admin page now has exactly one h1 at the page title scale, followed by h2 sections. Mail adapters,
Menus, Translation overview/jobs/settings and the dashboard move from hand-built `Heading level={2}` rows to
Core `PageHeader`; settings-style sections use `SettingsSection` without cards, and cards remain only for
repeated objects (mail adapters, translation providers). User edit renders Profile, SSO providers, primary
email, ban state and the personal access token as h2 sections; the profile Save sits at the end of the
Profile section, whose description states that the following sections apply immediately.

Core `TextInput textRole="title"` drops its inline padding and uses the page title scale at `size="xl"`,
so editable editor titles (post, page, email, map theme) match read-only titles. Core `SelectionPath`
adds `pageTitle`, rendering the current location as the h1; the admin file manager uses it instead of a
label-sized "Files". `LogoCropper` (client and label logos) no longer repeats its visible label inside the
empty dropzone, previews each variant on its theme surface, and the light/dark pair sits side by side
from `sm`.

## 2026-10-17 — settings hierarchy, logo slots and upload previews (unreleased)

Core `SectionHeader` adds `level={2 | 3}`: real headings on one scale (page title → section → group →
field label). Without a level it keeps the compact card/row label. New Core `SettingsSection` (level 2,
`lg` rhythm) and `SettingsGroup` (level 3, `md` rhythm) compose settings pages; admin Site settings and
OG image settings adopt them with Core `PageHeader`. Section-level fields precede groups.

Core `ImagePreviewFrame` adds `surface="theme-light" | "theme-dark"`, backed by the new invariant tokens
`theme-light-background` and `theme-dark-background`, so theme-specific artwork previews on its own
background in either app theme. `ImageUploadField` hug previews size the remove action's box to the
image, and the outside remove action is a corner badge: `IconButton placement="overlay-end"` centres an
opaque chip on the media's top-end corner, and `ImageUploadField` reserves half the control as a gutter
so the badge never covers adjacent text.

Site logos become full/symbol/email slots with light and dark variants (see `site-branding.md`). The OG
background moves from Site settings to OG image settings.

## 2026-10-17 — site header and brand placement (unreleased)

Core `ApplicationFrame` exports `SiteHeader`, a closed slot composition that centers branding whenever
the responsive menu toggle is visible. Public `ShellLayout` adopts it. Phone header groups are
balanced: menu + theme at the start, search + account at the end, so the centered logo keeps even
space down to 280px. The language menu moves from the phone header to the navigation drawer's last row
(`ShellViewSlots.languageMobile` is replaced by `languageNavigation`; `LanguageMenu` adds
`variant="navigation"`).
Core `ApplicationFrame.navigationTitle` optionally supplies a branded drawer heading; the public
shell uses the same logo there, while the text heading remains the fallback.

The existing Core chrome/spacing tokens and control variants are unchanged. `SiteLogoView` preserves
image flex size; public and admin consumers use explicit authored dimensions. Admin navigation keeps
its branding header outside the scrollable list's shrinking space.

Core `Disclosure` adds `density="chrome"`: compact geometry with the label on the chrome rows' `xs` line,
so navigation groups start where chrome links start. Core `SideNavigation` expanded groups now render this
Disclosure (sentence-case label, trailing turning chevron, no rules between expanded groups) instead of the
uppercase section header; items, the active boundary and the compact rail are unchanged. The public mobile
drawer groups move from `compact` to `chrome`, fixing a 4px label offset against sibling links. Admin
navigation branding and subtitle start on the same `xs` line as the navigation labels.

Console-clean Core contracts: `Field` names its child through aria-labelledby as well as `<label for>`;
`Tooltip` keeps React Aria's open state controlled for the trigger's lifetime (suppression no longer flips it
between controlled and uncontrolled); `SegmentedProgress` segments are labelled `img` tooltip targets; new
`DropdownMenu.Anchor` replaces hidden `DropdownMenu.Target` divs for context menus (file manager, editor file
picker). Feature fixes: unlabeled inputs gain aria-labels (form password, email test recipient, AI prompt),
non-control tooltip targets carry roles (participant role badge, track audio status).

Usage, migration and verification scope: [site branding](site-branding.md).

documents.title: Choice input contract review
documents.markdown:
# Choice input contract review

Reviewed: 2026-10-12. Code/jsdom scope: Checkbox, Radio, Switch and SegmentedControl. Browser visual review and actual assistive-technology approval are excluded. Installed React Aria Components: 1.22.1.

## Specification and current support

| Core             | Purpose / value                                              | Naming / errors / required                                                                                     | readOnly / disabled                                                                       |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Checkbox         | Independent boolean and indeterminate; Group uses string[]   | Individual label/ARIA name; individual/group description/error relations; separate Group name                  | Individual and inherited Group state. readOnly retains focus; disabled is native disabled |
| Radio            | Single string selection in Group; initially unselected       | Individual label/ARIA name; Group name/description/error. radiogroup carries invalid/required                  | readOnly belongs to Group; individual Radio readOnly is not forwarded                     |
| Switch           | One on/off value, checked or defaultChecked                  | Stable label/ARIA name; input description/error and invalid/required relations                                 | readOnly blocks changes; disabled is native disabled                                      |
| SegmentedControl | RadioGroup-based single string; defaults to first data value | Group name via string label/aria-label; icon options use accessibleLabel. required/error/description relations | Group readOnly/disabled and option disabled                                               |

Distinguish Checkbox multiple choices, Radio mutually exclusive choices and Switch settings that apply immediately.
Carbon purpose/group-state/documentation conventions informed the review; Carbon dimensions were not copied.
[Checkbox guidelines](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/checkbox/guidelines),
[Radio guidelines](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/radio-button/guidelines),
[Toggle guidelines](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/toggle/guidelines).

Checkbox uses Tab to reach each choice and Space to change it. Radio/SegmentedControl arrows change selection, skip disabled options and wrap. jsdom covered horizontal RTL and vertical Down.
Radio readOnly blocks arrow/click value changes while preserving selected-input focus.
Actual Checkbox/Switch Space defaults, Tab/Shift+Tab order and radios inside toolbars still need browser review.
[Checkbox APG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/checkbox/),
[Radio APG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/),
[Switch APG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/switch/).

## Correction and checks

Switch onLabel/offLabel read only props.checked, displaying Off with defaultChecked=true. The reproduction was corrected to use RAC children render-state isSelected.
Tests covered uncontrolled initialization/click transitions and controlled owner updates. Track copy is aria-hidden; the accessible name stays stable. External product copy, CSS and tokens were unchanged.

Six regression files passed 38 tests:
[ChoiceContracts.test.tsx](../../components/core/Input/ChoiceContracts.test.tsx),
[Switch.test.tsx](../../components/core/Input/Switch.test.tsx),
[SegmentedControl.test.tsx](../../components/core/Input/SegmentedControl.test.tsx),
[InputBehavior.test.tsx](../../components/core/Input/InputBehavior.test.tsx),
[InputWrappers.test.tsx](../../components/core/Input/InputWrappers.test.tsx),
[IconViewModeControl.test.tsx](../../features/admin/IconViewModeControl.test.tsx).
[Choice.type-test.tsx](../../components/core/Input/Choice.type-test.tsx) verifies allowed API and rejected visual escapes.
Storybook added Switch StateLabels, Radio ReadOnly and SegmentedControl ReadOnly.

## Consumers and remaining scope

[Form SelectField](../../features/form/FormField/fields/SelectField.tsx) consumes Radio.Group required/error/description/focus.
[SwitchField](../../features/form/FormField/fields/SwitchField.tsx) consumes Field naming and external error IDs.
[FieldEditor](../../features/form/FormBuilder/FieldEditor.tsx) uses Checkbox.Group for default-choice editing.
SegmentedControl supplies icon accessibleLabel in [IconViewModeControl](../../features/admin/IconViewModeControl.tsx) and layout values in [ContentLayoutFieldView](../../features/document-layout/ui/ContentLayoutFieldView.tsx).

SegmentedControl required/error/description support was corrected afterward. inputState manages required/invalid. When actual description/string error exists, the existing root separates the selection area and InputHelp. Border/orientation/fullWidth remain on the internal segments.
Without messages, or with a boolean error from Field, the original selection-area structure remains.
Field's external description/error IDs reach both group and actual radios; parent Field copy is not repeated.
Field's HTML label for alone cannot name or focus a radiogroup; this composition requires child aria-label or aria-labelledby. Changing Field label activation was outside scope.

ContentLayoutFieldView's three groups use existing visible labels.contentHeight/pageChrome/footer.
IconViewModeControl uses the existing common.actions.view label, View in English and its Korean translation. No visible copy was added.
[Naming tests](../../features/document-layout/ContentLayoutFieldView.naming.test.tsx) and IconViewModeControl tests check actual en/ko translations, existing selection callbacks and unchanged visible copy.
[SegmentedControlField.test.tsx](../../components/core/Input/SegmentedControlField.test.tsx) covers standalone help/errors, external IDs, Field required/error, no duplicate copy, state clearing, boolean errors and help with disabled/readOnly.
CSS, tokens and the preceding four Input components were unchanged.
The final run passed 7 files / 40 tests, including six new Core regressions and four en/ko consumer-name regressions. It combined SegmentedControlField/SegmentedControl/ChoiceContracts/Field with IconViewModeControl/ContentLayoutFieldView.naming/ContentLayoutField.
Scoped TypeScript, ESLint(max-warnings=0) and Prettier passed. Actual viewport/theme/AT review of help-bearing layouts remains.

The following props are open in types but not forwarded or displayed. A follow-up must choose implementation support or a narrower public contract.

| Core             | Unconsumed API                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Checkbox         | leftSection/rightSection; Group onClick/onKeyDown/onKeyUp (onLabel/offLabel removed)                                                                   |
| Radio            | Individual readOnly/required/error/description and onClick/onFocus/onBlur/onKeyDown/onKeyUp; Group onClick/onKeyDown/onKeyUp; leftSection/rightSection |
| Switch           | onClick, leftSection/rightSection (indeterminate removed)                                                                                              |
| SegmentedControl | onClick/onFocus/onBlur/onKeyDown/onKeyUp, leftSection/rightSection                                                                                     |

None of these four Core components has a pending API. Consumers own async saves; no arbitrary pending variant was added.
390/834/1440px, light/dark, long labels/help/errors, coarse pointers, actual Space/Tab and VoiceOver/Orca remain separate review items.

documents.title: Compact product interfaces
documents.markdown:
# Compact product interfaces

Compact presentation uses the existing Core typography, spacing, control sizes and semantic themes.
It changes visible hierarchy and layout together with the production consumers; it is not a Storybook-only scale.
No additional palette or token scale is introduced for these review corrections.

## Shared hierarchy

Use a short primary title, nearby secondary context and a separate action track.
Core Text sm/medium identifies a list item; xs/secondary carries language, version, contributor or time context.
Keep the primary content first in DOM reading order. Passive current/archive state is text, while actionable or
in-progress states retain their relevant control/status contracts. Do not put every metadata value in a filled badge.
Use an explicit compact control size for dense command rows, not a theme-dependent reduction of hit targets.
The existing Core coarse-pointer minimum and keyboard/focus behavior remain.

| Task                          | Shared owner and actual consumer                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Progress and processing       | Core Progress; ProcessingOverlay and RouteProgressBar consume its actual bar. Processing owns the protective media overlay; route owns fixed placement. Optional task/status text uses xs.                           |
| Modal and drawer              | Core OverlayDialog/Drawer compact density, a visible fixed header and a scrolling body. Standard density remains explicit. Map directions and version history consume this contract.                                 |
| Version history               | Primary title, xs context, passive semantic timestamp and an end-aligned restore command. The shared NearEndLoader requests further pages, retains loaded items on failure and provides retry/keyboard continuation. |
| Link creation                 | Named plus IconButton, compact inputs and a plain form track. Narrow social links give the URL track priority and retain a searchable platform picker in a Core Popover.                                             |
| Translation and legal history | Language names without duplicate codes; source identity and meaningful job/error information remain. Current/archive states use plain Text.                                                                          |
| Endpoint and identity         | MCP endpoint terms remain accessible but are visually hidden. Missing/failed site images fall back to site title or LOGO using named Typography sizes.                                                               |
| Image selection               | Supported source hints and recoverable validation; local preparation before managed crop/upload. Prepared server-bound files retain target validation.                                                               |
| Dense reordering              | Stable leading Core targets; motion shells update independently of expensive domain content. Keyboard/sensor/focus behavior remains.                                                                                 |
| Post hero                     | Contained photo geometry, metadata in normal flow and shared inset/gap to the real document body.                                                                                                                    |
| Cookie choice                 | The single optional category is disclosed with two equally available compact text decisions: Reject and Accept all. Account settings retain draft/save semantics.                                                    |

## Rules and boundaries

Accessible names retain control and target context when a visual label is hidden. Icon-only controls require names;
passive metadata must not acquire unrelated extra tab stops. Full timestamps remain accessible independently of hover.
A popup that exceeds a command rail belongs in the existing document portal, with trigger ownership, selection and
focus restoration preserved. Dropdowns scroll within the viewport rather than stretching the toolbar.

Automatic pagination is a transport-aware composition: the feature owns cursor/offset, cancellation, permissions
and error state; Core owns the near-end trigger and continuation affordance. A query replacement must discard stale
responses. Failed pages need an explicit retry, not an automatic request loop. Folder completeness and search paging
are distinct contracts; do not invent a cursor for a non-paginated endpoint.

The avatar removal fill is the user's scoped danger/strong exception. It does not change ordinary upload removal
or general row action defaults. Processing image contrast requires a real dark media/scrim surface.

Review current production stories at mobile, tablet and desktop sizes, both base schemes/custom presets and relevant
UI languages. Source render counts are not native drag latency or FPS; automated axe/keyboard execution is not
assistive-technology or live-service acceptance. The version-history storage audit identifies inspected source,
not the state of a deployed database.

## API and default migration

- Progress `title` is now a visible task title, not a native tooltip attribute; `status` is visible detail linked as the description. Existing explicit accessible names remain required. Use Core Tooltip or a described relationship for separate supplementary information.
- Progress xs uses a 2px bar instead of 4px. Route consumes this slim variant; ordinary progress remains sm. Existing xs consumers, including release track status, inherit the slim bar.
- ContentModal/OverlayDialog/Drawer default to compact density. Choose standard explicitly when its existing spacing is required. Width/placement and media/workspace fit rules are independent of density.
- ProcessingOverlay accepts the shared Progress contract in its progress slot. Route owns only phase/fixed placement, and callers migrate the old estimated numeric presentation to its phase contract.
- NearEndLoader callers provide an opaque next-page key, result-set reset key and an async load operation. Feature adapters preserve pending/error state and protect against stale queries.
- ImageUploadField `removeButtonEmphasis` adds only medium/strong; medium remains the default. Avatar is the explicit strong consumer.
- The cookie banner migrates draft/save callbacks to direct acceptance/rejection. Account settings retains draft/save behavior; consent storage/version is unchanged.

## Detailed contracts

- [Overlay density](./overlay-density-contract.md)
- [Link management](./link-management-pattern.md)
- [Version history](./version-history.md)
- [File browser](./file-browser.md)
- [Translation, identity and history](./translation-identity-history-contract.md)
- [Image upload](./image-upload-contract.md)
- [Sortable rendering](./sortable-performance.md)
- [Post hero](./post-hero-contract.md)
- [Cookie consent](./cookie-consent-contract.md)

documents.title: Component documentation contract
documents.markdown:
# Component documentation contract

Each Storybook `Core/<category>/<component>` document covers the actual component's purpose, anatomy, public API, states, accessibility and consumers. Search `Design System/Components` to open Core documentation and state examples.

Tokens, themes and Core own the adopted rules. Documentation examples and dimensions from external systems do not change these contracts automatically.

## Documentation content

Place a representative live example after the summary. Choose the CSF `Default` export when present; otherwise identify the actual first example. Expand the example to run the same Core component and Controls. Open other states through individual Canvas links.

An opened example stays open when the header language or theme changes. Explicit closing and
each component document's expansion state are independent. This state belongs to the review
session and does not change saved application preferences.

Controls change args exposed by the actual story. Connect static enum/boolean types and explicit defaults while preserving fixture options and `control: false`. Do not guess choices from unresolved aliases or conditional types. The code panel shows the example's original CSF; application usage examples belong in [Getting started](./getting-started.md).

| Section                | Editorial or extraction requirement                                                                                           |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Purpose and selection  | Task served and distinction from similar components                                                                           |
| Anatomy                | Root, label, slots, control order and responsibility of each layer                                                            |
| Public API             | Source props, permitted types, required status and explicit defaults                                                          |
| State examples         | Story IDs and display names actually exported by current CSF                                                                  |
| Usage guidance         | Semantic contracts, composition, data, content, placement and asynchronous work                                               |
| Accessibility          | Names, roles, values, states, relationships, keyboard, focus and error recovery                                               |
| Constraints            | Unsupported overrides, union combinations, unresolved inherited types and verification limits                                 |
| Consumers              | Core, Feature and App files identified through actual imports and barrel exports                                              |
| Related specifications | Repository-owned contracts and API reviews                                                                                    |
| Token references       | Static variables in owned TS files and direct/local CSS imports, with reference locations, central definitions and conditions |

[Usage Rules](./getting-started.md#documentation-structure) compares correct and incorrect compositions using actual Core components. Follow the [contribution process](./contribution.md) and update the affected regression tests.

The adopted documentation model follows Storybook's [documentation guide](https://storybook.js.org/blog/how-to-document-your-design-system-best-practices-tools/), [structure guide](https://storybook.js.org/blog/structuring-your-storybook/) and [Docs approaches](https://storybook.js.org/blog/4-ways-to-document-your-design-system-with-storybook/): usage guidance, live examples and API references stay connected to implementation.

Document the following family-specific contracts:

- Button, IconButton and TextButton: action/link branches, names and state semantics.
- Inputs: value, label, description, error, required, disabled and readOnly. Field: child associations and semantic relationships.
- Choices: boolean, single-selection and multiple-selection models, with group names.
- Tabs, menus and dialogs: actual keyboard models, focus entry and return.
- Tables: actual data, column headers, sorting, selection, row actions, pagination and two-dimensional content at narrow widths.

## Reading the public API table

`required=true` means **required in every union branch**. A `false` value does not always mean optional. IconButton's `label`, `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` are not individually required across all branches, but one naming branch is mandatory. A link's `href` is required in that branch. Read the complete Button/TextButton/IconButton types for valid action/link and drag-handle geometry combinations.

`never` identifies an unsupported property. Documentation must not reopen a closed styling API.

Explicit defaults come only from initializers in implementation parameters using the exact props contract. Story args and arbitrary internal fallbacks are not defaults. Guidance separately describes values affected by parent action-row, toolbar, density or contrast context. A blank default does not guarantee `undefined`.

External React/React Aria inherited types and unsupported mapped/conditional types remain listed as limitations. Do not assume that unlisted inherited properties are permitted: the public type and runtime projection define the boundary. Preserve original generic names such as `Row` and `T` rather than replacing consumer-supplied types with strings. Composed fixture props are not product Core APIs.

## Source ownership and updates

- Generator: `scripts/design-system/storybook-component-docs.mjs`
- Editorial purpose, anatomy and guidance: `stories/design-system/components/component-guidance.mjs`
- Generated registry: `stories/design-system/components/component-docs.generated.json`
- Catalog: `stories/design-system/components/Components.stories.tsx`
- API and behavior authority: `components/core/**`

Generation reads TypeScript ASTs, local imports/barrel exports and current CSF metadata without executing Core or stories. It fails for missing/stale guidance, missing/duplicate/stale registry groups, state IDs inconsistent with current exports and missing source/document references.

`tokenReferences` preserves reference locations, central CSS definitions and theme/media conditions. `styleSources` records the CSS files read and their importers. `computedTokenReferences` and `tokenReferenceLimitations` record computed names and unresolved scope. The extractor does not infer ordinary TS-import, nested-component or complete barrel style graphs, or runtime activation. An empty list means no static reference was found within this scope; it does not establish that the component is token-free.

```sh
node scripts/design-system/storybook-component-docs.mjs
node scripts/design-system/storybook-component-docs.mjs --check
node --test scripts/design-system/storybook-component-docs.test.mjs
```

Regenerate when Core APIs, defaults, states or consumers change. Update editorial guidance when usage, anatomy or accessibility meaning changes. `--check` rejects hand-edited generated output.

## Review sequence

1. Check purpose and actual consumers; compare the selection criteria with similar Core components.
2. Check API, anatomy, tokens/themes, unsupported overrides and valid state combinations.
3. Open state stories individually and exercise interactions, asynchronous work, errors, recovery, keyboard and focus.
4. Review consumers on mobile, tablet and desktop, in light/dark and custom themes, supported locales and long/empty content.
5. Record the scope and outstanding work for automated checks, keyboard tests and actual assistive-technology verification separately.

A story's existence does not establish that its state passed review. Successful generation demonstrates source/document connections; it does not establish product-page, VoiceOver, Orca or usability verification.

documents.title: Shared action and confirmation contract
documents.markdown:
# Shared action and confirmation contract

Ordinary actions default to neutral/medium. Dialog primary actions and all confirmation intents
use strong fill through the shared Core contract, as explicitly requested by the user. Core owns all color, geometry and states;
`features/confirmation` owns the product choice of confirmation intent.

## Expression

`tone` selects neutral, accent, positive, warning or danger. `emphasis` independently selects
transparent medium/low, a functional outline, or strong fill. Explicit semantic controls use the
existing status ink and new action fill/hover/pressed roles in both themes. Strong uses `text-on-action`;
normal, hover and pressed contrast are checked. Filled buttons have no border or inset pressed
outline; pressing changes their background. The outside keyboard focus ring remains available. Disabled controls override semantic ink, focus remains visible,
and pending confirmation locks dismissal and duplicate submission. Menus use semantic ink without
becoming filled commit buttons. Content/image overlay contrast keeps its existing Core contract.

| Feature intent            | Core treatment    | Typical command                                   |
| ------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| delete / discard / revoke | danger / strong   | Delete a record, discard changes, revoke a grant  |
| archive                   | warning / strong  | Archive Member criteria                           |
| restore                   | positive / strong | Restore a segment or document version             |
| regenerate                | warning / strong  | Replace a token, invalidating its previous secret |
| confirm                   | neutral / strong  | Change source locale or unsubscribe               |

`ConfirmationDialog` requires intent. It forwards the domain-owned command, message/impact summary,
pending state and disabled state to Core ConfirmModal. It does not infer risk from a label or
automatically execute commands. `confirmationDialogs.open` offers the same intent contract for
imperative use, backed by the existing Core host. Callers must return the real Promise; use
`mutateAsync` rather than a fire-and-forget `mutate` when the host owns pending/dismissal.

## Consumers

- Delete footers use the shared Feature: CommentItem,
  AdminFormSubmissionsPage, WorksPageView, PlaceEditor, LegalPolicyListClient and LegalPolicyEditor.
- Existing confirmations in administrator entity modals, map themes/places, email layouts/templates,
  mail adapters, event types, menus, release tracks, translation providers, user profiles, OAuth
  grants and personal access tokens select explicit intent.
- Artist/label impact previews and FileManager in-use blocking retain their domain details and
  revision/authorization checks while using the same confirmation surface.
- Both DataTable bulk deletion adapters share `useBulkDeletion`. It guards duplicate submission,
  waits for every item and preserves successful IDs when other items return domain errors or reject.
  Table selection, success notifications and refresh/invalidation remain caller-owned.
- The authoring EditorHeader composes the same Feature through a Core render slot. Post, page,
  form, work, release, event and event-series editors share that route. Core has no Feature import.
- Translation deletion and source-locale changes use the intent-aware imperative adapter and await
  their actual mutations. Version restoration and segment archive/restore keep separate intents.

## Domain flows retained

Account deletion sends an email and then displays a requested state, with recovery and anonymization
information. It retains its account-owned multi-step dialog. Deleting an attached reference, editing
a document block, removing a passkey, revoking a session and deleting a share link retain their
existing inline command flows; semantic tone is rendered consistently by Core. They are not
converted into record deletion or given an extra modal solely because their label says remove.

`Feature/Confirmation/Dialog` previews every intent, pending, blocked and an interactive localized
confirmation. Core's Button SemanticMatrix remains the source for every tone/emphasis combination.

documents.title: Changing and contributing to Geul design system
documents.markdown:
# Changing and contributing to Geul design system

Start with an actual usage problem.
Review tokens, Core implementation, consumers and documentation in the same change, and record both results and unresolved items.

## Propose a change

Include the source, story, user task and conditions that reproduce the problem.
Record viewport, theme, locale, actual behavior and expected behavior.
First check whether existing Core APIs, states or compositions can express the requirement.
Explain why the existing parts are insufficient and which consumers are affected.
Propose a new Core component when it owns a reusable responsibility across domains.
Features own domain data, authorization, services and product-specific flows.
Reuse count alone does not decide adoption.

## Acceptance criteria

| Decision                     | Required evidence                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Change existing Core         | A defect in its contract or a shared state/API required by actual consumers                                                   |
| Add Core                     | A distinct responsibility, public API, naming, interaction, states and token ownership                                        |
| Add a Composition or Pattern | A working arrangement of existing Core that solves a repeated task                                                            |
| Retain a Feature             | Domain data, authorization, services or a product-specific flow                                                               |
| Revise or defer a proposal   | Duplicated components, consumer-specific color/padding overrides, arbitrary state APIs or missing reproduction/usage evidence |

Assign review roles according to the change.
The proposer prepares reproduction and consumer evidence. Token/Core reviewers check meaning, API, composition and accessibility.
Reviewers of affected product consumers check actual tasks, responsive behavior, errors and recovery.
Assign reviewer names in the repository review for that change.

## Implement and document

1. Change the adopted token, theme or Core owner.
2. Update representative examples, supported states, Playground and actual consumers.
3. Update purpose, anatomy, use/avoid guidance, labeling, accessibility, tokens and compatibility.
4. Run `pnpm design-system:generate` to refresh documentation data and indexes.
5. Run `pnpm design-system:check`, `pnpm storybook:typecheck` and checks appropriate to the change.
6. Record actual browser results with viewport, theme, locale and interaction conditions.

Generated API and token references come from source.
Do not describe computed types, variables or runtime effects as proven by static extraction.
Record visual review, automated accessibility, keyboard and VoiceOver/Orca results with their separate execution scopes.
Do not mark every component or page passed when only a subset was reviewed.

## Compact presentation and custom themes

Compact composition and custom themes use the shared theme and token contract.
The current named registry is documented in the [system guide](../design-system.md#named-themes-and-compact-composition).
Keep theme appearance and interaction density explicit: choosing a theme must not silently shrink targets,
change keyboard behavior or add a Feature-local presentation authority.
Reuse existing size, spacing and density roles before proposing another role.

A theme proposal must identify its public selection API, semantic roles, Light/Dark behavior and actual consumers.
Check text, action, boundary, focus and status contrast in the supported surfaces and states.
Check compact layouts with long labels, translated content, keyboard focus and the shared coarse-pointer minimum.
Document supported combinations, defaults, migration and known limitations alongside real examples.
A requested theme is not an implemented or reviewed theme until the source change and evidence are recorded.

## Compatibility and change records

When public props, supported combinations, defaults or token meanings change, describe before/after behavior and affected consumers.
For breaking changes, provide consumer migration examples and the order of migration.
The repository currently does not version the design system as a separate published package.
Implementation and documentation are identified by the same Git change; application release records establish deployment status.
