documents.title: Field and Input API review
documents.markdown:
# Field and Input API review

Reviewed: 2026-10-12. Source, typing and jsdom review. Actual rendering at 390/834/1440px, Light/Dark, locales, browser keyboard behavior and screen readers require separate browser review.

## Contract and findings

| Concern             | Current contract / finding                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Public API          | Field requires label/children and accepts layout=stack\|inline (default stack), description/actions/error/required/htmlFor. Types reject arbitrary style/class/size/color; runtime does not forward them. Unsupported layout throws RangeError                                |
| Anatomy             | stack: header(copy(label, description), actions) → control → error. inline: header/control columns, with description/error spanning both                                                                                                                                      |
| Layout              | stack gap=spacing-role-field-label (xxs 4px since 2026-10-13; previously xs 8px). inline: two minmax(0,1fr) columns, column-gap=spacing-role-field-column (existing sm 10px), row-gap=spacing-xxs. Control uses end/fit-content/max-width:100%. No automatic mobile stack API |
| ID / description    | Uses the single child's existing ID or htmlFor, otherwise useId. Merges and deduplicates existing aria-describedby IDs with Field description/error IDs                                                                                                                       |
| Error               | Field error sets child aria-invalid=true and custom child error=true. Without Field error, the child's existing validation state is retained                                                                                                                                  |
| required            | Wrapper required reaches the child; visible asterisk is aria-hidden. Wrapper does not clear child required=true                                                                                                                                                               |
| disabled / readOnly | Input Core owns these states; they are not Field variants. Readonly Textarea retains focus and required/error relations but blocks editing. NativeSelect projects the existing readOnly API to disabled because native select has no readonly behavior                        |
| Label activation    | Native input/select retains htmlFor. Label clicks explicitly focus contenteditable=true targets, excluding aria-disabled/disabled targets. No extra tab stop. Native label focus still needs browser verification                                                             |
| Custom child        | An adapter forwards ID/ARIA relations/required/error to the actual editable control. Field does not discover arbitrary internal controls inside multiple children/Fragments. The adapter supplies contenteditable naming                                                      |
| actions             | Do not nest actions inside the label. Independent action clicks were tested; long label/action wrapping and overflow need browser review                                                                                                                                      |

Sources: [Field.tsx](../../components/core/Field/Field.tsx), [Field CSS](../../components/core/Field/Field.module.css),
[Input contract](../../components/core/Input/input-contract.ts) and [InputParts](../../components/core/Input/InputParts.tsx).

## Reproduced problems and corrections

1. NativeSelect replaced child aria-invalid with undefined when no error existed, losing validation state inside Field. Explicit child state is now preserved when wrapper error is absent.
2. PasswordInput copied the input aria-label to its visibility command, failing to describe Show/Hide. Input naming stays intact; the toggle uses visibilityToggleLabel or the localized Show/Hide name.

These semantic corrections did not change visual geometry or Field API. The parallel spacing-role cleanup makes field-label/field-column aliases of existing xs/sm values.

## Checks and actual consumers

Five Core test files passed 35 tests; ProfileFormView/EntityTranslationsPanel passed 21 tests in two consumer files. Closed Input API typing and changed-file lint passed.
jsdom does not certify browser visuals, native label activation or screen readers.
Scoped Field type-test/story typing passed with skipLibCheck. The same check including library declarations failed on existing Storybook generic declarations; it is not a complete Storybook type pass.

| Consumer path                                        | Reproducible story / task to inspect                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| /my/profile → MyProfilePageView → ProfileFormView    | feature-my-profileform--populated / --long-values / --validation-error / --disabled. Bio Field+Textarea+character-count actions; Website TextInput                                                                                            |
| EntityTranslationsPanel → inline source-locale Field | feature-translation-localerows--expanded / --read-only / --phone / --tablet / --desktop. Long locales, source changes and NativeSelect description relations                                                                                  |
| PageEditor → ColumnsEditor                           | feature-page-editor-columns--reorder-between-columns / --readonly. Field+NumberInput currently passes the same label to wrapper and child. Browser review must check duplicate visible labels/names; the consumer must choose one label owner |
| ImmersiveSceneDescriptionEditor                      | Field → custom adapter → ControlledTiptapEditor forwards IDs/descriptions and accessibleLabel to editable content. Actual label focus/error delivery needs the product editor fixture                                                         |
| Core fixture                                         | core-layout-field--basic / --required-with-action / --error-state / --inline plus --read-only / --long-content / --editable-label. The fixed 420px wrapper became max 420px/available width to permit mobile review                           |

## Priorities for the next sequential reviews

No code was changed for this plan. These are inspection tasks, not confirmed defects.

| Stage     | Priority                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Actual fixture                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Toolbar   | ToolbarLayout uses ordinary Tab order; ToolbarSurface uses arrows/Home/End. Inspect CSS-hidden controls, RTL, nested toolbars, input-arrow interference, wrapped reading order and actions-inline visual Grid versus DOM order         | core-layout-toolbarsurface--formatting / --compact / --header-commands; core-layout-toolbarlayout--table-controls; pages-admin-content-lists--posts; pages-admin-file-manager--browser |
| Table     | Inspect compact/cards/content defaults, desktop 640px and mobile container boundaries, aria-sort, select-all/row selection, independent actions without duplicate activation, loading/empty/result announcements and focus restoration | core-data-display-datatableview--selectable-and-sortable / --compact-list / --inline-list / --truncated-names / --footer-boundary; admin content/file-manager fixtures                 |
| AppDialog | Actual owners are OverlayDialog and ContentModal/FormModal/ConfirmModal. Inspect title/description, initial focus/trap/restore, dismissible/busy/alertdialog, mobile body overflow and scoped strong primary actions                   | feature-confirmation-dialog--interactive / --loading / --blocked; core-overlays-blockingalertdialog--loading; product deletion/save/discard dialogs                                    |

Review Field's columns through actual Core responsive CSS and HTML label/required behavior. A fixed-width example does not prove max-width:100%, long content or narrow-parent behavior.
The later Toolbar source corrections and 45 editor/translation consumer tests are recorded, with remaining scope, in the [Toolbar API review](./toolbar-api-review.md).

documents.markdown:
# File browser contracts

This guide applies to the app File Manager and the editor File Library Picker. Core owns
geometry and appearance; the file-manager feature owns selection and navigation policy.
Neither consumer may add local tile widths, column CSS, checkbox styling or responsive overrides.

## Ownership and production adoption

| Responsibility                                                   | Definition                                                                                             | Consumers                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| File grid sizing, label truncation, highlight and keyboard focus | [Core SelectionSurface](../../components/core/SelectionSurface/SelectionSurface.tsx) and its owned CSS | Shared FileBrowserGridView in File Manager and Editor File Library Picker    |
| Parent navigation glyph and visibility                           | Core SelectionPath in SelectionSurface                                                                 | FileBrowserHeader and EditorFileLibraryPickerView                            |
| Common action hit area, glyph size and interaction states        | [Core IconButton](../../components/core/IconButton/IconButton.tsx) and Control.module.css              | Parent, grid, list, settings and management commands                         |
| Slider geometry, keyboard behavior and accessible step text      | [Core NativeRange](../../components/core/Input/NativeRange.tsx)                                        | Shared FileBrowserViewSettingsControl                                        |
| Type icons and compact list metadata                             | Core Display/FileTypeIcon and DataTableView inline rows                                                | Shared FileBrowserListView in both file browsers                             |
| Modifier selection and marquee policy                            | [useFileManagerSelection](../../features/file-manager/useFileManagerSelection.ts)                      | Both grid and list presentations                                             |
| Folder highlights versus submitted files                         | EditorFileLibraryPickerView's scoped folder selection and controlled selectedFiles                     | Single and multiple editor pickers; folders never enter the file form values |
| Consent-gated preference persistence                             | [useFileBrowserViewSettings](../../features/file-manager/useFileBrowserViewSettings.ts)                | FileManager and EditorFileLibraryPicker controllers                          |

Selection and keyboard focus are distinct states. The single selected-cell background indicates
selection; Core's focus outline appears for keyboard focus. Do not add another filename badge,
checkbox overlay, focus border or padding layer in a consumer.

The live component and story index is [generated-inventory.md](./generated-inventory.md);
production usage is recorded in [component-inventory.md](./component-inventory.md). These indexes
are regenerated from imports and story exports, not maintained as manual claims.

## Grid sizing

Use `SelectionViewport` as the available-width container and `SelectionGrid` for the grid.
`SelectionGrid.columns` reuses Core Layout's finite column count (1–12) and named responsive
breakpoints (`base`, `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`), with `auto` as the default.
Responsive values inherit forward and measure the enclosing viewport container, including
narrow dialogs on large screens. Unknown values and breakpoints are rejected at runtime.

```tsx
<SelectionViewport inset="sm">
  <SelectionGrid density="workspace" columns="auto">
    {/* SelectionSurface items */}
  </SelectionGrid>
</SelectionViewport>

<SelectionViewport inset="sm">
  <SelectionGrid density="workspace" columns={{ base: 3, sm: 6, lg: 'auto' }}>
    {/* SelectionSurface items */}
  </SelectionGrid>
</SelectionViewport>
```

An explicit count uses `repeat(N, minmax(0, 1fr))`: each column receives an equal fraction of
available width after gaps, `(width - (N - 1) * gap) / N`. Long names cannot force wider tracks.
Auto mode uses `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(100%, minimum), 1fr))`. The minimum determines
how many columns fit; it is not a fixed tile width or maximum. The remaining space is shared
by all columns. `auto-fill` keeps the last row aligned with preceding rows and prevents a
single remaining file from expanding across the surface. Empty tracks in a sparse final row
are intentional; residual space after a full row is not.

File browsers use `SelectionSurface.appearance="file"`, rather than the large square media-tile
presentation. Fractional **cell width** and **icon/thumbnail size** are separate contracts.
`iconSize` is `small | medium | large` on both the grid and surface: 1.5rem, 2rem and 3rem
preview bounds. Images stay inside that same bound; a wide cell never produces a giant icon
or square placeholder. The file label stays on one line and uses trailing ellipsis when it exceeds its track, without a grid checkbox. Do not split names into artificial filename fragments. The complete name remains available through the accessible label and title. Selection uses one cell background with ordinary text; there is no separate label badge. File surfaces use one xxs inset and xxs icon-to-label gap. The preview reserves only its icon height. SelectionViewport follows content height, without a fixed blank region.
The existing `tile` appearance remains available for media collections.

The grid's automatic minimum is 4.75rem for small icons, the density minimum for medium icons
(workspace: 6rem, 4.75rem in narrow containers), and 7.5rem for large icons. `spacing` is
`compact | standard | comfortable`, using shared xs/sm/lg spacing tokens. These are our
finite design-system decisions, not pixel values prescribed by Apple. Touch scrolling stays
native. Fixed counts should use responsive values when the same surface must support phones;
a user-selected explicit count intentionally overrides automatic fitting. None of these contracts
accepts local CSS, numeric icon sizes or arbitrary gaps.

The CSS behavior follows the [W3C CSS Grid flexible track specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-grid-2/#fr-unit)
and [automatic repeat rules](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-grid-2/#auto-repeat).

## Common toolbar

File browsers use the same Core [ToolbarLayout](../../components/core/Section/ToolbarLayout.tsx) as client/server DataTable controls through the SelectionToolbar adapter. Core owns container reflow, compact action and search/filter density, slot alignment and content insets. SelectionSurface keeps path/grid/row geometry only; it no longer owns a separate toolbar stylesheet. See [tables-and-toolbars.md](./tables-and-toolbars.md).

## Shared content inset

Both browser Views consume the shared sm→md Core LayoutInset for the visible toolbar and selection
viewport. Header toolbar layout uses no second inset; grid and list do not add independent
padding. This keeps the same inline edges in narrow containers as well as narrow viewports.
`Pages / Admin / File Manager / Inset Alignment` compares the actual edges and retains selection
through grid→list→grid changes. Item preview size and arrangement still belong to the grid owner.

## Search scope and continuation

The editor picker displays two compact Core xs TextButtons for all files and the current folder.
The named group retains the search-scope label without repeating a separate bold “Search:” row.
Each command keeps its visible scope in its accessible name; the folder command also identifies
the current folder. `aria-pressed` and Core's selected state indicate the active scope. Changing
scope restarts the actual controller query while preserving multiple file selections. Type and
sort controls retain their existing named Core contract.

Search uses `searchFileManagerItemsAction`: the default request size is 50; explicit sizes are
clamped to 1–100. The opaque returned `nextPageToken` owns continuation. Both production
controllers pass that cursor to Core NearEndLoader and await the next query. Browsing a folder
uses `listFileManagerItemsAction` with a 10,000-item complete-directory limit and no incremental
pagination; a truncated, duplicate or incomplete directory response is rejected by the action.
These are current action limits, not a claim about an unbounded backend catalog.

NearEndLoader observes a 240px prefetch margin around the closest scrolling ancestor. An explicit
scroll-root ref takes priority; an unbounded surface uses the document viewport. Each cursor is
attempted automatically once per `resetKey`. The owner supplies an awaited `onLoad`, next cursor
or `null`, localized load/loading/end/retry/failure labels and pending/error state. A compact
TextButton is exposed when observation fails or is unavailable; during automatic operation it
appears on keyboard focus. Pending keeps that command and its focus with `aria-disabled` and
announces one status. Failure retains existing results and exposes an explicit retry. Automatic
failure retry loops are blocked. A null cursor announces the end and removes the continuation
command after it loses focus; a focused continuation remains unavailable until the user moves
on so the final response does not drop keyboard focus. The loader does not own server state or
manufacture a cursor.

FileManager and EditorFileLibraryPicker guard simultaneous requests synchronously, reset pending
state when the query context changes, and ignore responses from an obsolete request generation.
Appending pages deduplicates overlapping kind/id pairs without clearing selection. A non-advancing
cursor is treated as a bounded load failure. Pagination pauses while input differs from the
debounced query. The editor's Paginated Search Results story uses local delayed pages; its
Loading More Search Results story is a controlled pending state. Neither performs an authenticated
service request. Controller tests separately exercise the actual transport callback and cursor.

## Reference and view settings

[Apple's Finder guide](https://support.apple.com/en-za/guide/mac-help/-mchldaafb302/mac)
describes separate icon-size and grid-spacing settings in View Options.
[Apple's iPhone Files guide](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/guide/iphone/iphc61044c11/ios)
places icon/list view changes with file-browser controls. We adopt their separation of preview
size, arrangement and selection behavior, while retaining our Core controls and theme tokens.
Apple's public guides do not provide exact responsive Files pixel measurements; do not present
our values as an Apple specification.

`FileBrowserViewToggle` renders grid/list as a Core SegmentedControl with icon options (a named radiogroup) and places a labelled adjustments button next to it.
It opens the shared `FileBrowserViewSettingsControl` popover. Local settings use Core Popover `size="compact"` (15rem/240px, viewport capped) and `padding="compact"` (xs). The composition uses xxs gaps, an h6 heading, xs label/value pairs and an xs Reset action aligned to the end. NativeRange retains its normal 30px interaction height; reduce surrounding whitespace rather than shrinking slider targets. This dense layout is shared by both file browser consumers. All fields use Core `NativeRange` sliders with the current value beside the label: icon size (small/medium/large, using the Core preview bounds), item spacing (compact/standard/comfortable), and columns (0 means automatic; 1–12 means an explicit count). `valueText` supplies localized step names to assistive technology. Arrow keys change one step, Home/End reach the endpoints, and pointer/touch movement updates the view immediately. Grid-specific controls are disabled in
list view. Changes apply immediately; Reset restores the appearance defaults while preserving
the current view. Escape and outside click close the panel and focus returns to its trigger.
The popover dialog is named by its heading, and all labels exist in every supported locale.

Both `FileManager` and `EditorFileLibraryPicker` consume `useFileBrowserViewSettings`.
The versioned `geul.file-browser.view.v1` local-storage entry contains only view mode, icon size,
spacing and column count. It never stores files, selected IDs, paths or search queries.
The current cookie consent schema exposes essential and analytics choices, with no preferences
category. To honor the requested consent gate conservatively, persistence requires current
analytics-enabled consent (the existing analytics-true flag, saved by the current consent UI). This is an acceptance signal for this
implementation, not a claim that display preferences are analytics. Without acceptance, settings
remain in the active session. Acceptance stores current settings; revocation or obsolete consent
removes stored preferences and the old unconditional `geul.file-manager.view` entry. Old view
mode is migrated only after valid acceptance. Corrupt/unknown versions and unavailable storage
fall back safely. Changes synchronize across mounted browsers and accepted browser tabs.
Storybook's controlled presentation stories remain deterministic and do not modify consent.

## Selection and confirmation

| Context              | Controls                                 | Activation                           | Confirmation                     |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- |
| Single file picker   | No checkboxes                            | Eligible file click or Enter/Space   | Immediately returns one file     |
| Multiple file picker | List checkboxes / grid highlight and Add | Selects files; double click previews | Add returns all selected files   |
| File Manager         | Highlight and list checkboxes            | Selects items; double click opens    | Domain actions consume selection |

`useFileManagerSelection` is shared by grid and list. Ordinary item clicks replace selection,
Ctrl/Cmd toggles one item, Shift selects a range from the anchor, and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift adds a range.
List checkboxes toggle individually; Shift-click uses the same range policy. File grids use Finder-style highlights without checkboxes or selected checkmark badges. Desktop marquee begins
in empty space. Ctrl/Cmd/Shift marquee keeps prior selections. Interactive controls and touch
scroll gestures never start marquee selection. In multiple selection contexts, touch taps toggle eligible files so mobile users can choose several files without a modifier key. Folders participate in browser highlight selection, including range and marquee, but never become file form values. Incompatible files remain excluded. The picker keeps folder selection scoped to the current location/query and retains file selection across folders. Click/Space selects a folder; double click/Enter opens it in both grid and list. Add is enabled only for eligible selected files. List checkbox selection remains file-only. Selections across
folders remain available for Add; an ordinary file click still replaces them.

Selection eligibility is separate from preview availability. An ineligible picker file is never
added by click, Space, range selection, marquee or Add, but Enter, double click and its context
menu can still open preview. Core `SelectionSurface.selectionUnavailable` requires a localized
`selectionUnavailableDescription`, keeps the row enabled and forbids `selected=true`.
The picker maps eligibility to this state rather than whole-row `unavailable`/`aria-disabled`.
Use `unavailable` only when every item action is unavailable. Selection-only constraints use
the existing muted text role rather than reducing the opacity of readable names and available actions.
The list supplies the same message through `DataTableView.rowInteraction.getDescription` for
desktop rows and mobile commands. Descriptions supplement the file name; they do not replace it.

The Core `selectionControl` slot owns checkbox placement. Table header and body use the same flex wrapper to remove inline baseline offsets; inline mobile controls and all content share the same vertical center. File lists consume Core `DataTableView.columnSizing="fixed"`: short trailing metadata tracks retain their widths, and the primary name track fills the remaining space. Both consumers use the same FileBrowserListView composition; do not duplicate columns or name/icon layouts. Long names stay on one line with trailing ellipsis in desktop and mobile lists, retaining the full DOM text and title. `DataTableView` exposes
`selection.onRowSelectionClick` for modifier-aware range policy. Selection changes never
submit or show an alert. Storybook form adapters show selected and added files only on Add,
then show submitted files and actual `FormData` file IDs on Submit. Only SingleSelectionForm and MultipleSelectionForm include the surrounding form harness; Browser and AccessibleRoot show the browser itself. The form is a Storybook integration example, not part of the browser component.

## Navigation and authorization

`SelectionPath pageTitle` renders the current location as the page's h1 (Heading scale 3 below `sm`, 2 above) for a browser that is the whole page; the admin file manager uses it, the editor library picker keeps the compact location. `SelectionPath.items[0]` is the accessible root. Only reachable ancestors belong in the supplied
path. `parentLabel` enables the up action below that root; it is absent at the root. Never render
a disabled parent action or reveal ancestors outside an authorized scope. Below the Core `sm` viewport or toolbar-container breakpoint, SelectionPath displays only the current folder name and the authorized parent button; ancestor names and separators are hidden. The current name receives the remaining width and uses trailing ellipsis if necessary. The full authorized path remains in the navigation title. Wider surfaces retain clickable authorized breadcrumbs. This is a Core path rule shared by both browsers, not a mobile consumer override. The parent action uses the curved `IconCornerLeftUp` glyph and the same default Core IconButton hit area, density and glyph size as the grid/list/settings actions. Do not assign a larger size to the parent action.

The current backend exposes a shared logical folder tree. `ListFileManagerItems` requires
`File.List` (author); folder creation, rename, move and deletion require `File.ManageLibrary`
(admin). The current protocol does not expose per-folder ACLs or a role-specific root. API
metadata must define any future restricted root; do not infer permissions from names, uploader,
MIME type or lack of a download URL. The scoped-root story demonstrates the presentation
contract without claiming that the current backend implements folder-specific permissions.

## Icons and compact lists

Use `Display/FileTypeIcon` with `inline`, `compact` or `preview` sizes. Folder/file icons belong
to the same name cell. Type labels are lowercase; folders have no size value or placeholder.
Both file browsers consume [FileBrowserListView](../../features/file-manager/ui/FileBrowserListView.tsx), backed by Core `DataTableView.mobileLayout="inline"`, `columnSizing="fixed"` and `density="compact"`. Every row is one line at every width: selection slot → inline icon → flexible filename → short format → size. Icons and checkboxes share the row's vertical center; unavailable/folder checkbox slots stay reserved so names align. Name text uses trailing ellipsis, retaining the full name in its title and accessible selection label. There is no metadata line under the filename.

At container widths below Core's `sm` breakpoint, the format and search location are omitted through `column.mobileVisibility="hidden"`; size remains at the trailing edge. Wider rows show lowercase extensions (`wav`, `png`, `pdf`) instead of MIME strings. Full MIME remains in the format title and preview/details. The format and size tracks are 64px and 80px; their xs text is secondary and aligned to the end. The primary track has no fixed minimum, so it receives the remaining width and truncates instead of forcing horizontal scrolling. Folders have no size or placeholder. A shared capacity formatter uses B/KB/MB/GB/TB with at most one fractional digit so large files do not produce long MB values. Search location, when needed, occupies a separate desktop track and is never stacked below the name.

Core owns inline row flex geometry, selection slots, min-height, padding, rules and responsive switching. Compact inline rows use existing xxs block padding, xs gaps/insets and the sm control minimum. Desktop table cells use the same compact table tokens. No new tokens, feature CSS or viewport-specific row copies are permitted. Card and two-line compact layouts remain separate generic DataTable contracts for other domains; file consumers always use inline. File Manager's upload time, uploader and usage details remain in the detail view; its default list uses this same file-name/format/size contract. List insets do not add an extra top gap.

## Verification

Inspect Core / Selection Surface / Contracts / File Icons and Grid Columns (automatic, fixed and responsive controls in one story). These grid examples use the file appearance; States retains the generic tile example. Folder Navigation compares the parent action with the grid/list actions and also shows an accessible root without an up action.
Inspect Core / Input / Native Range / States for automatic, explicit and disabled slider steps. Inspect Core / Display / File Type Icon and Core / Data Display / DataTableView / States / Inline List.
The editor's Multiple Selection Form, Single Selection Form, Accessible Root and Browser stories exercise production views with local state and no API mutation.

Check phone, tablet and desktop widths, light/dark themes and locale changes. Verify equal
computed column widths and no horizontal overflow; test sparse rows and long file names.
Exercise view settings, Reset, Escape/outside dismissal, consent acceptance/revocation, normal/modifier clicks, Shift checkboxes, marquee, touch scrolling, folder round trips,
Add and Submit. Run Core contract typing, Storybook typing, relevant component tests, CSS/TS
lint, and `scripts/design-system/validate.mjs`; refresh deterministic inventories when contracts
or stories change. Passing static checks does not replace visual and interaction verification.

## Boundary composition

File pickers use one divider per boundary. The inset toolbar uses `divider="none"`: control underlines and the table header divider already establish hierarchy. The table uses `rowDividers="between"` so the status footer owns the final boundary. `SelectionStatus divider="content"` aligns its rule with the responsive list inset (`sm` below the `sm` breakpoint, `md` above it) and the grid viewport. Do not stack a final table rule with a footer rule or draw a wider outer rule beside inset row dividers. Standalone tables retain their final rule by default. File Manager retains the final table rule and uses its status bar with `divider="none"`, so an extra outer rule cannot duplicate the table boundary. Its header and status share the responsive content insets, and its main stack uses the shared sm gap.

## Storybook ownership and deduplication

| Purpose                                   | Canonical story                                                                       | Coverage within that story                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| File browser layout/settings              | Editor File Library Picker / Browser                                                  | Grid/list toggle, density sliders, column settings, folder navigation; no extra form                                                      |
| Multiple file selection + form submission | Editor File Library Picker / Multiple Selection Form                                  | Checkbox/range/marquee selection, Add, actual FormData IDs and Submit report; both views                                                  |
| Single file selection + form submission   | Editor File Library Picker / Single Selection Form                                    | Immediate confirmation without checkboxes/Add, one form value and Submit report; both views                                               |
| Search/data states                        | Search Results, Paginated Search Results, Loading More Search Results, Loading, Empty | One story per distinct data/loading state; toggle views instead of duplicating lists                                                      |
| Authorized root                           | Accessible Root                                                                       | No inaccessible parent navigation                                                                                                         |
| File management                           | Pages / Admin / File Manager / Browser                                                | Grid/list/settings, selection and management actions; author permissions, detail, loading/empty/error remain separate states              |
| Local file input                          | Core / Input / FileInput                                                              | Single, multiple, accepted types, error and disabled contracts                                                                            |
| Local dropzone                            | Core / Input / FileDropzone                                                           | One multiple-selection story for keyboard, pointer and drag/drop; disabled and selection limits have distinct stories and result readouts |
| Grid geometry                             | Core / Selection Surface / Grid Columns                                               | Automatic/fixed/responsive modes through controls                                                                                         |
| Editor insertion and download policy      | File Insertion / Local Files; Media Download / Access Policy                          | Separate domain workflows, not copies of the library selector                                                                             |

Use the global viewport toolbar for phone/tablet QA rather than creating identical phone exports. Only the two form stories render the extra form. Add reports `selected` and `added`; Submit reports `selected`, `submitted` and real `fileIds`. Single-file confirmation updates the story's controlled selection before submission so the report remains coherent.

# Generated UI source inventory

Run `node scripts/design-system/inventory.mjs` to regenerate; `--check` fails when any generated file differs. No timestamp is emitted, so identical source produces identical output.

Static TypeScript AST source index. PascalCase TSX exports are component candidates, not proof of a pure or canonical component. Consumers follow named barrel reexports. Story relationships are direct imports only. Args and props are bounded source evidence, not exhaustive inherited API or state verification. Pages are source entrypoints, including redirects and development-only routes; source existence does not prove a served page.

Source manifest SHA-256: `b4eaa2e037b2e5ddbcdc692fc274beaa1ff34e14553bc0596ed5c35da52da4b3`. The hash covers paths and full source content inside the scope, including tests and stories. CSS, assets, generated dependency packages and runtime data are outside this index.

documents.title: Getting started with Geul design system
documents.markdown:
# Getting started with Geul design system

Use this repository's tokens, theme and Core components, and review the same implementation in Storybook.
Start at `Foundations / Overview`, find components in `Design System / Components`, and find product views in `Design System / Pages`.

## Run and review

```sh
pnpm storybook
pnpm storybook:typecheck
pnpm design-system:check
```

Storybook opens at `http://localhost:6010` by default.
For a static build, run `pnpm storybook:build`, then `pnpm storybook:preview`.
Change Theme, Locale and Viewport to inspect the same example.
Expanding a representative example runs the real Core or View with Controls.
A `Default` export appears first when available, followed by `Playground` and the named states.
The representative example uses the actual `Default`, then `Playground`, then the first available CSF example.
Controls change only the args connected by that example.
Use the state links to inspect loading, disabled, error, long content and composed examples separately.

## Use the system in the application

The design system lives in the application repository.
Use the existing app shell's `AppDesignSystemProvider`, locale provider and token CSS.
Do not redefine themes, CSS variables, colors or fonts per page.
The following example uses the actual Core API for an ordinary save command.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/core/Button';

export function SaveAction({ onSave }: { onSave: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Button tone="neutral" emphasis="medium" onClick={onSave}>
      Save
    </Button>
  );
}
```

In product UI, resolve the label from locale messages and connect the callback to the real save operation.
Use `loading` while the request is pending, then connect failure feedback and retry behavior.
Read the [component documentation contract](./component-documentation.md) and the relevant Core documentation
for API unions, naming requirements and rejected props.
For composition, read [spacing and icons](./spacing-icon-contract.md) and [size and density](./size-density-contract.md).

## Documentation structure

| Location                                                       | Content                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Handbook / Getting Started, Contribution, Tokens and Changelog | Entry guidance, ownership, token intent, change proposals and change records                     |
| Foundations                                                    | Typography, spacing, icons, sizing, responsive behavior, specimen layout and accessibility rules |
| Core / Documentation                                           | Purpose, representative live example, anatomy, API, usage, tokens and states                     |
| Core / Playground and named state examples                     | Actual interaction, supported states, content and keyboard behavior                              |
| Design System / Usage Rules                                    | Paired examples of supported and incorrect composition for the same task                         |
| Design System / Patterns and Composition                       | Working forms, lists and input combinations built with Core                                      |
| Feature and Pages                                              | Product domains and production Views, fixture data and service boundaries                        |

A component's documentation follows Overview → Playground → states/features → recipes where those examples
are relevant. This order does not require an atomic component hierarchy.
Read the [page documentation contract](./page-documentation.md) for server, authorization, SSR and actual
assistive technology boundaries. Documentation registration and story counts are not verification results.

## Official writing references

- [How to document your design system](https://storybook.js.org/blog/how-to-document-your-design-system-best-practices-tools/): keep components, token intent, working compositions, paired usage examples and contribution rules discoverable together.
- [Structuring your Storybook](https://storybook.js.org/blog/structuring-your-storybook/): put entry and change guidance first, then distinguish explanation, Playground, states and recipes.
- [4 ways to document your design system](https://storybook.js.org/blog/4-ways-to-document-your-design-system-with-storybook/): combine real examples, source, API and guidance using the official Docs addon.

The implementation uses local Storybook 10.5.8 CSF and Doc Blocks APIs.
Reference articles' package names, old API examples and classification labels do not define the product API.

documents.title: Hierarchy spacing contract
documents.markdown:
# Hierarchy spacing contract

Hierarchy spacing consumes named design-system roles. A default is not a rule imposing one fixed pixel value on every screen.

## System definitions

- --geul-hierarchy-step: default ordinary child step, referring to existing spacing-lg. Currently 16px with a 16px root.
- --geul-hierarchy-reorder-step: compact reorder-row alignment to the parent label, referring to max(control-height-compact, interaction-minimum) + spacing-xxs. At the default root size, this is 32px for fine pointers and 48px for coarse pointers.
- @echovisionlab/design-system/tokens owns values; the generator projects CSS. Do not introduce a separate numeric scale.

## Core usage

```tsx
// Ordinary hierarchy consumes the system default.
<HierarchyIndent>Child content</HierarchyIndent>

// Select an existing spacing token when the screen needs another hierarchy step.
<Hierarchy spacing="md">
  <Disclosure label="Parent" density="compact" defaultOpened>
    <Disclosure nested label="Child" density="compact">
      Content aligned with the child heading
    </Disclosure>
    <TextButton nested density="chrome" href="/child">Child link</TextButton>
  </Disclosure>
</Hierarchy>

// Details aligned with the parent reorder-row label.
<HierarchyIndent alignment="parent-label">Track details</HierarchyIndent>
```

Hierarchy supplies selected spacing to descendants. A nested Hierarchy without spacing inherits the parent selection. HierarchyIndent enabled=false omits that step's indentation. Arbitrary numbers/pixels/style overrides are not public APIs.

Disclosure nested represents a child group inside a body aligned with the parent label. Include the child's default heading inset so spacing is not applied twice. Control tracks own handled-row alignment.
contentIndent="label" aligns a body with its own heading; it remains distinct from a child step.

Navigation lists group links with Disclosure density="chrome": compact geometry (28px control, end chevron)
whose label starts on the chrome rows' xs 8px line, the same start as TextButton density="chrome" links and
SideNavigation items. Do not mix density="compact" groups with chrome links; their labels differ by 4px.

TextButton nested includes internal chrome padding in text alignment and prevents margin-based horizontal overflow on full-width links.
SectionCard nested includes internal padding and its leading border. SideNavigation consumes the same hierarchy role between group headings and child labels, accounting for icon tracks and active borders.
Selecting spacing smaller than required controls/markers/card insets does not remove them or overlap them with negative margins.

## Consumers

- Core SideNavigation, ParameterPanel and nested Disclosure/SectionCard/TextButton.
- Form field/settings/validation groups and recursive condition groups.
- Menu editing, recursively nested menu translation targets and Shell mobile menus.
- Comment depth, public credit groups and email-editor variable lists.
- Release-track details and ReorderRow parent-label alignment.
- Tiptap child blocks and public document child blocks share the default step. Directly nested HTML lists also avoid duplicated margin/marker padding.

Quote borders, callout icon insets, list-marker space, code tabs, print specifications and authored-page geometry retain their own roles.

## Verification

Storybook Core/Layout/Hierarchy/Contract shows the default and md choice using actual Core consumers. Foundations/Tokens Hierarchy defaults charts show the source relationships.
Type fixtures permit named spacing and reject numeric/style/Core-state escapes. Runtime contracts verify inheritance, preserved heading alignment and removal of bypass props.
Core ReorderGutter reserves an editor control track on touch. Document layout and authored hierarchy remain domain content.

documents.title: IconButton and TextButton follow-up review
documents.markdown:
# IconButton and TextButton follow-up review

Reviewed: 2026-10-12. Status: code-contract and Storybook review draft.
Scope: API, states, semantics, glyph boxes and long indicator labels for both Core components. The code reviewer did not operate a browser.
Earlier behavior corrections and type contracts are recorded in the [Button family review](button-api-review.md).

## Criteria and actual contract

[Carbon Icons](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/foundations/icons/guidelines) informs the comparison of a 16px artboard, centered icon/text alignment and a minimum 44px touch target.
[Carbon Button accessibility](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/button/accessibility) requires hover/focus guidance for icon commands and Tab/Enter/Space activation.
[Carbon Button guidelines](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/button/guidelines) informs long-label wrapping and the distinction between commands and navigation. Carbon enums, fills and padding are not copied.

Authority: [IconButton](../../components/core/IconButton/IconButton.tsx), [TextButton](../../components/core/TextButton/TextButton.tsx),
[Control CSS](../../components/core/Control.module.css), [TextButton CSS](../../components/core/TextButton/TextButton.module.css) and the [spacing/icon contract](spacing-icon-contract.md).

| Concern              | Reviewed contract / decision                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ordinary commands    | neutral/medium; supporting commands use low. Existing IconButton neutral/low defaults were not changed indiscriminately without classifying roles                                                                                                                                       |
| Supporting consumers | FileBrowserViewToggle uses SegmentedControl icon options; FormattingButtons uses Core-owned IconButton `pressed`; ToolbarCommand defaults to low in supporting toolbars. No incorrect low ordinary command was found in this scope                                                      |
| IconButton name      | Exactly one of label / aria-label / aria-labelledby. Callers ensure external IDs exist. count is decorative; names/descriptions convey business meaning                                                                                                                                 |
| IconButton state     | Ordinary actions retain focus and block activation while pending. Pending replaces glyph/count with a named spinner and restores them afterward. disabled is native disabled. The drag-handle has a separate sensor contract; pending/disabled uses native disabled and blocks dragging |
| TextButton semantics | href renders an anchor; actions render native buttons. selected is visual ancestry; callers supply aria-current/pressed/expanded. No loading API                                                                                                                                        |
| TextButton defaults  | appearance default maps to neutral/medium, muted to low. Typography and control geometry are distinct. nowrap defaults to false; indicator follows the label                                                                                                                            |
| API escapes          | Existing types reject arbitrary style/className/framework props and control sizes, submit/form props on links, and indicators on links                                                                                                                                                  |

## Glyphs and optical space

IconButton padding is 0. Layout targets are compact 28px / xs 30px / chrome 32px, with a coarse-pointer minimum of 44px. The SVG frame stays at the 16px chrome-icon-size role.
Original Tabler 24×24 viewBox paths and live areas are preserved. SVG internal space, unused control target space and parent gaps are distinct measurements, not additive CSS padding.
Different close/menu/plus widths did not justify common scaling or cropping. The [spacing/icon contract](spacing-icon-contract.md) distinguishes path calculations from browser measurements.

[OpticalGlyphComparison Story](../../components/core/IconButton/IconButton.stories.tsx) compares close/menu/plus at compact/xs/chrome sizes. Short visible Tooltip copy and the target-specific accessible name are supplied separately.
This is a glyph-geometry example, not approval of real close/add/menu tasks. Original glyph and token sources were unchanged.

## Reproduced defect and scoped correction

TextButton with nowrap=false and an indicator still inherited common Control .label white-space:nowrap / ellipsis, contradicting its API and long-menu-label behavior.
TextButton now owns normal wrapping and overflow-wrap through its label class; nowrap=true retains the original single-line ellipsis. The shared .label rule for other Core components was unchanged.

Consumers: [ShellView](../../features/shell/ui/Shell/ShellView.tsx), [LanguageMenu](../../features/shell/LanguageMenu.tsx) and [LocationPlaceMenu](../../features/location/LocationPlaceMenu.tsx). Locale names, place names and navigation labels consume this indicator contract.
An explicitly nowrap Layout supplied by a caller retains its own composition reflow contract.

[LongMenuLabel / LongMenuLabelNoWrap Story](../../components/core/TextButton/TextButton.stories.tsx) compares real DropdownMenu triggers within 240px. The full accessible name and expanded/menu relationship remain; indicator is decorative.
The long English label is an authored fixture, not a check of every translation's length.

## Pending glyph correction

A reviewer identified the original glyph overlapping the spinner in pending Core IconButton. Local content retained children/count while adding ProgressBar.
Pending now removes the original glyph and decorative count, rendering only the named ProgressBar. Root, size, target, action name, busy state and duplicate-activation blocking remain. Glyph/count return after completion; PendingTransition demonstrates this transition.

PendingTransition restores idle after a three-second mock operation; PendingWithBadge is static pending.
Before correction, two action/drag-handle regressions failed because SVG content remained. Tests cover names, progress naming, size contract, duplicate blocking and idle restoration, not browser CSS pixel geometry.
The follow-up run passed IconButton/TextButton/ToolbarCommand: 3 files / 43 tests, the Core type suite and ESLint for three changed IconButton TS/TSX files. Stylelint was not rerun because common CSS and tokens were unchanged.

## Executed checks and remaining scope

The earlier runtime run passed IconButton / TextButton / ToolbarCommand: 3 files / 41 tests. Two added nowrap false/true cases check full names, decorative indicators and expanded/menu relationships.
The Core type fixture suite and TextButton CSS stylelint passed. ESLint --max-warnings=0 passed for four changed TS/TSX files, with 0 errors / 0 warnings.
jsdom does not verify actual wrap height, path bounds or touch geometry. Browser review must separately measure LongMenuLabel height/indicator placement, NoWrap single-line behavior, SVG frames/path spans, targets, padding and parent gaps.
Hover/focus Tooltip, disabled/pending/pressed, light/dark, locales and viewports remain browser-review items.

IconButton does not automatically copy its accessible name into a visual Tooltip. Carbon's hover/focus guidance must be reviewed in compositions such as ToolbarCommand and actual consumers.
This record does not approve all icon-only tooltips or VoiceOver/Orca integration.

## Baseline and change scope

Twelve dirty files in the two directories were copied and SHA-256 recorded first.
Local records: `/tmp/geul-icon-text-review-before.json`, `/tmp/geul-icon-text-review-before/`.
Scoped diff: `/tmp/geul-icon-text-review.patch`; before/after hashes: `/tmp/geul-icon-text-review-changes.json`.
Changes covered TextButton source/CSS/test/Story, IconButton source/test/Story and this document. Shared Control CSS, tokens and generated artifacts were unchanged.
The pending follow-up baseline and original copies are separately preserved in `/tmp/geul-icon-pending-before.json`. Its scoped diff is `/tmp/geul-icon-pending-review.patch`.

documents.title: Image selection, preparation and upload
documents.markdown:
# Image selection, preparation and upload

## Ownership and usage

`ImageUploadField` owns the named native picker and drop target. `ImageUploadCropField` adds the crop dialog.
`ImageUploadCropController` supplies product labels, source formats, upload type, preparation state and upload callbacks.
Artwork, featured images and social-card backgrounds consume this controller. Avatar and artist controllers consume
`prepareImageFileForPreview` through the same upload policy. `useUpload` owns preparation before transport and
validates the prepared file before starting the upload session.

The controller shows the field name and image surface without a persistent ratio caption, maximum-size caption
or information button. Crop geometry remains in the preview and dialog. Accessible crop handle names,
instructions and selection descriptions remain available; failures and preparation status are still announced.
Optional constraints supplied directly to the domain-free Core crop field remain supported for other tasks.

## Preview and removal

Hug previews (logos) size the preview box, and therefore the remove action's anchor, to the image itself.
`surface` previews theme-specific artwork on its own background (`theme-light`, `theme-dark`) independent of
the app theme. The default outside remove action is a corner badge: an opaque chip centred on the preview's
top-end corner. `ImageUploadField` reserves half the control as a block-start/inline-end gutter whenever a
remove action is offered, so the badge never covers the field label, description or neighbouring fields.
`removeButtonPlacement="inside"` (avatars) keeps the action within the image.

`removeButtonAppearance="avatar"` requires a circle preview and inside placement. It selects Core
IconButton's `appearance="media-overlay"`: a 16px circular visual with a 12px X or pending spinner,
using the existing `icon-size-md` and `icon-size-xs` roles. The rectangular native target stays 24px on fine pointers
and grows inward to the shared 44px coarse-pointer minimum. Its corners accept pointer input across the entire
painted badge. Hover/press affects the visual; keyboard
focus outlines the full target. Disabled/pending preserve the visual and block execution through IconButton.
The strong danger treatment remains an explicit avatar-removal choice.

Use the avatar appearance for profile-photo removal. It does not resize logos, artwork, crop actions,
ordinary media buttons or the global xs/compact sizes. The default appearance retains the existing full-target
treatment. `ProfileAvatarControl` selects the avatar appearance; `UserAvatarUploader` consumes it for account
profiles and the 56px admin `UserProfileFormSection`. The profile control's default image size remains 80px.

## Source and prepared-file policy

Managed raster sources accepted by their upload type are decoded and resized locally before entering the crop dialog.
PNG, JPEG, WebP and AVIF are encoded as WebP; HEIC/HEIF uses the installed local decoder before WebP encoding.
The longest prepared edge is at most 4096 pixels. Encoding starts at quality 0.86 and lowers quality/size when
necessary to satisfy the target's prepared-file limit. The shared tolerance is 30 MiB; smaller targets, such as
client/label logos at 5 MiB, use their own limit. The final upload validator remains authoritative for the output.

Managed originals have no byte-size rejection before this processing. This does not promise that every image can
be decoded on every device: malformed files, missing browser codec support and local memory failures remain
recoverable preparation errors. Strict managed preparation rejects decoding/encoding failure instead of quietly
sending the original. Files are not uploaded when preparation or final validation fails.

GIF, SVG, ICO and upload types that cannot accept the normalized format retain their existing passthrough and
server-compatible size/format restrictions. Animated loader GIFs retain animation and their actual loader-upload
limit. This change does not redefine backend limits or remove upload-session validation.

## Picker and recovery

Native `accept` hints include allowed source MIME types and equivalent filename extensions. This supports valid
source files for which the browser supplies an empty MIME type, including HEIC/HEIF. The native picker is a hint,
not a security boundary; dropped files and selections still pass runtime type and prepared-file validation.
Unsupported source types do not start a crop session. Local preparation is announced, repeat selection is blocked
while preparation runs, and failures leave the picker usable for a new selection.

`ReleaseArtworkView` explicitly supplies `RELEASE_ARTWORK`, rather than inheriting the featured-image default.
Callers with another upload type should pass that type so its source and output policy are used together.

## Review and verification

Review `Feature / Upload / ImageUploadCropController / Square Artwork` for the compact empty surface and native
accept policy. `Artwork Local Preparation` processes a real PNG in the browser, opens the real crop dialog and
closes it with Escape. Its image output remains local to the fixture; no upload or persistent relationship is written.
Review light/dark and named custom themes at mobile, tablet and desktop widths.

Source tests cover oversized originals entering normalization, target-specific prepared limits, strict decoder
failure, bitmap resize/release, MIME/extension hints, controller captions and preparation-state recovery.
Browser fixtures do not establish backend authorization, real upload deployment or native VoiceOver results.

For avatar removal, review Core ImageUploadField / AvatarRemovalComparison and AvatarRemovalStates at 56px and
80px, then Feature User / ProfileAvatarControl / AdminWithImage, WithImage and DisabledWithImage.
The comparison renders the default and avatar appearances side by side; the state fixture exercises badge-edge
hit-testing, removal, keyboard activation, disabled and pending behavior. Core IconButton / MediaOverlayHover and
MediaOverlayActive check that forced hover/active paints only the badge. Review light/dark, hover, keyboard focus,
RTL and coarse-pointer targets. The coordinator owns final browser regression and visual acceptance.

## Migration

Avatar consumers opt in with `removeButtonAppearance="avatar"`, `removeButtonPlacement="inside"` and a circle
preview. `ProfileAvatarControl` supplies these props centrally; account/admin callers need no size overrides.
Other image consumers keep the default appearance. Direct IconButton consumers must supply inside media placement
when selecting `appearance="media-overlay"` and cannot provide a local size or shape.

Before this review, managed sources were rejected above 20 MiB, and non-HEIC sources reached the crop dialog
without normalization. They now enter bounded local preparation before crop and retain final upload validation.
The crop controller's ratio, format and size hints are no longer persistent visual content; explicit crop accessibility
and runtime error information remain. Existing Core props and server upload contracts are preserved.

documents.title: TextInput, PasswordInput, NumberInput and Select review
documents.markdown:
# TextInput, PasswordInput, NumberInput and Select review

Reviewed: 2026-10-12, in that order. Scope: public types, states/relations/input events, jsdom regressions and Storybook examples. Browser visuals and screen-reader approval are separate.
Authority: [Input Core](../../components/core/Input/index.ts), [shared contract](../../components/core/Input/input-contract.ts),
[InputParts](../../components/core/Input/InputParts.tsx) and [Input CSS](../../components/core/Input/Input.module.css).
Installed versions: react-aria-components 1.22.1 / react-aria 3.53.1.

## Comparison criteria

[Carbon Text input accessibility](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/text-input/accessibility) informs native input and keyboard visibility-toggle review.
[Number input accessibility](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/number-input/accessibility) informs arrow increments, bounds, single-input Tab entry and description/error relations.
Explain range/step constraints in description before input. This review does not adopt Carbon dimensions, colors or borders.
[Carbon Select accessibility](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/select/accessibility) describes HTML select. Geul Select uses React Aria ComboBox, so input/button/listbox relations need separate verification. Carbon native-select behavior or results do not approve this ComboBox.

## Shared states and relations

| Condition         | Actual contract                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| label             | Uses an internal Label or parent Field relation. Placeholder is not a name. Standalone use requires label/ARIA naming                                              |
| description/error | Internal description and message errors join external aria-describedby IDs on the input. Boolean error expresses invalid state only                                |
| required          | Asterisk is decorative; required/aria-required belongs to the actual input. validationBehavior is aria                                                             |
| readOnly          | Value remains readable/focusable; editing is blocked. Password visibility remains available. Number increments and Select clear/open are blocked                   |
| disabled          | Disables the actual input and accessory commands; it is distinct from readOnly                                                                                     |
| pending           | None of these four Core components has loading/pending props. aria-busy alone does not block editing. The task owner chooses readOnly/disabled and status guidance |
| Events            | Shared onClick/onFocus/onBlur/onKeyDown/onKeyUp/IME composition handlers receive actual input events. Number onChange is a separate value callback                 |

Existing Field label/error/required relations were retained. This review did not add universal type/runtime rejection of nameless standalone inputs. Appropriate labels/ARIA names and existing target IDs remain consumer-review requirements.

## Public API and anatomy

| Core                                                           | API / defaults                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Structure / behavior                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [TextInput](../../components/core/Input/TextInput.tsx)         | size sm, density comfortable; appearance underline/bare, textRole body/title/code/caption. type text/email/tel/url/search/password/date/time/datetime-local. value/defaultValue string/number; onChange native event | label → leftSection/input/rightSection → help/error. Projects string values and forwards min/max/step, length/pattern/autocomplete/IME attributes                                              |
| [PasswordInput](../../components/core/Input/PasswordInput.tsx) | Excludes TextInput type/rightSection. Hidden by default. visible is controlled, defaultVisible initializes it; onVisibilityChange and visibilityToggleLabel are supported                                            | Core owns the trailing visibility command. Type changes preserve value. Its localized Show/Hide or explicit visibilityToggleLabel name is separate from the input name                         |
| [NumberInput](../../components/core/Input/NumberInput.tsx)     | value/defaultValue number/string; callback number or empty string. min/max/step, decimalScale, allowNegative/allowDecimal, hideControls, prefix/suffix. Default maximum 20 fraction digits                           | prefix/input/suffix/decrement/increment. allowNegative=false clamps min to at least 0; allowDecimal=false caps fraction digits at 0. Bounds/readOnly/disabled determine increment availability |
| [Select](../../components/core/Input/Select.tsx)               | width fill/content; string/option/group data. Controlled/uncontrolled selection/search/open APIs, searchable/clearable/allowDeselect, renderOption                                                                   | input/optional clear/open → portalled listbox/group/option. Non-search input can be internally readonly while still selectable. Core readOnly blocks selection/clear/open                      |

Installed NumberInput vendor code removes explicit spinbutton role and aria-valuenow/min/max for VoiceOver compatibility. Actual DOM is a text input with aria-roledescription="Number field" in en-US; arrow increments remain.
Evidence: installed react-aria dist/private/numberfield/useNumberField.mjs, role-override comment and inputProps. This review did not add spinbutton. Actual assistive-technology number-field announcements are unverified.

## Geometry and gaps

Root label/help/error gaps use spacing-xxs, 4px. Input padding is block 4px / inline 8px; the flex wrapper declares no separate label–accessory gap. Measure padding and accessory targets independently.
Password/Number/Select accessories use the greater of control-height-xs and interaction-minimum. These were not changed to Button HeaderDensity or control-label roles.
Input CSS owns size-dependent height/type and compact density height. ToolbarDensity compact projects TextInput and Select to xs/compact; the same automatic projection was not added to NumberInput.
Coarse targets and actual long-label/value/locale overflow require browser review. Existing rejection of style/className/vendor skins and reserved data attributes remains.

## Reproduced problems and corrections

| Reproduction                                                                            | Correction                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| External aria-describedby removed internal TextInput/PasswordInput help/error relations | Compose relations once at TextField; do not repeat naming/description props on Input that overwrite them |
| Public NumberInput/Select onClick/onKeyUp/composition callbacks were not called         | Forward handlers to the actual Input; regressions check callback targets                                 |
| readOnly Select opened with dropdownOpened=true                                         | Open bridge projects false when disabled/readOnly; both states block clear and selection                 |
| PasswordInput public rightSection was ignored and replaced by visibility accessory      | Remove rightSection from public types and add rejected fixture. No actual consumer use was found         |

An external aria-invalid=false could also turn off TextInput/PasswordInput error semantics. Explicit error now keeps invalid=true on the actual Input; without error, external aria-invalid is preserved.

## Actual consumers and examples

- [VerificationFlowView](../../features/auth/ui/VerificationFlowView.tsx): email/required/autocomplete and external description/error IDs.
- [ProfileFormView](../../features/my/ui/ProfileForm/ProfileFormView.tsx): parent Field relations and public profile editing.
- [SharePasswordView](../../features/share/SharePasswordView.tsx): readOnly while pending, retained value and input-focus restoration after errors.
- [ParameterPanel](../../components/core/ParameterPanel/ParameterPanel.tsx), [MultiFilterValueInput](../../features/data-table/MultiFilterValueInput.tsx): Number bounds/step/disabled and domain value callbacks.
- [EntityTranslationsPanel](../../features/translation/EntityTranslationsPanel.tsx): grouped locale options and clear/read states.

Storybook added ReadOnly for all four Core components, TextInput RequiredWithHelp, PasswordInput Visible and NumberInput WithoutControls. Existing error/disabled/selected/bounded/long-content stories remain.
Adding stories does not complete actual 390/834/1440px, light/dark or locale visual review.

## Executed checks and remaining scope

[InputContracts.test.tsx](../../components/core/Input/InputContracts.test.tsx) checks explicit-ID label relations, internal/external descriptions/errors, required, readonly focus/disabled, controlled Password visibility, one Enter/Space toggle with value/focus retained, Number arrows/bounds/Tab exclusion, Select forced-open blocking/allowDeselect and native events.
Existing Field and SharePassword/ProfileForm/EntityTranslations consumer regressions were also run.
The four-Core contract suite had 18 regressions; together with InputWrappers/InputBehavior/NumberInput/Field and SharePasswordView/ProfileFormView/EntityTranslationsPanel, 8 files / 72 tests passed.
Closed Input API fixtures and scoped typing for tests/four stories passed. ESLint --max-warnings=0 passed for ten changed Input TS/TSX files. Scoped typing used existing Next declarations and skipLibCheck; it is not a full-app build result.

Unverified: browser IME results, autocomplete, type-specific native UI, text selection/clipboard; complete Select arrows/Enter/Escape navigation; Number locale/fractions/negative/direct-input commit/mobile keyboard; pending announcements; VoiceOver/Orca.
jsdom composition-callback forwarding does not approve real Korean IME. Browser composition/commit/cancel must be reviewed separately.
New API reviews for Textarea, NativeSelect, MultiSelect, Date/Time and Pin/Tags/SearchCombobox are outside this four-Core scope.

documents.title: Core input contract
documents.markdown:
# Core input contract

The production Input and Field owners now use React Aria Components or an intentionally native
select. Mantine input inheritance, slot skins, `variant`, `styles`, `classNames`, `vars`, `unstyled`,
arbitrary width and margin props are absent from the public contracts. The runtime projection also drops
unknown style props and reserved `data-geul-*` attributes passed through JavaScript spreads.

Every input uses the existing size scale (`xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`) and density
(`comfortable`, `compact`). Behavioral `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`, validation and
controlled/default value props remain explicit. `grow` is a shared field-layout capability.
TextInput's `appearance="bare"` and `textRole="title|code|caption|body"`, and Textarea's
`textRole="code|body"`, belong to Core and replace former editor skin overrides. Named Layout
primitives own spacing. Authored media, table-column and field-container geometry can remain on
outer native content frames; they cannot restyle the inner input.

Default, hover, focus, invalid, disabled and read-only styling is shared in Input.module.css.
Focus is always visible, including `animate={false}` and reduced motion. Invalid focused fields
retain their danger underline and expose a separate focus outline. Error/description associations
are owned by RAC or explicit `aria-describedby`; Field injects label/required/description/error
into its actual child and supports checkbox association.

Core Switch slides its thumb using `transform` and transitions thumb/track colors with
the existing `motion.slow` (300ms) and `motion.easing` (ease-out) tokens. Geometry and
monochrome roles remain shared; RTL reverses the travel direction. `animate={false}` and
`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` remove transitions without removing focus or selected state.
CookieConsentBannerView and CookieConsentSettings consume this same Switch contract.

Checkbox, Radio and Switch share one choice grid: a 16px indicator (`chrome-icon-size`), an 8px
indicator-to-label gap (`spacing-xs`) and a 28px row (`control-height-compact`, 44px for coarse pointers).
The Switch track is 28×16px (`control-height-compact` × the indicator size) with a 12px circular thumb and
equal 2px end insets in every density, so it carries the same visual weight as a checkbox beside 14px text.
All three share one state language: off is an empty 1px `border-strong` outline; on is one `text-primary` mass with a
`text-on-action` mark (check or minus, a 6px point, or the thumb). Input accessories use 16px Core glyphs with a 1.5
stroke (`InputGlyphs.tsx`); text characters are not used as icons.
Optional onLabel/offLabel text sits outside the moving track so it cannot collide with the thumb;
it is decorative state copy, while the stable control name and native checked state remain accessible.
Its label remains the full click target; compact appearance does not shrink coarse-pointer targets.
Choice labels honor the shared size/density minimum height; disabled Switch tracks use the existing
disabled opacity while preserving thumb position. A compact track is not the whole interaction target.
Use Switch for one on/off setting, not for two named layout modes.

Visual references inspected on 2026-10-12: [Atlassian Toggle examples](https://atlassian.design/components/toggle/examples)
(rounded track, circular thumb, position and check/cross state cues) and
[Geist Toggle](https://vercel.com/geist/toggle) (compact track, minimal circular thumb, quiet off state).
Geul adopts their clear silhouette and position change with its existing monochrome semantic roles,
not their green/blue palette, icons, shadows or component APIs. Focus, disabled and reduced-motion
behavior stay with Core. Appearance does not determine whether an application saves immediately.

Core Radio uses the same 300ms ease-out tokens for background, ink and boundary color
transitions. Its circular geometry and selected colors stay unchanged; focus appears
immediately. `animate={false}` on a Radio or Radio.Group and reduced motion remove these
transitions. Public form SelectField consumes the shared Radio definition.

Select and MultiSelect use RAC collections and keyboard selection. MultiSelect additionally
supports the existing selected-value collapse, expansion, removal and order callbacks. Search
combobox controllers use `useInputCombobox`, not a vendor store. FileInput and FileDropzone share
Core file-selection accept/size rules. Visible auxiliary copy comes from caller labels or the
Core dictionary for the application's twenty locales; unknown locales fall back to English.

MultiSelectComboboxView retains its full option data while MultiSelect filters the menu, so
selected labels remain readable during search. Backspace removal uses the current controlled
search value. Its Editable story updates selection and options through Storybook args for
existing-option selection, removal and local creation; ReadOnly retains its disabled behavior.

## Date and time values

- DateInput: `yyyy-mm-dd | null`.
- MonthPickerInput: `yyyy-mm-01 | null` (only month/year segments are visible).
