- DateTimePicker: `yyyy-mm-dd HH:mm[:ss] | null`; granularity is controlled by Core.
- DateRangeInput: `[yyyy-mm-dd | null, yyyy-mm-dd | null]`.
- TimePicker: `HH:mm[:ss]`; 24-hour segments preserve the local wall clock.
- DateTimeInput retains the existing `{ date, time }` domain value and explicit translated labels.

RAC's locale controls segment ordering, labels and calendar presentation. Calendar values use
`@internationalized/date` rather than UTC conversion. Existing callers that supply `Date` are
normalized by local calendar fields; callbacks return the string contract. Public scheduling,
release/work editors, sharing, form conditions/settings and table filters use these Core owners.

## Proof and previews

`components/core/Input/Input.type-test.tsx` proves positive value contracts and rejects skin,
numeric size, foreign density, portal and reserved attribute overrides. The input-specific
`tsconfig.type-test.json` runs without relying on the application's excluded preview sources.
Runtime tests mount actual RAC inputs, date segments, dropdowns, file triggers and selection
callbacks. They cover style-spread projection, mandatory focus, error association, read-only
behavior, timezone-free values, file rejection and selected-value ordering.

`Core / Input / Contract / Interactive` provides size, density, animation, invalid, disabled
and read-only controls for real mounted parts. Light/Dark and Locale belong to the single global
DesignSystemProvider. The primitive fixture pages use the same production owners.

## Compact and content sizing

SegmentedControl uses the existing control height and compact density with 4px block padding.
`fullWidth` distributes the available width across options; omit it for a content-width choice.
Document layout settings in both PageEditor and PostEditor use compact, content-width selection
groups in a wrapping LayoutInline. Each heading stays with its two choices. They do not reserve
an entire row until the actual available width requires wrapping. This composition uses no new
tokens and keeps the three values independent, with radio-group naming and arrow-key selection.

Compact fields consume the shared 28px compact control role. Any coarse pointer raises interactive controls and accessories to 44px, and text entry to at least 16px. Visual glyphs stay compact. Select `width="content"` is a closed Core contract: its label measurement, clear/toggle tracks and narrow-screen fill are owned by Select. Callers supply options and behavior, not sizing CSS. Raw width strings and visual props remain rejected.

## Region size

`InputSizeProvider size="…"` declares one input size for a region. Every Core input inside it (text, select, number, date, file, tags, choice and segmented controls) takes that size unless the input sets `size` itself; a compact toolbar still forces `xs`. All inputs resolve size through one path (`useToolbarInputPresentation`), so labels, text and control scale cannot diverge within a panel. Page block settings (`PageBlockSettingsSurface`, the immersive scene inspector and the section settings popover) declare `xs`; block settings editors do not pass per-field `size`.

documents.title: Core Layout ownership gate
documents.markdown:
# Core Layout ownership gate

The gate has no migration baseline and does not expand the existing token baseline. It screens production TS, TSX and CSS under app, components, features and lib using the same source exclusions as the token policy. Tests (including `.type-test.*`), stories, fixtures, generated and vendor files are outside this production gate.

Core Layout owns `components/core/Layout/**`. Its seven public components are LayoutStack, LayoutInline, LayoutInset, LayoutSpacer, LayoutContainer, LayoutGrid and LayoutGridItem. External consumers may use the closed public variant contract, semantic native attributes and events. The scanner rejects direct visual escape props (`style`, `styles`, `className`, `classNames`, `vars`, `unstyled`, Mantine visual props) and reserved `data-geul-*` attributes on these components. Numeric grid columns and spans are structural API values; this gate does not classify them as physical spacing.

The exact strict consumer list is exported by `scripts/design-system/layout-policy.mjs`:

- `features/document-layout/ui/ContentLayoutFieldView.tsx`
- `features/admin/MapThemeEditor/MapThemeListView.tsx`
- `features/program-event/ProgramEventSeriesPublicView.tsx`
- `features/participants/ParticipantRow.tsx`
- `features/label/LabelEditor/ui/LabelParticipantsDialogView.tsx`
- `features/post/PostEditor/ui/PostParticipantsDialogView.tsx`
- `features/artist/ArtistEditor/ArtistBioEditor.tsx`
- `features/label/LabelEditor/LabelDescriptionEditor.tsx`
- `features/release/ReleaseEditor/ReleaseDescriptionEditor.tsx`

These nine files receive the additional raw Mantine layout prohibition. This scope is explicit; other files do not become approved styling exceptions. The policy recognizes aliased named imports, namespace members, the Core root barrel and simple relative or `@/` re-export chains. It checks namespace property/index access and destructuring in strict consumers.

Outside the Layout owner, CSS selectors targeting `data-geul-layout` and `data-geul-layout-*`, private `--_layout-*` definitions/references and imports of owned Layout CSS are rejected. This includes owned CSS-module imports resolved from relative paths and literal dynamic imports. Other subsystems' native `data-geul-*` markers are preserved; they are only forbidden when supplied to a public Core Layout component.

Object-literal spreads, const aliases, nested spreads and zero-argument helpers with a single object return are inspected. Bindings resolve lexically so an unrelated function's same-name constant cannot certify a spread. Literal computed keys are inspected. Unresolved dynamic spreads produce explicit CLI warnings; they are not certified safe and do not become ESLint errors. The component's closed TypeScript props and runtime safe-attribute projection must enforce those cases. Type assertions do not bypass the scanner's object inspection.

Known limits: the scanner does not typecheck variant values, resolve arbitrary runtime component aliases or destructuring of Core component namespaces, infer arbitrary computed property names, evaluate helpers with parameters or multiple returns, follow arbitrary runtime wrappers such as CSS-in-JS styled functions, inspect React.createElement calls, or prove every descendant/global CSS selector harmless. Local import-then-export barrels without a direct re-export are not resolved. Public import resolution is syntax based, not a full TypeScript symbol graph. Source parse errors fail the gate; unresolved spread analysis remains visible. These limits require the type/runtime contract and targeted source review rather than a broader exception baseline.

Map camera `fitBounds` padding and movement duration are external runtime geometry, not CSS spacing. `features/map/hooks/useMapInteractions.ts:159–170` uses padding 80 for cluster visibility and respects `instantTransitions` for both camera durations. Authored scene palettes and map geometry remain specialist data, distinct from product toolbar and control styling.

Validation: `node scripts/design-system/check-layout.mjs`; editor rule `layout-ownership/no-escape`; negative regressions in `scripts/design-system/layout-policy.test.mjs`. Both CLI and editor call the same ownership policy. The Node tests verify import aliases, spreads/helpers/shadowing, reserved attributes, CSS ownership, exact strict scope, parse failures and valid authored geometry.

documents.title: Link management composition
documents.markdown:
# Link management composition

This pattern uses existing Core contracts in the production share-link and social-link editors. It adds no tokens or Core presentation variants.

## Share links

`features/share/ui/ShareLinkSectionView.tsx` owns the section composition; `features/share/ShareLinkSection.tsx` owns expiry policy, authorization inputs, requests, clipboard actions and notifications.

The section header uses a compact IconButton with a `+` glyph and the localized new-link accessible name. Tooltip provides supplementary text. Expanded/controls relationships identify the form. Opening moves focus to the label field; closing returns focus to the trigger.

The inline creation form uses a plain SectionCard, named group, compact xs inputs and shared xs gaps. Label/password fields share a two-column LayoutGrid from `sm`, with a single column below it. Expiration and the conditional custom date use the same adaptive layout. The maximum-expiry guidance is associated with the expiration input. Cancel/create retain neutral low/medium command emphasis; this inline form does not adopt a Dialog primary-action exception.

This reduces the separate muted panel, padding and stacked field height while keeping visible labels. Core still owns control sizes, coarse-pointer targets, typography and feedback. Custom-date limits, password handling, request state and expired-link behavior remain in their existing owners.

Review `Feature/Share/ShareLinkSectionView`: Default, CreateLink, CreateLinkCustomDate, CreateLinkPending, Disabled, CreateLinkNarrowViewport and KeyboardLinkManagement. View stories model local changes; the production controller and service tests establish request behavior separately.

## Social links

`features/social-links/ui/SocialLinkInputView.tsx` owns placement. `SocialLinksEditor` and `useSocialLinksEditor` retain value normalization, ordered data, maximum count and callbacks.

At available row widths below the registered `xs` breakpoint, the selected platform appears as a Core SocialIcon in a compact IconButton. URL input receives the flexible track. The selected platform remains in the trigger and URL input accessible names. Wider rows retain the named, searchable Select.

The compact trigger opens a named Core Popover containing the existing searchable Select. It preserves option labels and selection callbacks. The full and compact wrappers switch with a container query; `display: none` removes the inactive branch from keyboard and accessibility navigation. The picker uses distinct IDs. Resize handling closes an open compact picker when its trigger is no longer visible and moves focus to the full Select.

Review `Feature/Social Links/Editor`: Desktop, Narrow, DisabledNarrow and NarrowPlatformSelection. Check search focus, nested option selection, Escape dismissal, focus return, label changes, URL editing and reorder controls. A narrow row on a desktop viewport must use the compact presentation too.

## Verification boundaries

Unit tests exercise naming, callbacks, permissions, pending/custom-date guards, nested search/dismissal and focus restoration. Browser stories verify actual container visibility and input allocation. Review mobile, tablet and desktop, light/dark/custom themes, translated labels, RTL and coarse-pointer targets. DOM tests alone do not establish geometry, contrast or assistive-technology behavior.

documents.title: Loading source inventory
documents.markdown:
# Loading source inventory

Run the read-only census from the checkout with its existing dependencies:

```sh
node scripts/design-system/loading-inventory.mjs > /private/tmp/geul-loading-inventory.json
node scripts/design-system/loading-inventory.mjs --root /path/to/checkout > /private/tmp/other-loading-inventory.json
node scripts/design-system/loading-inventory.mjs --help
node --test scripts/design-system/meaningfulmatching.test.mjs
```

The caller chooses the output artifact. The tool writes JSON to stdout and errors to stderr; it does not update inventories, documentation, configuration or source files. Importing `collectLoadingInventory({ root })` runs the same census without invoking the CLI. It uses the installed `@typescript/tooling` compiler and the existing `filesUnder`/`projectPath` helpers in [review-data.mjs](../../scripts/design-system/review-data.mjs). It does not run the existing inventory generators.

## Scope and source identity

The census enumerates every file below `app`, `features`, `components` and `lib`, including providers and contexts. It parses production `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mts`, `.mjs`, `.cts` and `.cjs` files. Missing roots appear as `present: false`. Immediate feature directories determine the domain list, so domains with no source or no candidates remain visible. The current application has 54 feature domains; the tool discovers that count rather than fixing it in code.

One exclusion function applies to scanning and import resolution. `excludedSources` records each excluded JS/TS path and its reason. Exclusions cover:

- Test, spec, type-test, story and explicit fixture filename suffixes, including `.test-fixture`, `.story-fixtures` and `-story-fixtures`.
- `test`, `tests`, `__tests__`, `testing`, `test-utils`, `spec`, `specs`, `__specs__`, `fixtures`, `__fixtures__`, `__mocks__`, `stories`, `__stories__` and `.storybook` directories.
- Declaration files and `node_modules`, `vendor`, `generated`, `gen` and `storybook-static` directories.

Production files such as route handlers, parsers and metadata helpers remain in scope even when they render no UI. CSS and assets contribute to `allFiles`/`nonSourceFiles`, but their contents are not read. The census does not read environment files, credentials or runtime environment values. It rejects symlinks through the existing review helpers.

`sourceManifest` contains every included path and its content SHA-256, sorted by path. `sourceIdentity.sourceManifestHash` hashes the UTF-8 sequence `file + NUL + sha256`, joined with newlines and no trailing newline. `enumerationHash` hashes the JSON object `{ all, domains }`, where `all` is the sorted list of every enumerated path and `domains` is the sorted feature directory list. Changes to excluded file contents do not change the production manifest. Their paths and exclusion reasons remain visible.

The identity also records the scanner hash, helper-module hash and TypeScript version. There are no timestamps, Git lookups or absolute checkout paths in the JSON. Identical inputs and tooling produce identical output. This identifies the inspected filesystem contents, including uncommitted changes, rather than a historical commit or generated inventory.

Before returning JSON, the tool repeats enumeration and checks every production file's content hash. If files changed during scanning, it fails before emitting JSON and names up to 12 changed production files. Rerun after the concurrent edits settle. This is an optimistic consistency check; it cannot provide an atomic filesystem snapshot or detect a file changed and restored between reads. Redirect stdout to a fresh temporary artifact and retain it only after exit code 0. Parse diagnostics remain explicit in `sources` and `totals`; a successful process exit does not approve incomplete syntax or loading behavior.

## Reading the JSON

| Field                               | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `totals`, `roots`, `domains`        | Included source, candidate files/nodes, lexical signal files/lines, named shared surface candidates, manual-required counts and candidate kinds. Zero-candidate domains are retained. Root totals also show all files and excluded sources. |
| `sourceManifest`, `excludedSources` | Sorted production content identity and excluded source paths/reasons.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `sources`                           | Owner directory, parser diagnostics, value-import resolution and bounded lexical signals for every production source, including zero-match files.                                                                                           |
| `candidates`                        | AST evidence with path, content hash, 1-based line/column, kind, directory owner, enclosing function, context, conditions, snippet, import target, shared surface and unresolved classification.                                            |
| `namedSharedSurfaces`               | Explicit site/Core symbol identities with matching candidate IDs. Presence or reuse does not establish correct placement or message behavior. React Suspense identity also appears on candidate rows.                                       |
| `manualClassification`              | Required review fields and an explicit `not-performed` status. No approvals or migration baseline are generated.                                                                                                                            |
| `limits`                            | Detection and validation boundaries carried with the artifact.                                                                                                                                                                              |

`id` is `file:line:column:kind`; it locates a candidate within this snapshot. It is not stable across source edits. `owner` names the source directory responsibility, not an inferred person or team assignment. Multiple candidates can describe one wait: a Suspense boundary, its fallback, a PageLoader and a loading prop can overlap. Count or group reviewed waits separately; do not report candidate counts as defect counts, migration completion or semantic coverage.

Snippets and condition/attribute excerpts are whitespace-normalized and capped at 240 characters each. Open the hash-matched source to read the complete expression. Lexical snippets can include imports, comments, metadata, native loading policies and non-UI names. Their lines are separate triage evidence and are not added to AST candidate counts. A domain with zero AST candidates can still have lexical signals that need inspection.

## Detection and resolution

| Candidate kind                         | Evidence and review boundary                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `jsx-surface`                          | JSX names containing Loader, Loading, Skeleton, Spinner, Progress, Suspense or ProcessingOverlay; native `progress`; and aliases resolving to those exported symbols or the named shared definitions. A name can describe infrastructure or data display.                                                                                              |
| `pending-prop`                         | Camel-case or separator-delimited loading, pending, fetching, processing or busy tokens, including prefixes/suffixes such as `isLoadingMore`, `savePending`, `loadingSurface`, `onLoadingStageChange` and `aria-busy`. Literal `loading="lazy"`/`"eager"` is excluded from this kind.                                                                  |
| `pending-property`                     | Object properties with the same pending tokens and JSX, callback, null, text or reference values. These expose state-model content slots and non-UI properties for manual separation.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `status-region`                        | Literal JSX `role="status"` or `role="progressbar"`. Its scope can be local feedback or measured data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `suspense-fallback`                    | A boundary's fallback expression shape, including missing, null, JSX, empty fragments, callbacks and references.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `dynamic-call`, `lazy-call`            | Resolved `next/dynamic` and React lazy imports, plus explicitly marked name-only matches. Dynamic loading options show callback return shapes, missing defaults and unresolved/spread options. Lazy identifies its enclosing Suspense responsibility rather than assigning a local fallback. Literal dynamic imports include their production targets. |
| `blank-return`                         | Explicit null, empty fragment/text/array returns, including concise arrow callbacks. Helpers remain visible as `non-render-or-unproven` unless there is render evidence.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `blank-branch`, `blank-jsx-expression` | Explicit blank conditional outcomes in render candidates, or blank JSX expressions. A blank branch alone says nothing about loading.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `pending-branch`, `pending-text`       | Render-related if/conditional/logical branches with recognized pending condition tokens or literal loading-state comparisons; literal JSX text under those conditions. Translated text and references remain in branch snippets/outcome shapes for tracing.                                                                                            |
| `jsx-spread`                           | Unresolved prop forwarding that can carry pending props or surfaces. The census records the expression without assuming its contents.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

Import resolution follows the existing inventory's `@/` and relative production-module convention. It supports source extensions, index modules, JS-extension references to TS source, named/default aliases, namespace member access, named/local/default/star/namespace barrel exports and simple top-level identifier/member aliases. Type-only imports and reexports are excluded. Cycles terminate; ambiguous, external and unresolved targets remain explicit. Compiler path aliases beyond `@/`, package internals, CommonJS, computed imports, lexical shadowing, arbitrary wrapper/data flow and runtime slot contents require manual tracing. This is an AST resolver, without type checking or source execution.

Default-export expressions follow identifier and member aliases, including `export default UI.PageLoader` and `export default (PageLoader)`. Consumers can import either as `Wait` and retain the defining path and symbol. Unsupported expressions such as calls and computed property access remain unresolved; the resolver does not infer their output from a synthetic `default` symbol.

Shared identities require both the defining production path and exported symbol. Another domain's `PageLoader` name does not become the site loader. The named set includes site `PageLoader`, Core `PageLoaderView`, `ProcessingOverlay`, `Spinner`, `Skeleton`, `Progress`, `RouteProgressBar` and `NearEndLoader`. It records reuse and does not ban or approve any of them. `importTarget.origins[].via` retains the import/barrel route to the definition.

For the map phase path, inspect `features/map/MapLibreMap.tsx` rows: its `loadingSurface` prop contains the site PageLoader, whose `message` points to `loadingMessage`. The source's import record traces `useMapLoadingState` to its hook. Continue in the hash-matched controller, hook and runtime to establish phase messages and actual transitions. An imported phase type or story does not prove that every phase occurs at runtime. The same resolution identifies the site-to-Core loader and the provider's direct Core presentation without merging their configuration responsibilities.

## Owner classification record

Use the record fields and ownership distinctions below to classify waits in the current four-root source snapshot. Reconcile owner reviews against `domains`, including domains with zero candidates, and record reviewed states and remaining gaps before claiming a whole-site review. Candidate counts alone do not establish review coverage.

Keep manual reviews in a caller-owned artifact after inspecting source and the relevant states. The following is a proposed record shape, not a committed baseline or CI taxonomy:

```ts
type LoadingReview = {
  sourceManifestHash: string;
  file: string;
  sha256: string;
  line: number;
  candidateIds: string[];
  owner: string;
  status: 'unreviewed' | 'reviewed';
  waitScope:
    | 'site-blocking'
    | 'page-blocking'
    | 'section-blocking'
    | 'command'
    | 'field'
    | 'upload-processing'
    | 'playback-buffering'
    | 'incremental'
    | 'navigation'
    | 'background'
    | 'invisible-infrastructure'
    | 'data-display'
    | 'not-loading'
    | 'unknown';
  currentSurface: string | null;
  messageSource: string | null;
  disposition: 'commonize' | 'retain' | 'intentional-invisible' | 'exclude-non-loading' | 'needs-trace';
  reason: string;
  evidence: Array<{
    kind: 'source' | 'test' | 'story' | 'browser';
    location: string;
    inspectedState: string;
    remainingGap: string | null;
  }>;
  reviewer: string;
};
```

Use `unknown`, `needs-trace` and `unreviewed` while evidence is incomplete. Record the actual region replaced or retained, message/phase source, reason and evidence scope. Group overlapping candidate IDs only when they describe the same wait. Inspect lexical-only signals too; add a source-backed review record when they identify a wait outside AST detection. Reconcile changed hashes and relocated lines before reusing a prior decision. A zero-candidate domain still needs its owner to account for lexical signals, indirect imports and detection limits. Empty domains do not imply an approved UI state.

Apply these ownership distinctions and exceptions when reviewing each wait:

- Blocking page/section waits can receive site `PageLoader` from their controller through a `loadingSurface`/state-content slot or Core `DataTable.loadingContent`. Site owns settings and localization; Core `PageLoaderView` stays pure. Pure Feature Views must respect the existing import boundaries.
- Catalogue bootstrap uses root-resolved image props because its boundary precedes `ManifestProvider`. Check generic/phase text and no-image/failed-image behavior at that owner; source identity alone does not verify it.
- Commands, field checks, uploads, processing, playback buffering, continuation loading and route progress retain their own task scope. Existing content during background/incremental requests must be considered before replacing a region.
- JSON-LD Suspense, route observers, locale synchronization and helper null results can be intentionally invisible or unrelated to loading. Member-switch freezes require their security context. Preserve access checks, terminal errors and recovery ordering when reviewing a blocking wait.
- Map precursor skeletons, delayed chunks and on-demand overlays need their own path/state review. Do not infer that using the shared map loader covers every preceding wait.

No rule in this tool requires a loader for every await, bans Spinner/Skeleton/null or approves all existing rows. Semantic enforcement can be designed after owners finish the classification and agree on the taxonomy. There is no CI gate or migration pass percentage here.

## Remaining validation

Static detection cannot establish request timing, invisible/background intent, translation output, runtime ReactNode values or waits with unrecognized names. Lexical triage helps expose gaps such as imperative DOM/CSS adapters, but it also includes false positives. Source imports and stories do not prove loading-state coverage.

Owners still need actual production-view and Storybook inspection for relevant waits, with delayed bootstrap/chunks, generic and changing phase text, missing/failed images, GIF delivery/playback, containing-region placement, themes/locales, viewport sizes, retained content, errors/retry and permissions. This tooling task performs no browser, build, server, production or visual validation.

The focused synthetic tests exercise the real collector and CLI: alias/barrel resolution, chunk fallback outcomes, pending text versus helper nulls, prefixed/suffixed props, provider/context inclusion, consistent exclusions, zero-match domains, bounded snippets and deterministic content identity. They do not pin repository counts or substitute a copy of the matching implementation.

documents.title: Common loading surface
documents.markdown:
# Common loading surface

Blocking page and section waits use the existing site `PageLoader` → Core `PageLoaderView` path.
The `/works` map reference supplies the composition: a configured image centered above compact,
localized phase text, with no card behind the message.

`PageLoader` owns manifest settings, CDN resolution and translation. It selects the first nonblank
`settings.loader_urls` entry deterministically and preserves GIF/SVG delivery with `unoptimized`.
The Core view owns image rendering, failure handling, typography and placement. It does not read
site settings or collect pending state.

## Visible text and recovery

The site controller displays `common.states.loading` when `message` is omitted, empty or whitespace.
An explicit generic message remains visible. A distinct phase replaces that generic text; changing
phases updates the existing status region. Core requires a nonblank visible `message` and rejects
blank strings. Its required `imageAlt` names the image and status independently; Core never derives
visible text from that accessible name.

Direct Core callers must now pass `message` explicitly, including default stories and tests.
The two production consumers already do: site `PageLoader` resolves the localized default or
trimmed phase message, and `CatalogueLoadingFallback` supplies the localized bootstrap message.
Site `PageLoader.message` remains optional; owners resolve visible copy before passing it to Core.

Without a configured image, the surface displays text alone. A failed image is removed while the text remains. Failure
does not rotate to another configured image. A different configured source can render afterward.
The status keeps its accessible name and implicit live announcement behavior; it does not set
`aria-busy` on itself, which would defer its own pending announcement. The requesting controller or
containing view owns busy state, request cancellation and terminal error/retry UI.

## Contrast

Core and site loaders accept `contrast="standard" | "inverse"`, defaulting to `standard`.
Standard uses the existing theme `text-muted` role. Inverse uses the full-strength, theme-invariant
`text-on-image` role for text on a dark scrim; it does not add a surface or change placement.
Core owns both colors. Callers select contrast instead of supplying styles, classes or colors.

Both the [standalone public form](../../features/form/PublicFormView.tsx) and
[embedded form block](../../features/page/blocks/form/ViewClient.tsx) explicitly select inverse on
their submission scrims through [FormSubmissionPendingState](../../features/form/FormSubmissionState.tsx).
The shared submission state defaults to standard for callers that do not request inverse.
The existing 55% black dialog overlay over the Light surface produces approximately `#706f6e`.
Full white text has 5.01:1 contrast there; the 88% white `text-inverse-primary` role would reach only
4.31:1. Light and Dark tests check both standard theme surfaces and the composed inverse overlay.
The overlay's layout, admitted fields and interaction remain owned by the form.

## Placement

Both components accept the same placement contract:

| Property    | Default   | Behavior                                                                                         |
| ----------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `placement` | `fill`    | `fill` uses absolute positioning with inset zero; `flow` reserves space in normal document flow. |
| `extent`    | `section` | Named region height owned by Core. See below.                                                    |
| `size`      | `md`      | Existing image sizes remain 48/64/80/100/120 for xs/sm/md/lg/xl.                                 |

| Extent      | Region                                                                              |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `container` | Follows a parent that already reserves height, such as a map, table or media frame. |
| `compact`   | Panel, dialog or list slot.                                                         |
| `section`   | Page section or editor entry.                                                       |
| `tall`      | Workspace whose content is known to be tall, such as a full editor or file manager. |
| `viewport`  | Standalone full-screen route.                                                       |

Numeric `height` and `minHeight` are not part of the public type; a region that needs another size
needs a reviewed extent. Fill does not itself reserve document space; the containing element must
establish the positioned region. A new section replacement uses flow without feature CSS:

```tsx
<PageLoader placement="flow" extent="compact" />
```

Placement does not disable other controls or manage focus. Regions whose geometry is already known
(list blocks, ordered credit rows, table rows) keep Core Skeleton; do not hide a skeleton under a
loader to reserve space. Rows, dialogs and fields keep Spinner or field `isLoading`.

Pure Feature Views receive a controller-supplied `loadingSurface` or existing content slot. They
must not import the site controller to resolve settings or translations. Core tables retain their
`loadingContent` slot and reserved-height container.

## Video runtime preparation

Core [MediaVideoFrame](../../components/core/MediaControls/MediaVideoFrame.tsx) accepts optional
`preparing` and `processing` flags, both defaulting to `false`. Its
[CSS](../../components/core/MediaControls/VideoControls.module.css) reserves the initial 16:9 region
only while either flag is active and no descendant `video` or `.video-js` is present to supply sizing.
The empty mount inherits that ratio. Once either media element exists, the reservation stops applying;
standard loaded-media sizing remains owned by the Video.js fluid runtime or native video. Core does
not force loaded media into 16:9.

[VideoPlayerView](../../features/media/ui/VideoPlayerView.tsx) requires `preparing`, forwards both
flags to Core and sets the mount's `aria-busy` from `preparing`. It renders `loadingSurface` only
for `preparing && !processing`; processing takes priority and renders `processingSurface` instead.
The [VideoPlayer controller](../../features/media/VideoPlayer.tsx) owns preparation identity and
completion through runtime loading and mounting, including the native fallback. It supplies site
`PageLoader` with localized loading text, `contrast="inverse"`, fill placement and `extent="container"`.
Core reserves the containing region and paints its fixed black background with the existing
`canvas-black` role, so loader contrast stays inverse in both themes.

Preparation ends at runtime/native mounting, independently of media metadata or playback buffering.
The [Video.js runtime](../../features/media/runtime/videojs-player.ts) retains loaded-media sizing
and playback behavior; processing retains its existing media status overlay.

## Catalogue bootstrap

`CatalogueLoadingFallback` supplies the localized loading message and the root-resolved image
directly to Core. It does not call a manifest hook: `ManifestProvider` is below this bootstrap
boundary. Catalogue failure still shows the localized error and retry action. Background prefetch
keeps the current page visible, and route/locale cancellation remains provider-owned.

Buttons, field validation, uploads, measured processing, playback buffering, incremental loading
and route progress retain their existing granular feedback.

## Review surfaces and checks

- `Core/Feedback/PageLoaderView`: default text, phase text, configured image, failed image, inverse overlay and flow
  region with content before and after it.
- `Feature/Site/PageLoader`: actual controller/Core path with a local manifest fixture; Controls
  expose the image URL, phase, contrast and placement.
- `Foundations/Catalogue Boundary`: actual bootstrap fallback, configured image, failed image and
  error-to-pending retry view before a manifest provider exists.
- [Video Player stories](../../features/media/VideoPlayer.stories.tsx): `RuntimePreparation`,
  `Processing` and `Playback` distinguish initial reservation from processing and loaded playback.

Stories use an existing static local image. Controls accept an observed public GIF without storing
its production URL in source. Missing-image examples intentionally request a missing local GIF.
The provider's deferred-promise tests cover completion, locale changes, cancelled requests and
retry recovery. Component tests cover visible text, image failure/source changes, deterministic
CDN/GIF handling, contrast selection and placement defaults. Browser review must still verify actual containing
regions, motion, spacing and announcements; DOM assertions do not establish visual approval.

documents.title: Mermaid theme adapter
documents.markdown:
# Mermaid theme adapter

The shared Mermaid renderer consumes Core roles through
`features/mermaid/mermaid-appearance.ts`. It always initializes Mermaid's `base`
theme, including callers without a DOM appearance. No Mermaid consumer chooses a
separate library theme or adds a local palette.

The adapter resolves concrete computed colors because an SVG image cannot inherit
the page's CSS variables. Unresolved or unsupported CSS colors fall back to the
same light/dark assignments in `@echovisionlab/design-system/tokens`. The mounted
diagram reads the computed interface font and size, and renders again when the
selected `ThemeId` or locale changes. Light to Ocean Light and Dark to Ocean Dark
also replace the SVG, even though the base scheme stays the same. Its abort signal prevents a stale render from
replacing the image from the newly selected theme.

| Diagram role                                                                                   | Core authority                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Background, nodes, notes, alternating rows, composite states, pie slices and category surfaces | `background`, `surface`, `surface-muted`                                              |
| Text, secondary axes, links, arrows and boundaries                                             | `text-primary`, `text-secondary`, `text-muted`, `border-default`, `border-strong`     |
| Chart series                                                                                   | `chart-series-primary`, `chart-series-secondary`, `chart-series-tertiary`             |
| Git branches and their filled labels                                                           | `chart-series-primary`, `chart-series-secondary`, `text-on-action`                    |
| Gantt active, completed and critical tasks                                                     | `status-accent`, `status-positive`, `status-danger` boundaries, with neutral surfaces |
| Gantt today marker and errors                                                                  | `status-danger`                                                                       |

Flowchart, sequence, class, ER, state, requirement, Gantt, pie, Git, timeline,
journey, quadrant, XY, radar, Cynefin, Wardley and event-modeling theme variables are assigned in this one adapter.
Explicit category variables prevent Mermaid from deriving unrelated hues from a
neutral base color. Category distinction uses the existing neutral chart roles;
it does not imply success, warning or danger. Pie uses neutral surfaces with
primary text. Git uses the two chart inks that support small inverse labels;
the tertiary chart ink remains available for line/bar series. Repeated categories continue to use
their authored labels and the library's geometry.

User-authored `classDef`, `style`, node styles and diagram geometry remain document
content. The renderer passes that source unchanged. Site-owned `theme`,
`themeVariables` and `themeCSS` configuration remains locked, together with the
existing security limits. This boundary applies to the standalone editor, Tiptap
node view, page block, page canvas, generated rich text and published page because
all of them consume `MermaidDiagram`.

## Accessible diagram representation

A successfully rendered diagram exposes one named image on a `div[role="img"]`. A visible
caption supplies that name through `aria-labelledby`; without a caption, the
authored accessible title supplies the name, falling back to the existing Mermaid
label. The inner SVG image keeps its pixels and intrinsic width and has an empty
alt because the enclosing image owns the complete accessible representation. The
caption is visible and does not create a second named image.

The renderer reads Mermaid's generated `accTitle` / `accDescr` title and description
metadata from the SVG document. Authored title text that differs from the visible
caption and the authored description are exposed through the image container's accessible
description. Caption-equivalent text is not repeated. No node relationships or
alternative explanation are invented. Authors must still provide an adequate
description for a complex diagram; a generic name does not convey its relationships.
The same `div` uses `role="figure"` while loading or showing an error, keeping its
status and alert descendants exposed before an image exists. Its visible caption
is a span associated by ID. A native `figure` containing `figcaption` cannot be overridden with `role="img"`;
the native host contract is checked against axe's `aria-allowed-role` rule.

This follows [Mermaid's accessibility metadata](https://mermaid.js.org/config/accessibility)
and the [WAI-ARIA named image role](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#img), with
the [ARIA in HTML host restrictions](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/#el-figure).
`Feature / Mermaid / Diagram / Accessible Description` exercises the actual renderer,
visible caption, single image name and authored description. The public/editor
comparison waits for a ready named image container and its successfully loaded SVG image before
running accessibility checks. Screen reader acceptance remains a separate review.

Storybook `Feature/Mermaid/Diagram` includes `ReadOnly`, `Sequence`,
`EntityRelationship`, `State`, `Schedule`, `Pie`, `Chart`, `Timeline` and
`AuthoredStyle`, alongside the real editor, Tiptap and page adapters. Switch the
global theme on a mounted diagram to inspect replacement of the generated SVG.
`AuthoredStyle` preserves its explicit content color in every preset while the
un-styled node and connecting line follow the site roles.

Regression coverage includes concrete-color fallback, real Mermaid base-theme
derivation, serialized renderer configuration, rendered image replacement after
a base or custom preset change, and rejection of a late render from the previous theme.

documents.title: Dialog actions
documents.markdown:
# Dialog actions

`DialogActions` owns the action-row layout for Core FormModal, ConfirmModal and
BlockingAlertDialog, and for composed ContentModal tasks. Concluding commands align
to the logical end: right in LTR and left in RTL. Buttons retain content widths;
the row wraps at narrow widths without turning the commands into full-width tiles.
The shared `action-group` spacing role owns their gap. No new token is introduced.

```tsx
<DialogActions>
  <Button emphasis="low" onClick={onCancel}>
    Cancel
  </Button>
  <Button emphasis="strong" onClick={onSave}>
    Save
  </Button>
</DialogActions>
```

Put secondary/cancel actions before the primary action in DOM order. File insertion
puts File library before Browse files when both are offered. The upload-only panel
keeps Browse files at the end. Labels, request state and callbacks remain owned by
the consumer; the row does not infer emphasis or reverse the reading order.

Use the optional `leadingActions` slot to separate a destructive or auxiliary
command from Cancel/Save, as in program-event type editing. Do not use it to put
the main command on the left. Input-plus-test rows, list pagination and per-item
commands remain separate compositions. Cookie consent keeps its own equal-choice
decision layout and does not acquire a primary/cancel hierarchy.

The public props are `children`, optional `leadingActions`, `id` and `dir`.
Alignment, gap, growth, wrapping and visual overrides are closed. The component
renders structural layout only; its buttons own names, focus, disabled state and
activation. It creates no extra tab stop or ARIA group. Modal focus containment,
dismissal and restoration still belong to OverlayDialog.

## Migration

Replace dialog footer `LayoutInline justify="end"` with `DialogActions`; remove
manual `gap`, `grow` and `wrap`. Wrap isolated concluding buttons in the same
component. Keep form submission and pending dismissal guards unchanged. Use
`leadingActions` for an existing deliberately separated destructive command.
Do not change generic LayoutInline's start-aligned default.

Actual consumers include editor file/video insertion, image cropping, map provider
selection, place creation, account dialogs, menu and legal dialogs, release relation
editors, translation provider settings and administrative edit forms. The file
library selection-status footer already has a distinct trailing action slot.

Core stories cover ordinary, phone, long-label and separated-destructive layouts.
The ordinary and phone play checks measure end alignment and content widths and
exercise keyboard order. Existing modal and consumer tests cover pending state,
submission, dismissal and file-selection behavior. Those checks do not establish
native assistive-technology acceptance or deployment.

documents.title: Navigation, Tabs, Menu, Popover and Pagination review
documents.markdown:
# Navigation, Tabs, Menu, Popover and Pagination review

Status: Draft. Reviewed against current Core APIs and actual consumers. Corrections and DOM tests below are not design approval or an application-wide accessibility pass. Colors, neutral emphasis and Feature CSS were unchanged.

## Adopted criteria

| Area                | Review criterion                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Geul application                                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Page navigation     | Ordinary site navigation uses links/disclosure. Menu roles require their keyboard contract. [APG disclosure navigation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/)                                                                               | Expanded SideNavigation uses links/disclosure; compact group popups use DropdownMenu                               |
| In-screen tabs      | Distinguish tablist name, tab/panel relations, selection, roving focus and automatic/manual activation. [Carbon Tabs](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/tabs/accessibility), [APG Tabs](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/)                   | Use NavigationLink for URL navigation; automatic activation suits consumers with immediate panel display           |
| Menu commands       | Check button name/expanded state, first-item focus, arrows, Escape and trigger restoration. [Carbon Menu buttons](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/menu-buttons/accessibility), [APG Menu button](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/) | Keep React Aria menu behavior. selected display is not a radio/checkbox-role implementation                        |
| Popup forms/content | Check dialog name, focus entry/restoration, Escape and background restrictions. [APG Dialog](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)                                                                                                                                       | Popover holds dialog/alertdialog content; DropdownMenu is a command menu                                           |
| Page numbers        | Check previous/next names, current page, disabled boundaries and keyboard interaction. [Carbon Pagination](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/pagination/accessibility)                                                                                    | Carbon page-size selection and interactive ellipsis are absent from Geul's current API; no new controls were added |

Carbon tags/appearance/approval results are not assigned to Geul. Geul uses React Aria div[role=tab] and a/div[role=menuitem]; their roles and behavior are what is verified.

## Current APIs and responsibilities

### NavigationLink, SideNavigation and MenuToggle

Owners: components/core/Navigation/NavigationLink.tsx, navigation-events.ts, NavigationIntentProvider.tsx, components/core/SideNavigation/SideNavigation.tsx and components/core/MenuToggle/MenuToggle.tsx.

- NavigationLink accepts string or Next URL-object href and supports replace/scroll/prefetch/target/rel/download/onNavigate. Defaults: appearance=content, mediaPosition=fill, separator=none, tone=primary. appearance content/quiet/block/media/row/graphic (graphic: content-sized inline-flex box around a logo or image, no underline, inherited color; used by public form and form dashboard logos and Marquee logo items); size xs/sm/md; weight regular/medium/strong; tone primary/secondary/muted/inverse/inherit.
- Only ordinary same-origin clicks pass through app NavigationIntentProvider. Canceled events, modifiers, other targets, downloads and external links retain browser navigation. No disabled link API. Callers name icon/media-only links.
- SideNavigation consumes caller ariaLabel/sections/mode/openSectionKeys/onToggleSection/onSelectItem. Consumer state controls expanded/compact mode. Active items use aria-current=page; expanded group buttons use aria-expanded/aria-controls and hidden content. showExpandedIcons defaults true.
- MenuToggle requires opened/label/onClick and renders a Core IconButton size=chrome (32px, 16px glyph, coarse pointer ≥ 44px) with aria-expanded/aria-controls and a menu/close glyph swap. It has no size prop; visibility defaults always (always/mobile-only). With controls, callers connect an existing target ID and open state. Not every toggle is a menu.

### Tabs

Owner: components/core/Tabs/Tabs.tsx.

- Root: value/defaultValue/onChange, keepMounted, orientation, activation, disabled, fill. Defaults: tone=neutral, appearance=line, keepMounted=true, orientation=horizontal, activation=automatic, disabled=false, fill=false. appearance line/outline/pills. null value maps internally to undefined; it does not guarantee empty selection.
- List: grow, wrap=wrap/nowrap, inset/paddingTop. Tab: value, disabled, leftSection/rightSection, externalPanel. Panel: value, inset/paddingTop. List/Panel inset/paddingTop default none.
- List aria-label/aria-labelledby takes precedence, otherwise Root naming is forwarded. Disabled tabs are skipped; manual mode separates arrow focus from Enter/Space activation. Inactive mounted panels use inert to restrict reading/keyboard access.
- externalPanel={id, tabId} connects an external panel; callers update its content/aria-labelledby for the active tab. Actual owners: features/admin/MapThemeEditor/MapThemeVariantTabs.tsx and ThemeEditorCanvas.tsx.
- MapThemeVariantTabs uses existing mapControls.fields.colorScheme naming (Color Scheme and its Korean translation). PageBlockSettingsSurface uses the existing section title passed from SectionItemView. Naming added no visible copy, translation keys or new props.

### DropdownMenu

Owner: components/core/DropdownMenu/DropdownMenu.tsx.

- Root defaults: size=standard, placement=bottom-start, trigger=click, portal=true, arrow=false, defaultOpened=false, closeOnItemClick=true, loop=true. size compact/standard/wide/expanded; trigger click/hover/click-hover. opened/onChange is controlled; defaultOpened initializes uncontrolled state. onOpen/onClose supported.
- Target is one ReactElement. Tooltip and Core/native triggers connect through OverlayTriggerTarget without nesting buttons. Hover adds an input path while retaining keyboard/click access.
- Item: icon/colorPreview, tone, selected, disabled, onClick, href/target/rel/download, id/title, aria-label/aria-current and data attributes. href items are anchors. String children or aria-label supplies typeahead textValue.
- Current selected means a check mark and aria-current=true. No selectionMode/selectedKeys, menuitemradio/menuitemcheckbox or aria-checked APIs. Mutually exclusive/toggle menus need a separate contract review against [APG Menu roles](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/).
- Supports Section(label), Label, Divider, Sub(size/placement), Sub.Target(children/icon/disabled), Sub.Dropdown. Sub placement defaults right-start. Sub.Target with only compound nodes has no separate aria-label/textValue API; inspect naming/typeahead in actual submenu consumers.
- Menu popup is isNonModal; open editor content is not hidden from AT. Command execution/dismissal and link navigation are separate. App guards canceling navigation do not remove existing Item onClick/dismissal behavior.

`DropdownMenu.Anchor x y` positions a programmatically opened menu (a context menu) at a viewport point.
It joins the menu trigger only as the positioning reference: hidden from assistive technology, outside the tab
order, and not a Pressable. Do not wrap an aria-hidden element in `DropdownMenu.Target` for this purpose.

### Popover

Owners: components/core/Popover/Popover.tsx and Popover.type-test.tsx.

- Root: open/defaultOpen/onOpenChange/onOpen/onClose, placement=bottom-start, size=standard, portal=true. placement bottom-start/bottom/bottom-end/top-start/top/top-end; size compact/standard/wide.
- Target is one ReactElement. Dropdown accepts padding=standard (none/compact/standard), id, aria-label/aria-labelledby/aria-describedby, role, click/mousedown and data attributes.
- role permits only dialog (default)/alertdialog. Other roles such as menu/group are rejected by types/runtime, not silently coerced. No separate modal-mode API; it uses React Aria Popover default modality.
- Consumer title/name takes precedence; otherwise trigger ID supplies naming. features/data-table/MultiFilterEditorView.tsx and MultiSortView.tsx provide explicit names. Actual form initial focus, scrolling and mobile Drawer transitions need browser verification.

### Pagination

Owners: components/core/Display/Pagination.tsx, features/data-table/DataTablePagination.tsx and features/data-table/ServerDataTable/ServerDataTablePaginationView.tsx.

- Core Pagination has two exclusive modes. Button mode requires value/total/onChange; link mode requires value/total/getHref(page) => string. Types reject onChange with getHref and reject replace/scroll/prefetch/onNavigate in button mode.
- labels: previousPage, nextPage, page(page) function; optional firstPage/lastPage add first/last controls in either mode. size defaults sm (xs/sm/md/lg/xl). nav uses explicit aria-label or current-page label.
- Both modes share the Core Button/IconButton item appearance. Button mode renders buttons. Link mode renders every reachable page and step as an anchor (Button/IconButton href, Core navigation guard and hover/focus prefetch); the current page is an anchor with aria-current=page. Boundary first/previous/next/last are native disabled buttons without href in both modes.
- Link mode: scroll defaults false (the list updates in place; consumers own scroll restoration), replace/prefetch pass through, onNavigate({ page, href, preventDefault }) runs only for ordinary same-origin primary clicks; Ctrl/Command/Shift/Alt and canceled events keep native anchor behavior.
- Pagination.tsx has no client directive: link mode renders from Server Components and only passes href/label strings to client parts. No client state is needed.
- value/total normalize to finite integers. total minimum is 1; current is 1..total; NaN/Infinity become 1. Shows first, current±2 and last; a gap larger than one page shows a decorative ellipsis. No page-size selection API.
- Server consumer: currentPage/totalPages/getPageUrl/labels, onNavigate(href), reserveSpaceWhenHidden. It composes Core link mode with first/last labels and labels.navigation as the nav name, centered in a Feature layout. totalPages<1 hides empty-data pagination; reservation leaves an existing 36px slot. Core value/total normalization now also applies to server pages. The former Feature pager used the same range (current±2 plus first/last with ellipses), so page visibility is unchanged; number items now use Core Button geometry and the Core ellipsis glyph.

## Reproductions and corrections

| Defect                                        | Reproduction                                                                           | Correction / regression evidence                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Root naming did not reach TabList             | Root name left tablist aria-label null                                                 | Naming fallback/List priority tests plus existing DocumentEditorPanels state-retention regressions                                           |
| Invalid page values                           | value=2.7 retained current=2.7; NaN lacked a current page; Infinity displayed Infinity | Finite integer/range normalization; four invalid-input cases and integer-emission checks                                                     |
| Popover role type differed from actual role   | Broad AriaRole accepted roles silently replaced by dialog                              | Closed role type, runtime rejection, alertdialog naming and rejected-type tests                                                              |
| Menu links bypassed edit-leave guard          | DropdownMenu.Item href invoked NavigationIntentProvider zero times                     | Existing NavigationLink guard connected to MenuItem onClick; canceled/allowed/modifier-click and SideNavigation expanded/compact regressions |
| Server pagination intercepted modified clicks | onNavigate adapter called preventDefault with modifiers                                | Ctrl/Command/Shift/Alt native-anchor and ordinary-click onNavigate regressions                                                               |

## Checks and remaining work

Final related run passed 10 files / 67 tests. Core type-contract checks and changed-file ESLint passed.
jsdom does not implement real cross-document navigation, producing warnings; tests check callbacks/cancellation/href, not successful new-tab/window navigation.

Later consumer-naming work passed 5 files / 20 tests covering MapThemeVariantTabs, PageBlockSettingsSurface, Core Tabs, DocumentEditorPanels and ThemeEditorCanvas. Six new naming regressions use actual Korean/English messages.
Four changed TS files passed ESLint, formatting and diff checks. Modal-path tests verify jsdom branches/DOM, not actual viewports or AT.

- Core tests: NavigationLink, SideNavigation, Tabs, DropdownMenu, Popover, MenuToggle and Display.
- Consumer tests: ServerDataTablePaginationView, DocumentEditorPanels and ThemeEditorCanvas.
- Coverage: Tabs automatic/manual/horizontal/vertical, disabled skipping, panel relations/state retention; menu arrows/Home/Escape/restoration; link guards; Pagination current/boundaries/numbers/modifiers and link-mode hrefs/disabled bounds/ellipses/server markup; Popover names/roles/dismissal.

| Remaining item                  | Owner                                                         | Required evidence                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Format-selection menu semantics | components/core/DropdownMenu and editor color/alignment menus | Decide command/current versus radio/checkbox selection, then verify keys/checked-state contract                                         |
| Compound submenu names          | components/core/DropdownMenu and Sub.Target consumers         | Names/typeahead, submenu entry/restoration, LTR/RTL                                                                                     |
| Mobile/tablet/desktop           | Relevant Core and actual Feature consumers                    | Light/Dark, Korean/long labels, wrapping/overflow, visible focus, portal overlap, touch, browser Back/modifier clicks                   |
| Actual assistive technology     | Relevant Core and actual Feature consumers                    | Names/current/expanded/selected, tab/panel movement, modal-background restriction and initial/restored focus. jsdom is not a substitute |

No UI/MCP was operated in this review. Screen/AT items remain pending. These results did not certify current code or a draft native library as Stable.

documents.title: Dialog density and scroll ownership
documents.markdown:
# Dialog density and scroll ownership

Core dialog chrome defaults to compact density. ContentModal and Drawer expose the
closed `density="compact" | "standard"` choice; density changes spacing and title type,
while `size` continues to control width or drawer height independently.

Compact header and body padding use `spacing-xs`; the title uses `font-size-sm` and
`line-height-sm`. Standard density retains `spacing-md`, `font-size-md` and
`line-height-md`. These existing roles also apply to FormModal, ConfirmModal and
BlockingAlertDialog through their shared OverlayDialog owner. Action tone, emphasis,
control geometry and dismissal behavior are unchanged.

The panel stays within its viewport budget and forms a flex column. Its dialog and
body can shrink; the header does not shrink or scroll. The body is the scrolling
owner for long content. When it overflows, it becomes a keyboard-focusable region
named by the visible dialog title, with an inset focus outline. Resize and content
observation update that state as the viewport or content changes. Short bodies and
`bodyLayout="fit"` do not acquire another tab stop. Native arrow, Page Up/Down and
Home/End keys remain available; Core does not replace them with scripted scrolling.
Features should compose their rows and status within that
body rather than add another full-height scroller. `bodyLayout="fit"` remains the
explicit ContentModal contract for media or workspace content that owns its internal
shrinking behavior. Workspace bodies keep their existing zero-padding rule.

Desktop modal insets, mobile safe-area handling, named sizes and drawer placement
presets retain their existing geometry. Compact density does not change the viewport
breakpoint or remove a touch target's minimum.

Core ContentModal and Drawer include long-content and phone stories. Their play checks
measure body overflow, body scrolling, header position and visible close controls.
Unit and keyboard tests cover density selection, pending dismissal, focus containment
and restoration. Browser runs supply the layout evidence; source and DOM checks alone
do not establish visual approval.

## Selection bubble menus

A nowrap toolbar owns a horizontal scrolling rail. A dropdown inside that rail is
clipped vertically as well. The selection bubble's More menu uses the Core document
portal so the popup escapes that clipping boundary. Core owns its viewport bounds,
scrolling and popup layer.

The editor adapter recognizes focus within a popup referenced by its trigger's
`aria-controls`. That relationship keeps the bubble valid while its portaled menu is
focused. Toolbar capture handlers leave nested menu keys to the menu; Escape closes
the menu and restores its trigger before an additional Escape can return to the
editor. Selected editor state remains available to the menu commands.

documents.title: Design ownership contract
documents.markdown:
# Design ownership contract

Core owns shared appearance, geometry and interaction state. Features compose its closed APIs and
own domain behavior. Types, runtime projection and source ownership checks enforce this boundary;
actual consumer previews verify the resulting composition.

## Ownership

| Definition                                  | Owner                                  | Consumer responsibility                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Theme roles, geometry scales, type, motion  | `@echovisionlab/design-system/tokens`  | Choose an existing semantic role; do not define another public visual authority           |
| Framework role mapping and default state    | `theme.ts` and shared runtime adapters | Consume the same theme and color-scheme contract                                          |
| Control appearance, size, density and state | Core component contract                | Supply semantic props, label, data and events                                             |
| Composition and domain behavior             | Feature/Screen                         | Arrange system parts; retain querying, commands and authorization                         |
| Third-party product controls                | Shared editor/map/media adapter        | Translate typed system roles into dependency options                                      |
| User-authored content and runtime geometry  | Domain/document renderer               | Preserve authored values and geometry; do not use the exception to restyle product chrome |

## Typed API boundary

Public Core types project the supported contract without inheriting vendor presentation props. `tone`, `emphasis`, `shape`, `size`, density, text typography and toggle state need named,
closed types. Derive supported sizes and token names from their existing authority. Keep accessibility,
form behavior, domain data and event props available.

`styles`, `vars`, `unstyled`, raw color/variant/radius, arbitrary numeric control sizes and arbitrary
font/border/background overrides must not remain general consumer APIs. If a real consumer requires
them, first determine whether an existing variant suffices or a shared variant is missing. Layout
constraints need a separate contract restricted to layout properties; preserving a general
`React.CSSProperties` style prop leaves the presentation boundary open.

Class names and stylesheet selectors also need enforcement. Closing TypeScript props alone cannot
prevent a Feature stylesheet from setting a shared button's hover color, dimensions or private CSS
variables. A layout class must not become an alternate presentation API. Dependency adapters with
genuine external-style obligations need explicit ownership records, not unrestricted exceptions.

## Minimum negative checks

| Case                                                                       | Required rejection or proof                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<Button styles={{ root: { background: ... } }}>`                          | Type error; consumer cannot replace presentation                                      |
| Raw Mantine control where Core already covers it                           | Import/ownership error, including aliases and namespace imports                       |
| Arbitrary numeric size for a Core control                                  | Type error; supported named size or a reviewed shared variant                         |
| Feature CSS setting `--button-height`, `--ai-bg`, shared hover/focus rules | CSS ownership error; fix the shared owner first                                       |
| Invalid token name or redefining a registered public role                  | Type/lint error outside the authority                                                 |
| Numeric visual props or CSS state literals outside their owner             | Ownership review or documented layout/content exception                               |
| Existing token used in an incompatible role                                | Role-specific component/adapter contract; token-name existence is insufficient        |
| Styled control hidden behind a spread/helper/callback                      | Type boundary plus resolved AST/stylesheet checks; source regex alone is insufficient |

Negative cases must be exercised alongside valid layout and specialist cases. Do not create a blanket
allowance for all inline styles, all numeric geometry, a whole editor file or every `--_` variable.
Shared adapter exceptions must name their owner and exact purpose.

## Shared state and preview proof

The shared owner defines default, hover, keyboard focus, pressed/selected, error, disabled and loading
priority. Turning off motion must preserve a static focus indication. Toggle selection must remain
visible when accent and neutral resolve to the same neutral palette. Media controls over an image
consume invariant overlay roles rather than the document action fill. These are existing-role or
shared-variant issues before they are new-token issues.

Storybook must render the actual owner and consumer composition under the same locale/theme stack.
Provide interaction cases for the changed contract, including conflicting states such as selected
plus keyboard focus, error plus focus, and pending plus dismissal. Document which production
consumers migrated; a component-only preview does not prove every page uses it.

## Completion evidence

Every design change reports the changed system definition, actual consumers, rejected escape cases,
runtime/story verification and remaining limitations. A passing token freshness/literal check alone
is insufficient.

## Shared geometry and composition

Common sizes, toolbar/action-row context, coarse-pointer minimum targets and breakpoint projections
are owned centrally. Shared CompactTiptapEditor frames and ParticipantRow consume these owners.
Responsive ownership checks reject numeric common thresholds and Feature overrides of private
control geometry; exact authored geometry exceptions stay narrow. See the
[size and density contract](size-density-contract.md).

## Layout

[Core Layout](../../components/core/Layout/index.ts) exposes closed composition APIs.

- Nine actual component exports: LayoutStack, LayoutInline, LayoutInset, LayoutSpacer, LayoutContainer,
  LayoutGrid, LayoutGridItem, LayoutVisibility and LayoutBleed. Space derives from the existing six primitive spacing keys plus
  structural `none`.
- Responsive values use the five breakpoint names registered in `@echovisionlab/design-system/tokens` and
  consumed by theme/PostCSS through `@echovisionlab/design-system/breakpoints.json`. Private Layout variables are
  assigned only by the owner, using an exhaustive static map of registered geul-spacing references.
- Public outer props select id/title/role/lang/dir/hidden/tabIndex, known native event handlers, aria
  and primitive-valued data fields. No public style/className/classNames/vars/unstyled/Box typography
  or custom component renderer exists. `as` is limited to structural HTML tags. The runtime projects
  the same allowed fields; cast/JS spreads cannot pass a visual override through to the element.
- All `data-geul-*` values are reserved and removed from consumer runtime props. Known internal Layout
  markers are explicit forbidden type keys; an index constraint also rejects identified reserved
  object assignments. TypeScript may ignore unknown dash-prefixed JSX attributes, so rejection of
  the entire reserved namespace additionally depends on the ownership lint/CI gate and runtime
  projection. Public component names alone do not bypass this limitation.
- Layout roots own min-width:0 and hidden display precedence. Inline controls named align/justify/wrap;
  Inset separates block/inline padding; Spacer is aria-hidden; Container consumes distinct named
  content-width roles. Grid supports structural column counts from 1 through 12. GridItem validates
  span plus offset against its real parent's resolved column count at every breakpoint, including
  full-span and orphan rejection.

Verification sources are [the dedicated negative type fixture](../../components/core/Layout/Layout.type-test.tsx),
[behavior tests](../../components/core/Layout/Layout.test.tsx) and
[actual interactive stories](../../components/core/Layout/Layout.stories.tsx). The dedicated compiler
project exercises valid native refs/events/aria and named responsive layout alongside forbidden
numeric/custom gap, visual overrides, reserved marker, known spread, custom renderer and invalid grid
span cases. Behavior tests cover fallback propagation, runtime projection, persistent draft/ref
identity during reflow, existing 7/5 layout, parent validation, inset axes and container/spacer behavior.
The interactive story uses production Core inputs/buttons and production message keys under the shared
locale/theme provider; its play function edits the draft and adds a real preview cell.

Compile with `pnpm design-system:typecheck`; run the Layout Vitest suite and
`pnpm storybook:typecheck`. New Layout source lint and stylesheet checks are required independently.
The [layout policy](layout-ownership-policy.md) lists consumers subject to the additional strict layout
gate and the scanner limits. Actual route coverage is tracked by the generated preview catalog.

## Input and specialist adapters

Core Input and Field expose closed size, density, value and state contracts with runtime attribute
projection and positive/negative type proof. [Input contract](input-contract.md) records their APIs
and validation. Shared toolbar and processing overlay frames own repeated editor chrome; executable
frames use Core SectionCard and LayoutInset. Authored canvas/source geometry remains local.

- SocialIcon/Glyph use named sizes from the existing font scale and reject SVG presentation overrides
  in types, runtime and ownership checks. ResizeHandle owns placement, visibility, keyboard focus and
  reduced motion; editor consumers pass interaction state through named props.
- MonacoSourceEditor owns font, density, chrome, notation colors and motion through its shared
  presentation adapter. Comments and numeric notation reuse document green; keywords, types and
  markup names reuse document blue; strings and regular expressions reuse document red. Identifiers,
  punctuation and operators use primary text. Inherited VS language-specific color rules and paired
  brackets follow the same palette. The installed Monaco matcher is checked against all four presets'
  editor, line-highlight, selection and search surfaces. The JavaScript Syntax Contrast story measures
  actual rendered tokens under the selected header theme. Its code viewport uses LTR notation under
  RTL pages while keeping localized accessible labels. Consumers can configure only the documented
  editing behavior options. These checks do not establish every grammar or assistive technology path.
  ImageCropper owns
  vendor selection, handle, overlay and focus appearance through its scoped Core adapter stylesheet.
- EditorMediaBlockFrame owns persistent selection and a separate keyboard focus boundary. External
  video consumes the frame selection outline. Editor toolbar toggle actions project
  pressed accessibility state. P5 capability controls compose SelectionRow and Checkbox without
  nesting labels, and Shader API references use Core Disclosure.
- Shader mode changes preserve an existing exact block/container selection within the same markup
  transaction; source-mode changes must not select or autofocus a neighboring Mermaid block.
  Shared selection toolbar actions preserve pointer selection at the Core button target, where React
  Aria press handling stops event propagation before a parent toolbar guard can run. Keyboard toolbar
  navigation and activation remain available.
- Release artist, label and credit connection commands consume neutral/medium Button emphasis.
  Public document table styles use the shared `data-geul-theme` contract for dark mode.
  Newly created default email HTML serializes the existing invariant paper text, ink and border roles;
  stored user-authored email content remains its own document data.
