- Product disclosures must use Core Disclosure. The ownership scanner permits native summary only
  in `app/editor-lab-local/EditorInteractionLab.tsx`, a development diagnostic owner. This narrow
  exception does not authorize native disclosure skins in product Features.
- CSS and runtime font references are checked against `lib/styles/font-assignment.css`, including
  cache invalidation. Undefined font variables cannot be hidden in the token baseline.

Negative type and runtime fixtures, ownership scanner regression tests and actual owner Storybook
states cover these boundaries. Token baseline updates may remove obsolete occurrences only.

## Token and runtime authority

The token baseline is empty. New violations fail; do not add allowances to make a change pass.
Authored palette rendering, document serialization, map identity and geometry, private variable
producers and nested Callout behavior retain their dedicated regression tests and owner stories.

- Product spacing and typography use the shared scale. Callout glyph clearance and drag gutters
  derive from the actual Core control geometry.
- Browser safe-area values remain environment inputs. Component, map, pagination and scene variables
  are private owner contracts. Persisted scene, map and document geometry remain authored data.
- Durable editor color names consume document text/background roles through `authoredEditorPalettes`.
  Generated projections cover system and explicit themes. Map provider identities retain their
  exact shared brand values; valid user colors are preserved.
- Site branding has one canonical `brand-color` fallback and a validated adapter that projects only
  that role. Document anchor clearance uses `chrome-scroll-offset` at the shared sm breakpoint.
- PostCSS light/dark mixins consume `data-geul-theme`, matching the actual provider. Their regression
  tests compile the real Core stylesheet and root/where mixins.
- Locale font assignments and site-brand projection have exact shared owners. Generated authored
  color references and runtime setters reject unknown roles; unrelated declarations remain rejected.

## User-authorized semantic action treatment

An explicit user request may authorize a scoped change to semantic color or emphasis. Keep the
implementation in the shared token/Core authority, document the affected consumers, and verify the
Light/Dark states. Feature-owned confirmation intent is implemented in `features/confirmation`;
Feature CSS cannot supply an independent button palette. See [confirmation contract](confirmation-contract.md).

Feature UI may import the exact pure presentation entry
`@/features/confirmation/ui/ConfirmationDialog`. Its intent mapping is a local static module, and
it imports only Core. The enforcement rules continue to reject the confirmation barrel, imperative
host adapter and bulk command hook from UI, and every Feature import from Core. This is an owned
presentation composition, not a general exception for cross-Feature controllers.

documents.title: Storybook page documentation
documents.markdown:
# Storybook page documentation

Open `Design System/Pages` to search routes, task groups and source files. The same
contracts appear in the Docs for mapped `Pages/*` groups. Open the existing page
stories to review production Views; documentation does not duplicate their implementations.

Documentation stays in English. The toolbar locale controls production UI and fixture
copy, while the active theme supplies the same Core tokens to documentation and examples.
Documentation neither changes those globals nor installs a separate provider.

## Ownership

| Definition                             | Owner                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Production rendering and behavior      | App route, Feature View/controller and Core                                             |
| Static route/View correspondence       | `page-preview-coverage.json`, `ui-kit-route-index.json`                                 |
| User tasks and review criteria         | `stories/design-system/pages/page-docs.ts`                                              |
| Documentation navigation and rendering | `stories/design-system/pages/PageDocumentation.tsx`                                     |
| Data, callbacks and transport fixtures | Linked `stories/pages/*.stories.tsx` files and fixture imports                          |
| Execution results                      | Evidence for the executed story, state, viewport, theme, locale, input method and scope |

The documentation consumes Core Layout, Typography, Input, Section, Disclosure and
DataTableView. `StorybookLink` preserves toolbar globals between entries. Page
documentation does not define independent colors, spacing, breakpoints or controls.

## Read a page contract

1. Inspect the route pattern, entry kind, source path, SHA and disposition.
2. Read the user task and steps to reproduce it.
3. Identify the production owner and story fixture.
4. Read local behavior and server, permission, SSR, network and persistence exclusions.
5. Open the selected branch examples and exercise the supported default, empty,
   pending, failure and recovery states.
6. Check the args of other branches and mobile examples before using them.
7. Verify keyboard interaction, focus, names, state, error relationships, content
   and responsive behavior in the browser.

One CSF file can serve several routes: Posts/Pages, Terms/Privacy or Translation's
Overview/Jobs/Settings. Its exports are not all states of the selected route. The
documentation separates focused examples from other branches and states. A `Phone`
story uses its own args and does not establish mobile coverage for another route.

## Evidence and status

| Record               | Establishes                                     | Does not establish                                        |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source mapping       | Static import/JSX and named View correspondence | Served route or all branches/states executed              |
| CSF example          | An export that reproduces a fixture             | Browser, design or accessibility approval                 |
| Review criterion     | A task and observable check                     | A completed execution                                     |
| Local fixture result | Its callback/transport implementation scope     | Service, permission, delivery, CAS or persistence success |
| Automated result     | Executed rules and scenarios                    | VoiceOver/Orca integration or complete WCAG conformance   |

When this catalog has no execution evidence, documentation says
`No result recorded in this catalog`. This is not an overall pass or failure count.
Record the actual environment, state, input method and evidence before reporting a result.

A View story does not make a route reachable when its parent layout terminates with
`notFound`. Redirect-only, development and provider entries retain their disposition
and source instead of inventing an independent page.

## Viewport and content review

| Review viewport  | Checks                                                                                                    |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mobile 390×844   | Long labels and errors, menus/toolbars, touch targets, virtual keyboard, page overflow                    |
| Tablet 834×1112  | Tabs, sidebars, column transitions, table/card density, orientations, touch/keyboard and breakpoint edges |
| Desktop 1440×900 | Maximum width, toolbar gaps, table/content scrolling, hover/focus, overlays and low heights               |

These dimensions are fixtures, not product breakpoints. Read Core Layout and inspect
immediately around actual boundaries. Switch supported locales and themes on the same
View. Check long/empty text, unbroken strings, 200% zoom and relevant input methods.
Separate intentional table/map/editor scrolling from general product UI overflow.

## Updates

Regenerate the existing inventory/coverage after route, View or story export changes.
The documentation reads that catalog directly and maintains no separate page-data snapshot.
Update `page-docs.ts` when a task or review criterion changes, then inspect its running story.
An unspecified task is a visible gap rather than an invented completion state.

documents.title: Public page motion
documents.markdown:
# Public page motion

The public Marquee and Immersive renderers own playback behavior for their page blocks.
They consume existing Core Button, Disclosure, Layout and Typography contracts.
No new theme, spacing or control tokens are introduced.

## Marquee

Owner: [MarqueeView](../../features/page/blocks/marquee/MarqueeView.tsx).
Consumers: text-marquee, client-marquee and label-marquee public views and editor previews.
Review: `Feature / Page / Motion / Marquee` (`feature-page-motion--marquee`).

- Pause is a persistent user action. Moving focus or the pointer away does not resume playback.
- Paused and reduced-motion views show every currently resolved item once in a wrapping static group.
- The moving lane stays mounted and pauses while the static group is visible; an explicit resume retains its animation position.
- Measured and repeated visual copies remain hidden from reading and inert. The static group becomes the only semantic copy while paused.
- Hover and focus stopping supplement the explicit control. They do not replace it.

The resolved items retain their authored names, selected theme logos, destinations, target policy and missing-logo policy.
This view does not retrieve omitted items or verify external destinations.

## Immersive scene

Owner: [SceneRenderer](../../features/page/blocks/immersive-scene/SceneRenderer.tsx).
Consumer: the actual public ImmersiveSceneView, plus the editor canvas and workspace previews.
Review: `feature-page-motion--immersive-autoplay` and `feature-page-motion--immersive-scroll`.

- Pause stops the owned autoplay clock, frame loop, automatic rotation and pointer repulsion.
- Resume retains elapsed playback time, the current unit and accumulated rotation; time spent paused is not replayed as a jump.
- Read all scene information opens a static list of every authored title, description and attribution, including its existing links. Opening that list also pauses playback; closing it does not resume playback.
- With reduced motion, automatic playback stays stopped, the complete information list opens by default, and public scroll scenes use their intrinsic height.
- When the complete list is open, animated overlay copies are hidden from reading and inert to avoid duplicate semantics.
- Constrained editor previews retain the same complete-information path inside Core ScrollArea, which provides a named keyboard scroll region.

Titles, Markdown descriptions and attribution remain authored content. The list does not invent a description for a mesh or texture.
The canvas remains decorative in the accessibility tree. If a 3D asset conveys information beyond the authored copy,
its author must provide an equivalent explanation in that content. The renderer cannot establish equivalence from an asset name.

## Compatibility and review

The serialized shape, public props and consumer calls remain unchanged.
Public page UI gains visible localized motion controls and a complete-information path.
The three `common.motion` messages are present in all 20 locale bundles; existing messages are preserved.
Reduced-motion views no longer depend on movement to reveal later authored information.

The light scene background default now uses the existing invariant `paper-background` token,
matching theme-derived `paper-ink` and `paper-secondary` copy. The dark default remains unchanged.
This affects new blocks and configurations that omit `backgroundColor`; an omitted value now resolves to the paper surface.
Explicitly stored background and text colors are preserved. No migration rewrites authored colors, and no new tokens are added.
The public fixtures exercise these actual defaults without background overrides.
Regression checks resolve the current CSS roles for all four theme presets, composite inverse text alpha against the default dark background,
and require at least 4.5:1 for both title and body. Authored custom colors and 3D textures require their own review.

The selected Vitest run passed 182 renderer and message checks, including GPU/CDN-adapted runtime tests for pause,
resume, pointer effects, complete authored content and reduced-motion behavior.
GPU adapters in those tests do not verify actual WebGL rendering. The public Storybook examples use the production
runtime and its existing fallback with local authored fixture content.
Review them at mobile, tablet and desktop widths, with browser motion preference, keyboard navigation, theme and locale.
Fresh browser/axe and assistive technology review remain separate from these unit results.
External map clusters, audio/video transcripts, backend destinations and asset-level visual alternatives are outside this change.

Reference: [WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide.html).

documents.title: Public post hero and reading flow
documents.markdown:
# Public post hero and reading flow

## Scope and ownership

`features/post/PostHeader/PostHeader.tsx` owns the post-specific title, featured image,
authors, location and taxonomy. `features/post/PostViewContent.tsx` composes the same
header with generated authored body blocks, series navigation and comments.
`stories/pages/PublicDocuments.stories.tsx` renders these production owners together.

The system definitions consumed by this pattern are Core `MediaImage`, `ImageChrome`,
`Heading`, `PublicMetadataRows`, `PublicMetadataValueGroup`, `UserInlineLinks`, `IconButton`
and `LayoutInset`, plus the Core heading `title` role and the document-layout `ContentLayoutView`.
No new token, feature color, type scale or control skin is introduced.

## Geometry and hierarchy

The featured image stays within the document's available inline width. This pattern does
not assume that a parent supplies padding to cancel with a negative margin. Authored
image selection, cover fit, managed-image preset and existing alternative text are retained.
The current post model supplies no separate featured-image credit or focal-point field;
this pattern does not invent or discard such metadata.

The image fills the hero's growing geometry. Its minimum height remains 232px below
`sm` and 400px at `sm` and above: these are existing media geometry choices, not new
interface spacing tokens. The title and metadata use normal flow through Core
`ImageChrome`; a separate decorative cover consumes the existing Core header shade across
the whole photo. Long titles and additional metadata can
increase the hero height instead of overflowing an absolutely positioned content layer.

One action row holds edit, Markdown export and the content language menu (`languageControl`)
with the Core `action-group` gap (8px), centered on one axis. On the hero it sits at the
`md` inset of the top trailing edge, with its space reserved in the flow; on the plain
header it is centered on the title's first line box without enlarging it. The language
menu is no longer an absolutely positioned layout control with a fixed 4.5rem reservation,
so longer locale names cannot overlap the export command.

The post title consumes the Core heading `title` role (`scale="title"`: 32px below `sm`,
40px at `sm` and above, 22pt on paper), the same title size as Page chrome and public document
details, and at least one text-scale step above an authored body `h1` at every width.
Title → metadata is 16px in both headers (`xs` gap plus the rows' own `xs` offset), the
shared public detail relationship. Plain and hero headers render the same metadata rows,
including collaborators; only the tone follows the surface. Collaborators, categories and
tags use `PublicMetadataValueGroup separator="slash"`, the same grammar as the author list.
The authors label centers with its avatar-height value.

Title and body share the Core `md` inline inset. `ContentLayoutView` owns the single `md`
gap between document chrome (plain header, hero or Page title) and the body, on screen and
paper; consumers no longer add their own block-start inset. Plain posts retain their
existing available inline width. The authored body carries its content `lang` and the
matching `dir`; series previous/next glyphs follow the interface direction.

The title shares the body's reading column at every width. The body sits in the space the table of
contents reserves (`--_table-of-contents-inset-start`/`-end` from the `ContentLayoutView` scope: 0
without an outline, the rail on the inline end below `sm`, both sides from `sm`, the column track
from `lg`) and centers the reading measure there; the hero content pads its title by the same insets
plus the centered remainder, and the plain header uses `ContentChrome measure="reading"`. Title and
first body line therefore share their start edge from 390 to 1920px, with and without an outline and
on coarse pointers (the 2026-10-13 review measured 14–22px drift at 640–767px before this).

## Use and avoid

Use the hero when a post has a featured image. Render the same header without hero
geometry when no featured image exists. Keep the actual authored body in the preview:
an isolated photograph does not show the reading transition or alignment.

Do not stretch the photo beyond the content container, repeat document padding as a
negative margin, place long metadata inside a fixed absolute cover, float controls over the
header with a fixed reservation, or change authored image meaning to make a fixture look cleaner. Product controls use Core inverse contrast
inside image chrome. Body content continues to use the selected theme's normal surface.

## Review stories and checks

- `Pages/Public/Documents / PostHero`: image, metadata, locale control and real body.
- `PostHeroLong`: long title, multiple authors and long taxonomy content.
- `PostHeroPhone` and `PostHeroTablet`: the same long content at named device viewports.
- `Post` and `PostEmpty`: plain and empty bodies remain independent states.

Hero plays measure image/container edges, title bounds, title/body inline alignment,
block spacing and absence of document-wide horizontal overflow. They wait for the real
fixture image to load. The focused source tests preserve image URL/alternative text,
author identity links, full metadata and print fragment behavior.

Review Light/Dark and custom Light/Dark presets in English, Korean and Japanese.
At mobile, tablet and desktop widths, inspect all metadata, the top actions and the first
body heading together. Check that long content increases height and the locale control
does not overlap export/edit commands. Printed output, native screen-reader reading and
service-backed export/media responses require their own execution evidence.

The local story uses a bundled poster and fixed English authored body. Locale selection
changes interface and localization metadata, not the fixture's authored translation.
Comments and Markdown responses are local fixtures. Browser checks do not establish
backend authorization, live image delivery, publication or signed-download behavior.

## Print

Paper keeps the screen composition. The hero prints as one unbroken fragment (minimum
62mm, `print-color-adjust: exact`) under the same header shade, without an extra image
filter; its inverse title keeps inverse ink because the global heading ink rule skips
`data-tone="inverse"`. Header actions, the language menu, series previous/next links,
comments and the table of contents are print-hidden; the series name and part remain.
Every theme (including dark and custom presets) prints with the light semantic roles on the
paper surface. Review with `Pages/Public/Documents / PostLongDocument` (shell, print
header), `PostHeroLong` and `PageLongDocument` under emulated print media and `page.pdf`.

## Compatibility

`PostHeader` replaces `reserveLanguageMenuSpace?: boolean` with `languageControl?: ReactNode`;
its only consumer, `PostViewContent`, passes the content language menu there instead of
`ContentLayoutView controls`. The featured-image data model is unchanged. The visual change
removes parent-dependent bleed, allows hero content to grow, aligns the action row, enlarges
the post title to the shared document title scale and moves the chrome → body gap into the
document layout. Production and Storybook consume the same updated owners.

documents.title: Accessibility release-readiness matrix
documents.markdown:
# Accessibility release-readiness matrix

Review actual pages, views and features in order. Prepare semantics and interaction while preserving the existing design and copy within each accessibility change. Actual macOS VoiceOver and Linux Orca integration remains a separate later stage.

Baseline date: 2026-10-11. Current source registers **119 pages**, **141 visual entrypoints**, **12 query editor branches** and **12 additional tab/preview/share branches**. Review **54 Core families**, **70 feature contracts**, **17 body-block kinds**, **22 page-section kinds** and **10 form-field kinds** separately. Dynamic IDs, slugs and authored data are reviewed by applicable view structure/state, not an infinite inventory of individual URLs.

Each row starts **Pending**. Existing Storybook stories are review entrypoints, not evidence of complete accessibility preparation. Detailed N/R/V/O/K/A/S/D/B states are in the [JSON matrix](./release-readiness.json); saved results use stable row IDs in the [review store](./release-readiness-reviews.json). Pending, In progress, Needs fix, Checked and Not applicable remain distinct. Accessibility and visual review are reported separately. Generation preserves saved states. Maintain the plan in [review-plan source](../../scripts/design-system/release-readiness-plan.mjs) and regenerate with [generation and missing-reference check](../../scripts/design-system/release-readiness.mjs).

## Saved verification record

These statements and row notes preserve an earlier run. They are not a fresh result for later source changes; current review evidence must identify its source and execution conditions.

- The saved full-build record inspected 230 Storybook files and 1,244 states with Chromium play/axe: 1,219 passed, 25 failed, none skipped. This does not establish complete accessibility preparation.
- The recorded failures were 8 dangling notification IDREFs, 7 target-size failures, 3 contrast failures, 6 inline-link distinction failures and 1 unnamed math-block command. SourceEditor contrast was also detected in an earlier full run and remains a recheck item.
- Six account scenarios per Korean/English locale and four actual 390×844 mobile-list cases were checked separately. Actual VoiceOver/Orca speech and full-screen pixel comparison were not run.
- Story existence, source type checks and passing axe results do not establish every page semantic, reading order, state or user scenario.

## Change boundaries

- Do not arbitrarily change visible text, button/field labels, placeholders, tooltips, dates, numbers, units, filenames, language codes or translation keys solely to add accessibility semantics.
- Do not arbitrarily change layout, order, size, spacing, density, colors, icons, emphasis or design tokens. Consume existing Core/theme contracts; separately authorized visual work is reviewed at those owners.
- Supply needed names, descriptions, groups, relationships and states at the semantic layer. Do not put everything into one long aria-label or ban aria-label entirely. Preserve visible-label wording in accessible names.
- When aria-label replaces descendant content in a role's name, check whether meaningful content becomes inaccessible. Do not add names or tabIndex to every paragraph or generic container.
- Do not add a general a11y-off option for required semantics or interaction. Decoration and context-specific optional announcements use explicit contracts.
- ARIA does not fix contrast, focus visibility, obstruction or target geometry. Record the defect and design impact at the shared owner and review visual changes in the authorized scope.
- Do not invent UI, commands or steps for review convenience. Recording creation inside the app and uploading a recording file are separate features.

## Review sequence

| Phase | Subject                                   | Work                                                                                                                                |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 00    | Scope and current-screen baseline         | Register all entrypoints, branches and features; record existing copy and visual states as the baseline.                            |
| 01    | Core and design system                    | Review shared semantics, behavior and theme contracts first, then propagate corrections to consumers.                               |
| 02    | Shared frames, authentication and account | Review global navigation, login, permissions and account screens.                                                                   |
| 03    | Authoring and editing                     | Review body content, settings, files, translations, collaboration and recovery in each actual editor page.                          |
| 04    | Public views, sharing and responses       | Review the actual output and navigation of public documents, entities, shared views and forms.                                      |
| 05    | Administration and operations             | Review administration lists, settings, analytics and provider editors.                                                              |
| 06    | Site-wide regression                      | Check theme, language, viewport, permissions, asynchronous transitions and visual preservation on each page.                        |
| 07    | Actual assistive-technology integration   | Later, check the same screens and interactions with macOS VoiceOver and Linux Orca. Track this separately from current preparation. |

Follow the page/branch order below. For each row: **identify actual controls → check name/role/relationships/value → check order/keyboard → check data/permission states and transitions → compare the screen under identical conditions → connect Storybook regressions**. A shared-component correction does not replace per-page target names, columns, permissions and transition checks.

## Gates for every row

| Gate | Area                                  | Required preparation                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| N    | Name and target                       | Identify each control's purpose and target. Supply necessary names and preserve visible label wording. Do not hide identifying information only in a description.             |
| R    | Role and relationships                | Expose roles matching actual interactions and relationships among headings, labels, descriptions, errors, groups and panels. Distinguish decoration from meaningful content.  |
| V    | Value and state                       | Values, selection, checked, expanded, read-only, disabled, required, invalid and progress states match actual data and permissions.                                           |
| O    | Reading and navigation order          | Provide meaningful document titles, landmarks, heading hierarchy and content order for structural navigation. CSS position alone does not establish reading order.            |
| K    | Keyboard and focus                    | Every offered command has a keyboard path. Focus is appropriate after entry, changes, deletion and close; editor selection is preserved.                                      |
| A    | Transitions and announcements         | Communicate progress, success, failure and empty results when needed. Avoid unnecessary focus movement, duplicate announcements and excessive progress updates.               |
| S    | State reproduction                    | Reproduce applicable data, permissions, errors and transitions with typed local inputs and outputs connected to production UI.                                                |
| D    | Visual and existing-copy preservation | Do not arbitrarily change visible copy, translation keys, placeholders, tooltips, date/number/unit/filename formatting, tokens, layout, density, colors, icons or sizes.      |
| B    | Storybook and regression              | Distinguish a rendered screen from verified semantics and interaction. Assert names, roles, states, order, focus and transitions; review axe findings and incomplete results. |

Document reading order, Tab order, the VoiceOver navigation cursor and text insertion/selection cursors are separate contracts. ARIA snapshots and DOM-focus checks are not actual screen-reader speech verification. Inspect UI and document-content languages separately.

## State and presentation combinations

| Axis         | Applicable combinations                                                                                                        |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Data         | Initial, normal, empty value/result, partial data, long values, loading, error and retry.                                      |
| Permissions  | Applicable signed-out, user, author/owner, administrator, read-only, disabled and revoked-permission combinations.             |
| Interaction  | Default, focus, selected, expanded, menu/dialog open, pending, success, failure, cancel and undo.                              |
| Presentation | light/dark, Korean and supported locales, content/mixed languages, RTL, narrow/medium/wide viewports, zoom and reduced motion. |
| Output       | Actually offered editor, preview, public, shared, print and conversion outputs.                                                |

First identify real data, permission and transition combinations, then define semantics and operation for each. Check narrow/wide layouts and light/dark on each actual View; other languages, RTL and zoom include long labels/values, hidden panels and layout boundaries. Typed local fixtures/transports reproduce server states. Provider and OS file-picker boundaries separate local UI preparation from actual integration checks.

## Feature review

Feature IDs link from page rows below. Inspect the actual fields, commands and kinds offered by each production owner. Core checks C01–C16 and shared gates also apply to each page.

### Core and design system

#### C01 Copy and visual preservation

**Copy and visual preservation** · [Owner](../../lib/styles/variables.css) · In progress

| States                                                                                                  | Checks                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| light · dark · each supported language · narrow viewport · wide viewport · before and after interaction | Compare visible copy, formatting, tokens and geometry before/after accessibility changes with identical data. Accessibility text must not leak into visible children, labels or titles. Record contrast/focus defects and review them at the shared visual owner. |

- The recorded change modified/deleted none of 76,180 existing messages across 20 UI locales and added 19 accessibility-only keys to each locale. Full-screen visual comparison (D) was not run.

#### C02 Buttons and icon commands

**Buttons and icon commands** · [Owner](../../components/core/Button) · Needs fix

| States                                                 | Checks                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| default · hover · focus · pressed · disabled · pending | Check native button/link distinction, icon names, targets of repeated commands, pressed/disabled semantics, keyboard activation and absence of nested controls. Do not append role words such as button to every name. |

- The saved RAC pending-button deletion case unmounted aria-labelledby targets retained by a live-announcement role=img, causing role-img-alt failure. Correct the upstream name lifetime; do not hide it with exclusions or by removing isPending.

#### C03 Inputs and fields

**Inputs and fields** · [Owner](../../components/core/Input) · In progress

| States                                                              | Checks                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| empty · populated · required · invalid · readonly · disabled · help | Check field names, values, required state and description/error relationships. Names must not depend only on placeholders. Check entry, editing, paste and autocomplete; do not expand visible labels solely for accessibility. |

- Field names, descriptions and errors were connected to actual inputs and contenteditable label-click focus was improved. Error, disabled and IME behavior remained under consumer review.

#### C04 Selection and value adjustment

**Selection and value adjustment** · [Owner](../../components/core/SelectionSurface) · In progress

| States                                                                          | Checks                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| unselected · single selection · multiple selection · mixed · disabled · min-max | Check the actual checkbox/radio/switch/listbox/combobox/slider pattern, group name, current value, selection and arrow/keyboard operation. Do not give a decorative grid a selection role. |

- SearchCombobox human-readable item text was connected to nine consumers. Selection/grid/Dnd/slider keyboard contracts remained under review.

#### C05 Menus and popovers

**Menus and popovers** · [Owner](../../components/core/DropdownMenu) · In progress

| States                                             | Checks                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| closed · open · submenu · selected · disabled item | Check trigger name, haspopup, expanded and relationships; arrow navigation, Escape and focus return. Distinguish menus from ordinary popovers and exclude hidden items from navigation. |

#### C06 Dialogs, drawers and confirmations

**Dialogs, drawers and confirmations** · [Owner](../../components/core/Modal) · In progress

| States                                           | Checks                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| entry · open · submit · failure · cancel · close | Check title, description, initial focus, background exclusion, focus containment/return and Escape/close paths. Do not use the entire long body as aria-describedby or announce it twice. |

#### C07 Tabs, disclosures and hierarchy

**Tabs, disclosures and hierarchy** · [Owner](../../components/core/Tabs) · In progress

| States                                                                              | Checks                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| selected · unselected · expanded · collapsed · hidden panel · responsive transition | Check tablist/tab/tabpanel and disclosure/tree names, selection, relationships and arrow operation. Exclude hidden keepMounted controls from navigation and preserve state. |

#### C08 Document structure and navigation

**Document structure and navigation** · [Owner](../../components/core/Typography) · In progress

| States                                                                | Checks                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ordinary · nested headings · long body · list · table · each viewport | Check page title, actual main/nav/aside landmarks, heading hierarchy, reading order and link purpose. Avoid excessive meaningless regions/names and exclude decorative icons. |

#### C09 Theme, contrast and focus

**Theme, contrast and focus** · [Owner](../../theme.ts) · Needs fix

| States                                                                  | Checks                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| light · dark · surface variants · selected · invalid · disabled · focus | Check token-owned text, control and focus contrast against actual composited backgrounds. States must not rely only on color. Do not conceal inconsistencies with page-specific CSS. |

- The saved 32 theme-contrast unit checks passed, while actual Display, PublicMetadata, ProcessingOverlay and SourceEditor states failed color-contrast in full rendering. Palette tests do not establish consumer contrast. Existing color/opacity/CSS was not arbitrarily changed in that run.
- Six Login states failed link-in-text-block in the saved run. Preserve copy and review link distinction at the shared design owner.

#### C10 Size, zoom and motion

**Size, zoom and motion** · [Owner](../../components/core/Layout) · Needs fix

| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| narrow viewport · wide viewport · zoom · long translation · reduced-motion | Check clipping, overlap, obstruction, scroll traps, obscured focus, targets, menu/dialog placement, motion preference and logical direction. Consume existing breakpoint/density contracts. |

- Marquee and meaningful immersive-scene pause/full-information navigation paths were incomplete in the saved record. An accessible name alone does not pass this scope. Extend shared behavior while respecting separately authorized visual scope.
- The saved Chromium/axe run reported TableOfContents link target-size failures. Existing link height was approximately 19.6px; retaining that geometry does not establish a pass.
- The saved Form Submissions run reported a DateRange Calendar trigger obscured by the following sort button. Its nominal 30×30 target exposed only approximately 23.8px width. Review width/layout rather than adding ARIA or an audit exclusion.
- The full run also reported target-size failures in TextButton Inline, three DateTimeInput states and executable controls. Include these shared size/spacing consumers alongside contents links and DateRange overlap.

#### C11 Language and existing formatting

**Language and existing formatting** · [Owner](../../lib/i18n) · In progress

| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Korean UI · supported UI languages · content-language change · mixed languages · RTL | Check lang/dir, translated accessible names, distinction between UI/content languages and existing date/number/unit/field wording. Do not copy accessibility names/descriptions into visible copy. |

#### C12 Notifications and progress

- The saved RAC pending-button deletion case unmounted aria-labelledby targets retained by a live-announcement role=img, causing role-img-alt failure. Correct the upstream name lifetime; do not hide it with exclusions or by removing isPending.
- The saved RAC Toast dismissal case similarly removed the title referenced by LiveAnnouncer. Recheck toast lifetime against the currently installed implementation before claiming this historical failure resolved.

#### C13 Tables and mobile rows

### Shared frames, authentication and account

#### G01 Public, administration and account frames

| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| signed out · signed in · admin · narrow viewport · menu collapsed | Check current location, navigation groups, body entry, header/footer structure, duplicate banner/main landmarks, drawer navigation/focus return and actual permission-dependent commands. |

#### G02 Global search and language menu

**Global search and language menu** · [Owner](../../features/post/PostSpotlight) · In progress

| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| before search · input · results · empty result · error · selection · close | Check search name, result relationship, active item, keyboard choice, Escape, result-count announcement and destination focus. Check language-menu value, selection and language names. |

#### G03 Cookies, global notifications and route loading

| first entry · consent · reset · navigation · error · recovery | Check consent controls/banner structure, route transitions and current title/body position, notification duplication/timing, and progress that obscures existing content or repeats announcements. |

## Every form-field kind

Inspect every type in [actual FIELD_TYPES](../../lib/types/form/model.ts) through builder settings, public responses, submission details and analytics. Connect actual schema required/condition/validation/option/error states; preserve current labels and number/date formatting.

| Field type    | Checks                                                                                | Accessibility / visual |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `text`        | Name, placeholder, required, pattern/length, value, errors and editing.               | In progress / Pending  |
| `email`       | Email-field name, autocomplete, format/required errors and retained value.            | In progress / Pending  |
| `textarea`    | Multiline, line breaks, length, required/errors and retained input.                   | In progress / Pending  |
| `tel`         | Country/country-code/phone relationship, country selection, format, value and errors. | In progress / Pending  |
| `number`      | Current value, min/max/step, keyboard increment/decrement, units and errors.          | In progress / Pending  |
| `date`        | Existing date format, calendar, segments, min/max, selection and errors.              | In progress / Pending  |
| `select`      | Group/field name, choices, current value, active item, open/close and errors.         | In progress / Pending  |
| `multiselect` | Multiple selection, selected chips/removal, current value, arrows and errors.         | In progress / Pending  |
| `checkbox`    | Checked state, label, required consent/validation and toggle.                         | In progress / Pending  |
| `switch`      | On/off, label, value, keyboard toggle and errors.                                     | In progress / Pending  |

## Embedded execution documents and external boundaries

[/tools/p5-runner](<../../app/(general)/tools/p5-runner/route.ts>) is an HTML route handler rather than page.tsx. E06/P05 review parent-block/execution-document semantics, focus, permissions and errors. Names alone do not complete iframe, map, external-video, code-editor, chart or executable-canvas review. Inspect actual production settings, states, alternatives and operation. OS file selection and external authentication require later app integration checks. Product purchase/download flows are outside the specified scope; service-content attachments and audio controls remain in scope.

## Conditions for completing a row

- Check every applicable N/R/V/O/K/A/S/D/B gate at both owner and actual consumer. Explain Not applicable with an actual absent product feature.
- Reproduce applicable states, including failure/retry/cancel, in Storybook and assert expected semantics, values, states, order, focus and outcomes. Do not invent UI for impossible state combinations.
- Preserve the existing copy, formatting and design under identical conditions within accessibility-only work. Track accessibility and visual review separately; unresolved screen impact keeps the row open.
- Axe alone does not complete a row. Inspect ambiguous names, relationships, keyboard paths and data alternatives in actual code/interaction.
- Keep actual VoiceOver/Orca checks separate. Prepared implementation is not completed assistive-technology verification or legal certification.

Use stable JSON matrix IDs as keys in the review store's rows. Record pending, in-progress, needs-fix, checked or not-applicable for N/R/V/O/K/A/S/D/B. Connect exceptions and fixes to actual code/work. Source or presentation-condition changes require affected checks to return to Pending. Do not add audit-only instructions or UI to production screens.

## Scope maintenance

Generate with `node scripts/design-system/release-readiness.mjs`; use `node scripts/design-system/release-readiness.mjs --check` for missing plans, invalid references and stale documents. New pages, query editor branches, Core families, body kinds, page-section kinds and field types require explicit plans. Update additionalSurfaces or feature states with new tabs, menus and conditional branches. Static analysis does not identify every arbitrary query branch. This command checks scope/documents; it does not run accessibility tests.

Read actual page source, production view/controller owners and exact existing Storybook mappings. Import overlap alone does not count as a complete page preview. Track frame, permission, network and native-environment differences per row as reproduction/integration work.

## References

- [Adobe React Aria quality, semantics and visual design](https://react-aria.adobe.com/quality) and [semantic testing](https://react-aria.adobe.com/testing)
- [W3C names and descriptions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/names-and-descriptions/) and [label in name](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/label-in-name.html)
- [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) and [WCAG2ICT guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/non-web-ict/)
- [ATAG authoring tools and generated content](https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/atag/)
- [Apple VoiceOver evaluation criteria](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-app-accessibility/voiceover-evaluation-criteria)

The web implementation target is WCAG 2.2 AA; WCAG2ICT informs desktop interpretation. Legal applicability, private audits and Section 508 delivery requirements are separate decisions. This matrix records implementation preparation across the site.

documents.title: Run and record a design-system review
documents.markdown:
# Run and record a design-system review

Use the project review tool for repeatable source, tooling and Storybook checks.
Review plans live in `design/storybook/review-plans/`; logs stay in the ignored
`.artifacts/design-system/reviews/<name>/` directory. Successful evidence is
published to `design/storybook/<name>-review.json`.

## Commands

Run from the repository root with the installed dependencies:

```sh
node scripts/design-system/review.mjs --help
node scripts/design-system/review.mjs run compact-product
node scripts/design-system/review.mjs status compact-product
node scripts/design-system/review.mjs record compact-product
```

The package alias is `pnpm design-system:review <command> <name>`.
The direct Node command is the tested primary path and also works when a local
pnpm shell wrapper cannot execute.

`run` regenerates documentation, runs the listed source tests with at most two
workers, runs native Node tooling tests, executes optional named checks, checks
generated contracts, type-checks Storybook, builds Storybook and runs the full
official Storybook test runner. Generation precedes the tested source snapshot
because generated documentation may legitimately change during generation.
The build uses installed package contracts. Unset `LOCAL_CONTRACTS`; sibling
checkout aliases are outside this review workflow. The default build sets
`UI_KIT_MINIFY=0`, as recorded in the phase environment and build identity.

The tool reuses a running preview. Its index, compiled iframe entry and built
inventory must match the current `storybook-static` build. If the preview is
unavailable or stale, start the existing server in another terminal:

```sh
node scripts/design-system/serve-kit.mjs
```

Then rerun the review. This tool does not create a server, add GUI automation or
change browser/account settings. The official runner owns its browser execution.

`status` prints phase status, log paths and actual source/tooling/story counts.
A failed or interrupted run remains inspectable. Rerunning archives the previous
working files under `history/` before using the same predictable filenames.

`record` is a separate action after reviewing manual notes and screenshots.
It only publishes `ready_for_review`; it never declares design approval,
deployment, assistive technology acceptance or live-service acceptance.

## Review plan

The filename is a lowercase name with letters, numbers and single hyphens,
starting with a letter. Traversal, absolute names and unknown plans are rejected.
All file paths are project-relative. A minimal plan has this structure:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "title": "Example owner review",
  "scope": "The changed shared owner and its actual consumers.",
  "sourceTests": ["components/core/Progress/Progress.test.tsx"],
  "toolingTests": ["scripts/design-system"],
  "checks": [
    {
      "name": "core-types",
      "command": [
        "node",
        "node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc",
        "--noEmit",
        "--project",
        "components/core/tsconfig.type-test.json"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "build": { "minify": false },
  "storybook": { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:6010" },
  "criticalPaths": ["components/core/Progress", "components/core/LoadingSurface", "docs/design-system"],
  "manualNotes": "design/storybook/review-notes/example.json",
  "screenshots": ["design/storybook/previews/example/progress.png"],
  "priorRuns": [],
  "boundaries": ["Local fixtures do not verify backend persistence or native AT."]
}
```

`sourceTests` can also name a JSON file containing a test-file array. Tests are
explicit `.test.ts`, `.test.tsx`, `.test.js` or `.test.jsx` files, without duplicates.
`toolingTests` accepts `.test.mjs` files or directories; directory entries are
expanded without shell globs. Additional checks use literal Node argument arrays,
with optional string-valued `env`. They cannot override `HOME`, `home` or
`CODEX_HOME`. Keep credentials out of tracked plans and recorded environments.
The Storybook endpoint must be a loopback HTTP origin. Checks are local project
commands, not arbitrary GUI automation.

Critical files and directories are hashed recursively. The plan, listed test
files, package/lockfile and Storybook configuration join that snapshot automatically.
Include source CSS, feature owners, source documentation and relevant adapters;
do not put the output review record or `.artifacts` in `criticalPaths`.
Manual notes must contain a nonempty `observations` array. Describe the actual
scenario, viewport/theme/locale, observed result and any timing or fixture limits.
Screenshots are hashed at recording time. Their names do not prove that a scenario
was exercised; observations must explain that evidence.

## Reports and identity

| Working file                       | Meaning                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `run.json`                         | Plan hash, phase commands/environments, times, exit results and report/log hashes              |
| `source-tests.json` / `.log`       | Affected Vitest report and process output                                                      |
| `tooling-tests.tap` / `.log`       | Actual native TAP counts and process output                                                    |
| `generate.log`, `check.log`        | Existing generation and design-system validation                                               |
| `checks/<name>.log`                | An optional plan check                                                                         |
| `storybook-types.log`, `build.log` | Type and build results                                                                         |
| `build-identity.json`              | Source/built inventories, index, compiled HTML/JS/CSS/JSON hashes and critical source snapshot |
| `storybook-tests.json` / `.log`    | Full official test-runner report and output                                                    |
| `history/`                         | Previous runs and replaced published records                                                   |

File counts come from `testResults` entries, rather than Vitest describe-suite
counters. Test counts come from actual assertions; tooling totals come from native
TAP. The browser report must cover every story in the current index, not only a
passing filtered subset. Failures, skipped/incomplete results, changed reports,
stale JSON timing, changed critical source/plan/CSS, altered build assets or
mismatched inventories prevent recording. Logs are printed by path; detailed
process output remains in its fixed file.

Build hashing excludes the copied `design-system-review/` evidence directory.
Compiled code and document inventory are identified; media and fonts require
explicit critical paths when they belong to the review scope. `priorRuns` records
and hashes earlier reports/logs without counting failed history as acceptance.
The published file includes the supplied manual notes and explicit boundaries.
Its static preview copy appears on the next Storybook build; recording does not
silently rebuild or modify the served bundle.

For owner, API and browser-review requirements, read the
[contribution process](./contribution.md). The existing release-readiness tool
produces planning matrices; the size/density browser tool is a specific regression.
This review CLI reuses validation and the official test runner instead of replacing
those owners with another UI automation system.

## Before/after screenshots for behaviour-preserving changes

`scripts/design-system/story-screenshot-compare.mjs` captures the same stories and interaction
states (hover with a real pointer entry, focus, click, key press) on two running Storybook servers,
for example a baseline snapshot of the tree and the working tree, and reports differing pixels per
case. Plans and images stay in ignored `.artifacts/` directories.

```sh
node scripts/design-system/story-screenshot-compare.mjs --plan <plan.json> --out <dir> \
  --before http://127.0.0.1:6132 --after http://127.0.0.1:6131
```

A zero-pixel result is evidence of parity only for the captured states; look at the images.

Entries can also script reading states: `{ "scroll": 1200 }` or `{ "scroll": "#heading-id" }`,
`{ "tab": 3 }`, `{ "move": [x, y] }` and `{ "drag": { "selector": "…", "from": 0.1, "to": 0.6,
"release": false, "pointer": "touch" } }` (a vertical drag across the element; `touch` dispatches real
touch points, so pointer handlers see `pointerType: "touch"`). `"touch": true` emulates a touch screen
(coarse pointer) and `"reducedMotion": "no-preference"` keeps animations. `"measure": { "title": "h1" }`
records the bounding box of each selector's first match (and the viewport) in `summary.json`, for
alignment and overflow evidence next to the images.

For print review, an entry may set `"media": "print"` (emulated print media for the screenshot)
and `"pdf": { "format": "A4" }` (Chromium's paged print path: `@page` margins, breaks and real
pagination, written next to the PNG). `--label <name>` replaces the `before` file suffix when one
running server is captured across phases. Render every page of a PDF into one contact sheet
(macOS PDFKit) to inspect margins and break placement:

```sh
node scripts/design-system/story-screenshot-compare.mjs --plan <plan.json> --out <dir> \
  --before http://127.0.0.1:6010 --label after
swift scripts/design-system/pdf-contact-sheet.swift <dir>/<name>.after.pdf <dir>/<name>.after.pages.png 4 420
```

## Spacing relationship audit

`scripts/design-system/spacing-audit.mjs` inventories and measures spacing relationships.

```sh
node scripts/design-system/spacing-audit.mjs static
node scripts/design-system/spacing-audit.mjs measure --label before --widths 1440,390 --theme light
node scripts/design-system/spacing-audit.mjs measure --label after --stories core-layout-field--state-matrix
```

`static` lists Layout props (including `Ds*` aliases) classified by the relationship their
children express, CSS spacing values, literal/`calc()` bypasses and inline style spacing.
`measure` opens stories in the running Storybook (default `http://127.0.0.1:6010`), records
vertical gaps between visible siblings (including dialog and menu portals) and label →
control → help gaps, and saves full-page screenshots. Output stays in
`.artifacts/design-system/reviews/spacing-audit/`. Text gaps are box gaps; an inline label's
glyph box reads about 1px larger than its line box. Look at the screenshots.

## Typography role audit

`scripts/design-system/typography-audit.mjs` inventories and measures type roles.

```sh
node scripts/design-system/typography-audit.mjs static
node scripts/design-system/typography-audit.mjs measure --label before --widths 390,834,1440 --themes light,dark
node scripts/design-system/typography-audit.mjs measure --label after --locales ar --stories pages-public-documents--post-heading-hierarchy
node scripts/design-system/typography-audit.mjs measure --label print --media print --themes light,dark,ocean-dark --pdf
node scripts/design-system/typography-audit.mjs measure --label before --out .artifacts/design-system/reviews/<name> --plan <stories.json>
node scripts/design-system/typography-audit.mjs compare <dir>/before/measure.json <dir>/after/measure.json
node scripts/design-system/typography-audit.mjs gaps <dir>/after/measure.json
```

`static` lists CSS `font-size`/`line-height`/`font` values (token, private, expression or
literal, print rules marked), feature CSS that sets a type size directly, Core `Text`/`Heading`/
`SupportingText` usage by prop combination (to find one role rendered at several sizes) and TS
inline/runtime font assignments. `measure` opens stories in the running Storybook, reads the
shared role sizes at the current width/media, records every visible text node's computed size,
flags sizes outside the roles (authored runtimes such as KaTeX, Monaco and maps are excluded),
reports the document hierarchy (title, body headings by authored level `data-heading-level`,
paragraph), every visible `.prose` heading (element, authored level, size, line height, box) and
the page outline (`h1` count, levels), and saves full-page screenshots. It also records the reading
measure (`reading`: width, leading and characters per full line of the first long published and
editor paragraph, spaces included, the last line excluded), the block rhythm (`blockGaps`: box gap
and kinds between consecutive blocks of every `.prose`, nested children, callout content and Tiptap
block group) and the outline clearance (`layout`: outline presentation, reading column and outline
boxes, the column's offset from the viewport center and the body/breakout → outline clearance in
the document direction). `gaps` pairs the editor and published gap above each block by block id
(blocks after an unpublished blank draft are reported as unpaired) and writes `gaps.md`. `--out` writes under another
review directory. `compare` matches two runs heading by id per story/width/media and fails when a
size, line height, weight, box or authored level differs (`compare.md` beside the second run). `--media print` emulates print at A4 width (794px); `--pdf` also writes the A4 PDF
for `pdf-contact-sheet.swift`. Output stays in `.artifacts/design-system/reviews/typography/audit/`.
Literal type sizes are enforced separately by `check-tokens.mjs` (`raw-font-size`).

documents.title: Geul design system review order
documents.markdown:
# Geul design system review order

Status: **Sequential review using Storybook documentation and running examples**.
This document defines review order and completion criteria, not completion of every Core, page or accessibility check.

Follow the [Carbon writing criteria](carbon-reference.md), [Core specifications](core-specifications.md) and
[ownership contract](ownership-contract.md). Find targets, source, stories and consumers in the
[generated inventory](generated-inventory.md). Separate supported contracts, examples and verification results;
apply changes in the relevant token/Core/consumer owner.

## 1. Buttons and commands

Owners: [Button](../../components/core/Button/Button.tsx),
[IconButton](../../components/core/IconButton/IconButton.tsx),
[TextButton](../../components/core/TextButton/TextButton.tsx),
[shared state CSS](../../components/core/Control.module.css),
[density context](../../components/core/control-context.tsx).

Compare the API, defaults, action/link, pending and naming contracts in the [Button review](button-api-review.md)
and [IconButton/TextButton review](icon-text-button-api-review.md) with documentation and actual stories.
Use the [command contract](confirmation-contract.md) for ordinary neutral/medium, supporting low and the
designated Dialog primary/confirmation strong scope.

Use relevant SemanticMatrix, MultilineLabel, Indicator, Loading, PendingTransition and LongMenuLabel/NoWrap examples
for Light/Dark, long Korean/English labels, icon/indicator, wrap and density.
Measure fine/coarse targets, SVG frame/path span, CSS padding and parent gap separately.
Verify keyboard focus, activation, duplicate blocking, pending restoration and tooltips in actual consumers.

## 2. Fields and inputs

Owners: [Field](../../components/core/Field/Field.tsx), [Field CSS](../../components/core/Field/Field.module.css),
[Input](../../components/core/Input), [Input CSS](../../components/core/Input/Input.module.css).

Compare anatomy, API, names, descriptions, errors, required, disabled/readOnly and controlled/uncontrolled behavior
in the [Field](field-api-review.md), [input](input-api-review.md) and [choice input](choice-api-review.md) contracts.
Distinguish single inputs, groups and contenteditable adapters; Field's HTML label alone does not prove a group name.
Verify inline equal columns, full-row description/error and content width in actual CSS.

Reproduce long labels/values, actions, description+error and invalid+focus.
Inspect narrow-parent wrapping/clipping, coarse 16px input text, accessory targets, label focus and ID/ARIA relationships in the browser.
Verify IME, password visibility, numeric boundaries, selection popovers and choice states through their actual input behavior.

## 3. Toolbars

Owners: [ToolbarLayout](../../components/core/Section/ToolbarLayout.tsx),
[ToolbarSurface](../../components/core/Section/ToolbarSurface.tsx),
[ToolbarCommand](../../components/core/Section/ToolbarCommand.tsx).
Follow the [Toolbar API review](toolbar-api-review.md).

Review Layout flow/actions-end/actions-inline, leading/search/filters/actions, inset/divider and container transitions.
Surface appearance/width/wrap, density and overflow has a separate contract.
For Layout check ordinary Tab order and native input keys; for Surface check Arrow/Home/End, RTL,
disabled/hidden exclusion, nested toolbars and input arrows.
Compare DOM and visual order in actual table/editor consumers.

## 4. Tables and collections

Owners: [Table](../../components/core/Display/Display.tsx),
[DataTableView](../../components/core/DataTable/DataTableView.tsx),
[DataTable CSS](../../components/core/DataTable/DataTableView.module.css).
References: [Table API review](table-api-review.md), [tables and toolbars](tables-and-toolbars.md).

Compare density, mobileLayout, columnSizing, sort, selection, rowAction, reservedRowCount and footer contracts.
Distinguish Core inline/compact/cards examples from actual Posts/FileManager/Picker choices.
Check long titles, numeric alignment, unselectable rows, empty/loading/error states, hidden columns,
modifier selection, row menus and overflow.
Review sort naming/state, select-all, independent row actions, reading order and focus recovery through interaction.

## 5. Dialogs and confirmation

Owners: [OverlayDialog](../../components/core/Modal/OverlayDialog.tsx),
[ConfirmModal](../../components/core/Modal/ConfirmModal.tsx),
[FormModal](../../components/core/Modal/FormModal.tsx),
[ConfirmationDialog](../../features/confirmation/ui/ConfirmationDialog.tsx).
Follow the [Dialog API review](dialog-api-review.md) and [confirmation contract](confirmation-contract.md).

Compare size/density, placement/workspace, bodyLayout, title/description, role and dismissible/busy.
Reproduce actual domain intent, pending, blocked, errors and cancellation.
Verify Promise waiting, duplicate submission blocking, dismissal locks, initial focus, Tab containment,
Escape and focus restoration after closing.
Review primary command access at the three viewports, low height, long content/actions, text zoom and keyboard/safe-area conditions.

## 6. Navigation, selection and actual pages

Review [navigation, overlay and pagination](navigation-overlay-pagination-api-review.md), then ApplicationFrame,
PageHeader, EditorHeader and actual Pages.
Specify which route View/states a preview reproduces in [page coverage](page-preview-coverage.md) and
[page documentation](page-documentation.md).
Review actual tasks across ready, empty, error, loading, permission, editing, saving and recovery states.

## Evidence and decisions

Each result records `Core export / source·build / story ID·args / viewport·surface width / pointer /
theme·locale / state·query / expected·observed / evidence / defect owner / unresolved scope`.
Use the current rendered examples and executable interaction checks.

| Stage                            | Required evidence                                                                      |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Contract documentation           | Correspondence between current source/tokens/API/consumers and documentation           |
| Running examples                 | Production Core/View, fixture boundaries, supported states and accepted/rejected usage |
| Automatic checks                 | Actually executed types, regressions, story play, axe and token checks with scope      |
| Browser review                   | Computed geometry, reflow, overflow, keyboard, focus and visual states                 |
| Product adoption                 | Owner change, consumer application, related regressions and page tasks                 |
| Assistive technology integration | Actual VoiceOver/Orca, OS/browser, user scenario and results                           |

Documentation, example presence and automatic passes are separate evidence. Unexecuted checks remain pending.
Do not replace actual route authentication/server/external-service verification with fixture results.
Do not mark the manual [release readiness](release-readiness.md) items automatically passed.

documents.title: Site branding and header composition
documents.markdown:
# Site branding and header composition

Core `ApplicationFrame/SiteHeader` owns the public header grid, shared insets and responsive placement.
`ShellLayout` supplies the site logo link, navigation toggle, search, language, theme and account actions.
Pages consume that shell; they do not position their own copies of header controls.
Below `sm` the menu toggle opens Core's phone navigation panel: a `nav` named by `navigationLabel` that
fills the screen below the header. The header stays in place, so the brand keeps its position and is
not repeated in the panel, and the toggle that opened it (now a close glyph) closes it. While open,
the page behind is inert and does not scroll, Escape closes it and returns focus to the toggle, and
the panel covers the consent banner while staying below popups such as its language menu.

Below the shared `sm` breakpoint, the menu toggle is visible and equal flexible tracks keep the brand
at the center of the header viewport. The theme toggle sits beside the menu toggle; search and account
occupy the opposite track. Both groups hold two controls (signed-in: two icons; anonymous: an icon and
the "Sign in" text), so the space on either side of the brand stays close to even down to 280px.
The group widths do not change the brand center, but uneven groups leave visibly uneven space at
320px, so keep `mobileLeadingActions` about as wide as `mobileActions`. The language menu is not in the
phone header: it is the last row of the navigation panel (`LanguageMenu variant="navigation"`, a
full-width row matching the panel links) and remains in the mobile footer. At `sm` and above, the
brand sits at the start beside the desktop navigation/actions. This uses the same breakpoint as Core
`MenuToggle` and the navigation panel, including narrow windows on desktop computers; widening past it
closes an open panel.

Use `SiteHeader` in the `header` slot of `ApplicationFrame kind="site"`. Pass semantic content through
`logo`, `navigationToggle`, `mobileLeadingActions`, `mobileActions` and `desktopActions`. Styling props
and arbitrary inset/width overrides are rejected. Core buttons, icon buttons, navigation links and
menus continue to own interaction geometry, focus and hover states. No new visual tokens are added.

## Logo slots

Site settings store six logo slots, each with a light and a dark variant:

| Slot                                     | Artwork                         | Used by                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `logo_full_light` / `logo_full_dark`     | Symbol with wordmark            | Public header (all widths), expanded admin navigation, forms, OG images |
| `logo_symbol_light` / `logo_symbol_dark` | Symbol only                     | Compact admin navigation rail, print watermark                          |
| `logo_email_light` / `logo_email_dark`   | PNG (SVG uploads are converted) | Email layouts (`{{logo_email_url}}`, `{{logo_email_dark_url}}`)         |

The API resolves display fallbacks once for every consumer: a missing theme uses the other theme of the
same form, then the other form. `SiteLogo form="full" | "symbol"` reads the resolved manifest pair, so
consumers never repeat the fallback. Email logos fall back across themes only. Admin settings show the
stored slots without fallbacks, each previewed on the theme background it is drawn for
(`ImagePreviewFrame surface="theme-light" | "theme-dark"`). OG images always use the full light logo and
print uses the light symbol (paper and the OG renderer are light).

`SITE_LOGO_HEIGHT` (`features/site/SiteLogo/placements.ts`) owns the image heights. The full logo is drawn
at its own size (`{ min }`) in the public header, expanded admin navigation and form pages: the site sizes it
by the `width`/`height` attributes of the uploaded SVG. Core `SiteHeader` caps the brand at the header height
less `--geul-spacing-xxs` above and below (44px on phones, 56px from `sm`); elsewhere `SiteLogoView` caps it
at `--geul-chrome-header-height-sm`. `min` is the height for a file that declares a smaller size or none:
header 28px, expanded admin navigation 36px, form pages 24px. An SVG with only a `viewBox` declares no size
and would collapse in these content-sized slots without it. In the expanded admin navigation such a file
fills the navigation width instead, up to the cap. A wide logo declared at the full header height can crowd
the phone header actions at 280px; check that width when choosing the upload size.
The symbol keeps fixed heights: compact admin rail 28px, print watermark 18px. These are proportional
image dimensions, separate from control/text sizes. `SiteLogoView` prevents image flex shrink; the admin
navigation's header remains outside its shrinking, scrollable navigation list.
In expanded admin navigation the logo and subtitle start on the navigation labels' `xs` line. The
image box is aligned, not the artwork: clear space inside an uploaded SVG's viewBox shifts the visible
mark. Upload logos whose viewBox is trimmed to the artwork so the mark itself sits on that line.

Rawsector uploads one red label for both themes: the stacked logo on its red field at 56px high as the
full logo, and the simplified symbol on a 28px red square as the symbol. The files and their vector sources
live in `/Volumes/dev/rawsector` (`logo/site/`); the source vectors are not duplicated into the product
repository. The `StackedBrand` stories use copies of those two files from `tests/fixtures/media`.

Preview the actual Views at `Pages/Application/Frames`: `StackedBrand`, `StackedBrandAdmin` and
`StackedBrandAdminCompact`. Review light/dark, 280/320/390/767/768/1280px, anonymous/authenticated,
menu open/close, keyboard focus and admin navigation expansion. Storybook mocks session/route data;
it does not prove live authentication, asset settings persistence or deployment.

## Migration

Public shell composition moves from a Feature-local row to Core `SiteHeader`. Existing `ApplicationFrame`
header slots remain compatible. Other header consumers should use this composition when they need
the same hamburger/centered-brand contract, and supply content through slots instead of CSS overrides.

documents.title: Size and density contract
documents.markdown:
# Size and density contract

Geul shares control sizes, density and responsive behavior through Core. Screens
compose the same owners for spacing, interaction targets and recurring arrangements.

## Design rules

Keep the existing 4, 8, 10, 12, 16 and 24px spacing scale. Share an owner when the
meaning is the same; a different value alone does not justify a token or variant.
Align headings, labels, values and actions before adjusting density. Preserve needed
labels and focus, selected, error, loading and disabled feedback.

This product interpretation draws on Rams's restraint and attention to detail and
norns's repeatable interaction vocabulary. References: [Rams's principles](https://www.vitsoe.com/us/about/good-design),
[norns manual](https://monome.org/docs/norns/play/).

Screens compose Field, SectionHeader, Toolbar, SelectionRow and shared Features,
then supply data, order and events. Extend the shared owner when a recurring role is
missing. Map, media and authored-content geometry belongs to its domain and does
not authorize independently styled product controls.

## Size and input mode

| Role                        | Fine pointer at the default root size    | Coarse pointer     |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
