| Standard controls           | xs, sm, md, lg, xl: 30, 36, 42, 50, 60px | At least 44px      |
| Compact commands and inputs | 28px                                     | At least 44px      |
| Chrome icon commands        | 32px                                     | At least 44px      |
| Menu rows                   | At least 26px                            | At least 44px      |
| Body links                  | Natural content line height              | Content typography |

Authority: `controlHeight` and `interaction` in `@echovisionlab/design-system/tokens`.
Button, IconButton and chrome TextButton in the same action row consume
ActionRowSizeProvider. A compact Toolbar's density takes precedence over row size;
independent controls use their named size. Font size, visible height and interaction
target remain separate roles. Arbitrary size, style and className overrides are
closed to consumers.

`any-pointer: coarse` also covers hybrid devices. Larger interaction targets occupy
real layout space; overlapping transparent hit areas are not used. Text inputs use
at least 16px type. ToolbarSurface wraps by default and provides horizontal scrolling
for explicit nowrap. Touch commands retain labels. ReorderGutter reserves the
editor's leading track for touch interaction.

Reorder grips keep their existing 28px fine / 44px coarse targets in the leading track.
Hover and pickup strengthen the glyph ink instead of painting the full target as a square.
The target remains present and stable before hover; rows do not gain padding or move on interaction.
Do not place the grip over a neighboring item or make a transparent target overlap another control.

Date and time fields are compound editable sequences. Numeric segments retain a minimum 28px
width and grow for their text; coarse input keeps 44px segment height. Field accessories keep
their 44px coarse targets. DateRange sequences use intrinsic width rather than distributing
empty space between the start, separator and end. Focus underlines the segment text in the
theme focus color; it does not paint the entire segment target. These exact dimensions and
presentation are product choices, not prescribed Adobe/W3C measurements.

Review `Core / Input / Input States / Intrinsic Date Range` and `Core / Interaction /
SortableGroups / Grip Hover Geometry`. These geometry checks do not prove complete drag
accessibility. A keyboard reorder route does not by itself satisfy the separate single-pointer
non-drag alternative in [WCAG 2.5.7](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements.html).
The current Archive, Page section/column and Form Builder consumers still require that
alternative to be connected to their existing reorder commands.

44px is the product's touch target. WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 requires 24×24 CSS px or
one of its stated exceptions; 44×44 is the AAA enhanced target. References:
[minimum target size](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html),
[enhanced target size](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-enhanced.html).

## Responsive behavior and shared compositions

CSS media and container conditions consume generated `$mantine-breakpoint-*`
variables. JavaScript and image sizes use `breakpointQuery(name, 'below' | 'at-least')`.
Below means `<`; at-least means `>=`, so the exact boundary has one owner.
LayoutContainer's compact, standard and wide content widths are separate roles of
48, 62 and 75rem. A responsive transition does not automatically change content width.

UploadPlaceholder containers, MapLibre callout scale and Mermaid figure conditions
have specific owner/query exceptions. These do not permit arbitrary numeric
breakpoints in new screens.

- CompactTiptapEditor owns the square biography/description frame, minimum writing
  area and readOnly state. Artist, Label and Release supply collaboration bindings
  and data. Read-only content remains selectable and copyable.
- Label and Post participant rows share ParticipantRow. Each domain owns permission
  and mutation behavior.
- Core Select `width="content"` calculates label/accessory width and constrains it
  to available space. Narrow layouts use full width. Features do not duplicate its CSS.
- Overlays account for viewport height and safe areas. Review content scrolling and
  primary-action access together on narrow and short viewports.

## Enforcement and review

CI and ESLint invoke the same responsive ownership policy. It rejects numeric shared
breakpoints and private control geometry redefined outside its owner. The nine
strict Layout consumers are listed in [layout policy](layout-ownership-policy.md).
The token baseline is empty and must not be expanded to admit new violations.

`Composition/SizeDensity` composes actual Core controls and participant rows.
`Feature/Editor/CompactFrame` renders the collaboration-connected editor. Both
consume Storybook's global theme and locale providers. Review 320, 390, 768 and
1280px, breakpoint boundaries, light/dark, Korean, long labels, RTL and fine/coarse
input. Check overflow, clipping, targets, row changes and focus, selected, error and
pending states.

The previous size/density verification record reports Core, app and Storybook types,
changed-file ESLint/stylelint, 164 Vitest tests in 20 files (129 component regressions
and 35 import-boundary checks), 101 policy checks and 18 browser cases. Its browser
scope includes 320, 390, 767, 768, 769 and 1280px; fine/coarse input; light/dark;
Korean, German and Arabic RTL; menus, focus, editing, read-only selection and handle
menus. It also includes 200% root text size and a 360px-high viewport. This historical
record is not a fresh result for later source changes. Physical-device keyboard and
safe-area behavior require separate checks.

With the static Storybook running, repeat the suite with
`node scripts/design-system/verify-size-density-browser.mjs`. The first argument can
select an installed Playwright module and the second the preview URL. Results and
screenshots are written to `.artifacts/design-system/size-density`. The suite covers
shared compositions and the actual Block-room controller/NodeView. It does not
establish full media-playground execution or physical-device keyboard behavior.

documents.title: Sortable rendering and performance review
documents.markdown:
# Sortable rendering and performance review

`SortableGroups` keeps the sortable shell and domain editor content separate.
The shell still receives every live transform and transition from `useSortable`.
Unchanged group/item content is memoized with stable drag bindings and item collection nodes.
Changing data, renderer callbacks, drag state or drop-target state updates the relevant content.
Child editor state and context updates remain independent of this optimization.
Pointer and keyboard sensor options also keep a stable identity across parent renders.
The pointer activation distance remains eight pixels and the existing vertical keyboard
coordinate getter is unchanged. This avoids replacing unchanged Dnd Kit activators and
listener maps when a parent updates its own state.

The production Form Builder preview updates when its schema order changes. Its
`FormStep` requests focus only for explicit Next/Previous navigation from
`FormRenderer`, including Enter in a valid text input. A passive schema update does
not move focus from the builder grip into the preview. This keeps response-form
navigation focus and editor focus under their respective owners.

## Reproduction and source evidence

The controlled source-hook regression uses two groups and twenty item views.
Before the change, four transform-only updates called group renderers eight times and
item renderers eighty times. After the change, both counts are zero while the rendered
shell transform still updates. Starting a drag updates the active item; entering an empty
destination updates that destination group. Existing reorder, cancellation, announcement,
identifier and Form Builder behavior tests run separately.
The sensor regression uses the installed Dnd Kit hooks and verifies that an unchanged
parent render preserves both descriptors and their activation/keyboard options.

These counts measure the React content path with controlled hook snapshots in jsdom.
They do not measure browser frame rate, layout cost, pointer latency or assistive technology.
The optimization leaves activation distance, pointer/keyboard sensors, collision detection,
animation timing, focus restoration and announcement behavior intact.

## Review the actual examples

- `Core / Interaction / SortableGroups / Motion Rendering` renders real Core inputs and
  displays renderer counters when **Sample render counters** is pressed. Drag horizontally
  within the first row to inspect motion without changing the item order. The play test
  checks that motion does not repeatedly render unchanged field content.
- `Feature / Form / Builder / Large Form Reorder` uses the production `FormBuilder` with
  two steps and twenty-four text fields. The play test checks keyboard step reordering
  and the same connected handle's focus after Dnd Kit's deferred focus restoration.
  Expand steps/fields to inspect production editor responsiveness.
- Existing keyboard reorder and cancel examples continue to test semantic behavior.

Renderer counters record executions, including any extra development/Strict Mode renders.
Activation, drop-target changes and dropping can update active content even without an
order change. Sampling also updates the diagnostic fixture's parent state; compare samples
as a complete interaction, rather than treating their delta as transform-only work.
React Profiler duration and commit counts are meaningful only in a profiling-enabled build;
an ordinary production build may report zero profiling commits. Capture actual browser
timings with the build mode, device, viewport, item count and expansion state before making
a frame-rate or latency claim. Read the [React Profiler reference](https://react.dev/reference/react/Profiler).

## Consumer responsibilities and accessibility boundary

Keep renderer functions and unchanged source objects stable when practical. Source edits,
locale changes and changed callback behavior must still reach the visible editor; memoization
does not permit mutating item/group objects in place or ignoring a changed callback.

Drag and keyboard reorder currently exist in the reviewed Form Builder/SortableGroups path.
A single-pointer non-drag movement alternative remains a separate known gap. Keyboard
equivalence alone does not establish [WCAG 2.5.7](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements.html)
conformance. This rendering change does not add or remove movement commands.

## Single-list item wiring: `useSortableItem`

Feature lists that own their own `DndContext` (release tracks/credits/artists/labels, work
clients/credits, menu items, page sections, marquee items, validators, poster tiles) bind each
entry through `useSortableItem({ id, data?, disabled? })` from `@/components/core/Sortable`.
Features do not import `useSortable` or `CSS` from Dnd Kit for item wiring.

| Returned field | Consumer                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `setNodeRef`   | the moving Core surface (`SortableSurface` `ref` or `Table.Tr` `ref`)                                                                                |
| `motion`       | `SortableSurface` `motion`                                                                                                                           |
| `dragState`    | `Table.Tr` `dragState` (translate-only string; the sensor scale is never applied)                                                                    |
| `isDragging`   | domain state such as `SectionCard` `state="dragging"`                                                                                                |
| `handle`       | spread onto the leading `IconButton interaction="drag-handle"`: activator `ref`, Dnd Kit attributes and listeners, filtered by `interactionBindings` |

Spread `handle` before the handle's own `aria-label`. To add a description, merge
`handle['aria-describedby']` with the feature's id so Dnd Kit's instructions remain referenced.
Each returned object keeps its identity until its own inputs change, so memoized rows may
depend on `handle` without re-rendering for unrelated motion. The hook does not choose sensors,
collision detection or sorting strategy; those remain on the list's `DndContext`/`SortableContext`
with the same eight-pixel pointer activation. `Core / Interaction / ReorderRow / Sortable Item Hook`
shows the complete wiring.

documents.title: Spacing and icon contract
documents.markdown:
# Spacing and icon contract Authority: `@echovisionlab/design-system/tokens`. Dimensions below assume a 16px root. Carbon's [Button specification](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/button/specifications) provides an 8px ghost label–icon comparison. Its larger filled-button spacing is not applied to every Geul command. | Role | Value | Owner | | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | control-label | 8px → spacing-xs | Label, icon and indicator inside a control | | control-label-compact | 4px → spacing-xxs | Control under compact HeaderDensity | | action-group | 8px → spacing-xs | ToolbarLayout, SectionHeader, table command groups and outer media groups | | toolbar-item | 4px → spacing-xxs | Comfortable ToolbarSurface and media command clusters | | field-label | 4px → spacing-xxs | Stacked label → control → help rows in Core Field and every Core Input | | field-column | 10px → spacing-sm | Two columns in an inline Field | | section | 24px → spacing-xl | Independent sections in an outer composition | `spacingRole` aliases foundations rather than copying values. `derivedTokenRoles` checks the same projection in TypeScript and CSS. Layout `gap="action-group"` and `gap="section"` expose outer relationships. `control-label` is not a Layout option; Features cannot alter control internals. Existing `xxs/xs/sm/md/lg/xl` values remain 4/8/10/12/16/24px and do not scale automatically with viewport width. `control-label-compact` applies under `HeaderDensityProvider density="compact"`. Button `size="compact"` and compact ToolbarDensity retain the default 8px `control-label` gap. Inspect the 8px compact Button gap and 4px compact HeaderDensity gap separately in Storybook. Core `controlPadding` aliases own inline padding: compact 4px, xs 10px, standard 12px and large 16px. IconButton padding is 0. Compact/inline ToolbarSurface's zero gap and inset are explicit density exceptions. Field description/error rows span both columns. Table command groups consume `action-group` and wrap when their toolbar narrows. They previously chose `xxs` independently; the shared external command relationship now resolves to 8px at a 16px root. Compact media command clusters keep 4px through `toolbar-item`, while the media clock's content separators retain `xxs`. This keeps command relationships explicit without changing every 4px gap into a toolbar role. The [token migration record](token-contract.md#2026-10-12-consolidation-and-migration) explains the removed unused media roles and the contracts kept separate. ## Composition relationships Reviewed 2026-10-13 with `node scripts/design-system/spacing-audit.mjs static|measure` (results in `.artifacts/design-system/reviews/spacing-audit/`). One module, one value per relationship. Text gaps are measured between line boxes; an inline label's glyph box reads about 1px larger than its line box. | Relationship | Value | Owner / how to express it | | ---------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | | label → control → help/error | 4px | `field-label`; Core Field and Input. Features do not rebuild it | | label → description (above the control) | 0 | One text block inside Field's header | | field → field | 12px (`md`) | LayoutStack/LayoutGrid default `md` | | SectionHeader → its content | 12px (`md`) | LayoutStack `gap="md"` | | subsection → subsection inside one card | 16px (`lg`) | LayoutStack `gap="lg"` | | section → section | 24px | `section` (`xl`) | | dialog body → DialogActions | 12px (`md`) | Confirm/Form/BlockingAlert dialogs; body copy carries no own margin | | public detail title → PublicMetadataRows | 16px | Parent `gap="xs"` + the rows' own 8px block-start margin | | commands in a group / toolbar items | 8px / 4px | `action-group` / `toolbar-item` | Changes from this review: - `field-label` moved from 8px to 4px. Core Input already used 4px between label, control and help; Core Field used 8px plus a 24.8px label line box (inherited 16px/1.55), so Field labels sat about 7px further from their controls than Input labels in the same form. With 12px between fields, a 4px label gap keeps every label closer to its own control than to the previous field's line. Field's label row now uses `font-size-sm`/`line-height-sm`. - ConfirmModal rendered its message in a bare `

`, adding the 16px UA margin above and below (body → actions measured 28px against FormModal's 12px). It now uses Core `Text`. - SectionHeader → content used `sm` (10px) in account settings and admin sign-in sections and `xxs` (4px) in the Page/Post editor Options block, against `md` (12px) everywhere else. - Public detail title → metadata measured 20px (artist, label), 18px (release) and 16px (work, event); all five now resolve to 16px. - Site asset uploads rebuilt a field with insets (label → description 4px, description → dropzone 8px); they now follow Field's label/description block and 4px control gap. - `inset` literals in Tiptap node error overlays, the MapLibre attribution offset and the OG preview loading badge use spacing tokens. SelectionSurface derives its 26px action offset from the selection mark size plus `xxs`. Enforcement: the token scanner (CLI and ESLint `design-tokens` rule) now treats `inset` and `inset-*` like padding/margin, and rejects literal numbers or dimensions in JSX `style={{ gap | padding* | margin* | inset* }}`. `em` offsets on positioned text markers follow glyph metrics and stay allowed. The only geometry exception is the immersive scene's viewport-scaled presentation (`authoredGeometryFiles` in `token-policy.mjs`). Physical `top/left/right/bottom` hairline geometry (table resize handles, editor page decorations) is not part of the spacing scale and remains a review item. ## Glyph and interaction target Core displays Tabler's original 24×24 viewBox in a 16×16 glyph box. Preserve source paths, proportions and optical centers; a glyph need not fill the entire box. Exclude Tabler's empty background path when measuring drawn geometry. Measure the SVG frame, visible paths, CSS padding, control box and parent gap separately. Visual clearance alone does not justify cropping paths. The named size or row density determines IconButton's fine-pointer target: compact drag 28px, ordinary xs 30px and chrome 32px. Coarse-pointer targets occupy at least 44px of real layout space without scaling glyphs or overlapping transparent targets. A Button's label–icon gap is separate from an IconButton's target clearance. [IBM icon usage](https://www.ibm.com/design/language/iconography/ui-icons/usage/) also distinguishes live area from touch clearance. The shared roles and owners define the spacing contract. Enlarge or optically adjust a glyph only with measurements and actual consumer evidence at the common owner. Record Storybook wrapper spacing separately from product padding/gaps, together with the actual CSS viewport and control box. ## Original glyph live-area comparison Reviewed 2026-10-12. Geul Core uses installed `@tabler/icons-react` **3.49.0**. Actual consumers include [IconButton](../../components/core/IconButton/IconButton.stories.tsx) OpticalGlyphComparison and [MediaTransport](../../components/core/MediaControls/MediaTransport.tsx). The installed outline defaults are viewBox 24×24, fill none, stroke width 2 and round line caps/joins. The following values are **source calculations** at a 16×16 CSS px display size, not browser-painted bounds, CSS stroke measurements or raster ink area. | Action | Tabler path bbox at 16px | Calculated stroke envelope | Carbon filled-path bbox at 16px | | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | close | IconX: x/y 6..18 → 8×8px | 9.33×9.33px | Close16: viewBox32, x/y 8..24 → **8×8px** | | menu | IconMenu2: x4..20, y6..18 → 10.67×8px | 12×9.33px | Menu16: viewBox16, x2..14, y3..13 → **12×10px**; four lines, versus Tabler's three | | plus | IconPlus: x/y 5..19 → 9.33×9.33px | 10.67×10.67px | Add16: viewBox32, x/y 8..24 → **8×8px** | | chevron down | IconChevronDown: x6..18, y9..15 → 8×4px | 9.33×5.33px | ChevronDown16: viewBox16, x3..13, y5.3..11 → **10×5.7px** | | grip | IconGripVertical: x8..16, y4..20 → 5.33×10.67px | 6.67×12px | Draggable16: viewBox32, x10..22, y6..26 → **6×10px**; Tabler uses circles, Carbon squares | | search | IconSearch: x/y 3..21 → 12×12px | 13.33×13.33px | Search16 uses a curved filled path; exact painted bounds still require path measurement | The Tabler envelope assumes original stroke width 2 and round caps/joins. For close, adding stroke 2 to the 12-unit axis span gives `14 × 16/24 = 9.33px`. Different computed stroke, transforms or vector-effect invalidate that assumption. Bounding-box occupancy measures rectangular live-area extent, not ink area or visual weight. In a 16px box, Tabler close's path occupies 50% of each axis; the calculated stroke envelope occupies 58.3%. Carbon's default Close16 also occupies 50%. The sources do not establish a rule that Carbon's ordinary close fills 12px. CloseLarge16 is a different 10×10px glyph; CloseFilled16 includes a 14×14px circular background. A background-inclusive glyph is not a scaling reference for an ordinary X. Menu width is 12px in both the Tabler stroke calculation and Carbon, while line count, height and stroke differ. Tabler plus is larger than Carbon Add under these assumptions. Uniform cropping/scaling changes these differences and source centers and requires consumer-specific evidence. ### Versions and official sources The reviewed Carbon distribution is `@carbon/icons` **11.90.0**. Close16, Add16 and Draggable16 have 16px width/height while retaining **viewBox 0 0 32 32**. Do not infer a separate same-named source SVG in a 16px directory. Menu16, ChevronDown16 and Search16 have their own viewBox16 sources. - Tabler official distribution **3.49.0**: [default attributes](https://unpkg.com/@tabler/icons-react@3.49.0/dist/esm/defaultAttributes.mjs), [stroke default](https://unpkg.com/@tabler/icons-react@3.49.0/dist/esm/createReactComponent.mjs), [IconX](https://unpkg.com/@tabler/icons-react@3.49.0/dist/esm/icons/IconX.mjs), [IconMenu2](https://unpkg.com/@tabler/icons-react@3.49.0/dist/esm/icons/IconMenu2.mjs), [IconPlus](https://unpkg.com/@tabler/icons-react@3.49.0/dist/esm/icons/IconPlus.mjs). - official distribution: [Close16](https://unpkg.com/@carbon/icons@11.90.0/es/close/16.js), [Add16](https://unpkg.com/@carbon/icons@11.90.0/es/add/16.js), [Menu16](https://unpkg.com/@carbon/icons@11.90.0/es/menu/16.js), [ChevronDown16](https://unpkg.com/@carbon/icons@11.90.0/es/chevron--down/16.js), [Draggable16](https://unpkg.com/@carbon/icons@11.90.0/es/draggable/16.js), [Search16](https://unpkg.com/@carbon/icons@11.90.0/es/search/16.js). - official repository source, commit `47ab67155b185d56bf147b33cd9536e479ab0203`: [Close32](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/blob/47ab67155b185d56bf147b33cd9536e479ab0203/packages/icons/src/svg/32/close.svg), [Add32](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/blob/47ab67155b185d56bf147b33cd9536e479ab0203/packages/icons/src/svg/32/add.svg), [Menu16](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/blob/47ab67155b185d56bf147b33cd9536e479ab0203/packages/icons/src/svg/16/menu.svg). - distinct glyph: [CloseLarge16](https://unpkg.com/@carbon/icons@11.90.0/es/close--large/16.js), [CloseFilled16](https://unpkg.com/@carbon/icons@11.90.0/svg/16/close--filled.svg). ### Remaining browser measurements For close/menu/plus, record the SVG frame, visible paths, button target, CSS padding and parent gap in the same consumer view. The current read-only measurement scope uses SVG/path `getBoundingClientRect()` alongside viewBox, display size, computed stroke/cap and transform. A path rectangle is not assumed to include painted stroke. Exclude transparent background/artboard rectangles. `getBBox()` was not available in that read-only scope and is not recorded as executed evidence. For example, the 4px clearance on either side of an 8px glyph span inside a 16px SVG is separate from button padding. Identify whether excess space comes from the SVG, control target or parent layout, then review the relevant shared owner. This source calculation table does not establish completed optical correction or design approval.

documents.title: Storybook toolbar contract
documents.markdown:
# Storybook toolbar contract

The global decorator in `.storybook/preview.tsx` owns the selected locale, message catalog, document language/direction and `ThemeId`. Its shared `DesignSystemProvider` applies Light, Dark, Ocean Light or Ocean Dark to the document and portaled UI through the same semantic roles used by the application. Stories read language with `useLocale()` and `useTranslations()`, and theme context with `useColorScheme()`. Date/time fixtures pass the selected locale to formatting and calendar components. Presets override existing roles; they do not add component token families or persist application preferences.

`node scripts/design-system/check-story-globals.mjs` runs within `design-system:check` and `design-system:generate`. It scans every CSF story under components, features and stories, plus TypeScript/JavaScript helpers under stories and .storybook. Tests, fixture directories, generated builds and the main/manager/global preview entrypoints are excluded.

The guard rejects:

- Story `globals.locale` and `globals.theme`, including local aliases, computed string keys and object spreads. Viewport globals remain valid.
- Fixed string locale args and JSX locale props, including inspectable local aliases and spread props.
- Local provider wrappers, including `DesignSystemProvider`, `AppDesignSystemProvider`, `LegacyThemeBridge`, `I18nProvider`, `RouterProvider`, `MantineProvider`, `NextIntlClientProvider` and `LocaleProvider`. Aliased imports and implicit defaults also shadow the shared decorators.
- Invalid source syntax and uninspectable or cyclic story globals.

User-authored content, artwork, brand identities and translation metadata such as `requestedLocale` remain valid fixture data. The guard does not ban invariant imagery colors. It does not infer whether arbitrary text is an interface label, follow imported helper implementations outside stories, evaluate dynamic JavaScript expressions, or prove visual contrast. Translation and interaction tests plus browser checks complement this static invariant.

Run `node --test scripts/design-system/check-story-globals.test.mjs` for the guard regressions. Keep locale and theme selections in the toolbar; additional component states belong in args and viewport variants.

## Docs string control names

The installed Storybook Docs 10.5.8 `TextControl` did not name its textarea by the
property key. With a length limit, its wrapping label instead supplied the count;
without a limit, the accessible name was empty. Undefined values also exposed the
same “Set string” name for every property.

`patches/@storybook__addon-docs@10.5.8.patch` names the textarea with its property key
and the setter “Set string for {key}”. It retains the visible setter wording, original
IDs, callbacks, length limits, required state, read-only behavior and autofocus.
The correction changes only those two TextControl branches. pnpm's patch entry and
lockfile make it reproducible after installation. Recheck the patch when upgrading
Storybook and remove it when upstream supplies equivalent names.

`.storybook/TextControl.accessibility.test.tsx` mounts the installed public
`TextControl` and `PureArgsTable` exports. It checks distinct names, edits and setter
transitions, read-only activation, IDs and scoped axe form-label rules. The direct
accessible-name assertions matter because axe's label rule accepts the original
placeholder even when it does not identify the property.

documents.title: DataTable API and state review
documents.markdown:
# DataTable API and state review

2026-10-12. Draft code and DOM-event contract review, not design approval or an application-wide accessibility pass.
Existing Geul colors, density and mobile presentations remain. Changes concern click boundaries, sort semantics and keyboard access below.

## Carbon criteria and Geul decisions

| Criterion                                                                            | Geul application / retained behavior                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Collection-wide actions belong to toolbar; individual actions belong to row controls | Distinguish Core DataTableToolbar/DataTableSelectionToolbar from kind='action' cells. Cell controls must not duplicate row activation       |
| Header selection is checked/unchecked/indeterminate; rows are checked/unchecked      | Header state uses selectable current-page rows, not selection across all data                                                               |
| Sort buttons and cell controls have normal keyboard behavior and names               | Retain native button/link/checkbox. One primary sort header carries aria-sort; hidden descriptions provide secondary order/direction        |
| Row menus remain discoverable on touch                                               | Preserve mobile action cells; no new hover-only menus                                                                                       |
| Carbon's 24/32/40/48/64px row scale and skeleton are Carbon choices                  | Preserve Geul's three padding-based densities and PageLoader. Carbon values and reserved-height estimates are not measured Geul row heights |

Sources: [Carbon Data table guidelines](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/data-table/guidelines),
[Carbon Data table accessibility](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/data-table/accessibility).
[WAI-ARIA 1.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-sort) specifies aria-sort on one header per table.
Geul has no Carbon expansion/radio-selection/dedicated batch-mode APIs. No features or palette were added.
The current bulk toolbar does not automatically lock row menus; do not describe it as Carbon batch-mode behavior.

## Public contract

Owners: [DataTableView.tsx](../../components/core/DataTable/DataTableView.tsx), [Display Table](../../components/core/Display/Display.tsx) and [selection.ts](../../components/core/DataTable/selection.ts).

| Area                    | Allowed API / defaults                                                                                                         | Usage                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Data                    | columns, rows, getRowKey, emptyMessage required                                                                                | Stable unique row/column keys. renderCell(row) returns content/controls. Core does not fetch/filter/sort data                                                                                          |
| Naming / announcements  | accessibleLabel, resultMessage, loadingMessage                                                                                 | Same collection name reaches desktop table, scroll region and mobile collection. Do not merge announcement sentences into visible cells/names                                                          |
| Density / boundaries    | density='compact', rowDividers='all', highlightOnHover=false                                                                   | compact/standard/comfortable; all/between. Use between next to a footer to avoid duplicate final rules                                                                                                 |
| Mobile                  | mobileLayout='cards'                                                                                                           | cards/compact/inline. cards switches by viewport; compact/inline by component container below sm. Both DOM presentations are generated                                                                 |
| Column sizing           | columnSizing='content', desktopMinWidth=640                                                                                    | content/fixed. fixed includes numeric width/minWidth sums and a 44px selection track in minimum width; it does not delete long content                                                                 |
| Columns                 | key/header/renderCell; optional accessibleLabel/width/minWidth/kind/align/mobileVisibility/sort                                | kind=data/action, align=start/center/end. Empty image/action headers need accessibleLabel                                                                                                              |
| Hidden columns          | mobileVisibility=visible/hidden                                                                                                | Only inline secondary metadata; not a general desktop/cards/compact hiding API. Do not hide primary/leading/action content                                                                             |
| Sorting                 | sort.ariaLabel/description/direction/order/showOrder/disabled/onToggle                                                         | asc/desc; display and request intent only. Lowest positive active order is primary; without order, first active column. Localized descriptions convey secondary order/direction                        |
| Row activation          | rowAction.onActivate/getAccessibleLabel; optional getHref                                                                      | Native link with href, otherwise button. Return a real navigation URL; distinguish cell controls                                                                                                       |
| Selection               | selection.selectedRowKeys/onSelectedRowKeysChange/selectAllRowsLabel; optional getRowLabel/isRowSelectable/onRowSelectionClick | Controlled keys; caller names individual/select-all checkboxes. Caller callbacks own Shift-range policy                                                                                                |
| Additional row behavior | rowInteraction.isSelected/isDisabled/isDimmed/preventTextSelection/onClick/onDoubleClick/onContextMenu/onKeyDown               | FileManager/Picker selection/open/context policies; no arbitrary visual overrides for selected state                                                                                                   |
| Async / reservation     | loading/loadingContent/reservedRowCount/rootRef                                                                                | loading replaces body. Positive finite count is ceiled, then reserves 44 + 60 × count px; unspecified loading minimum is 240px. This estimate is not measured row height across densities/long content |

status, error, arbitrary style/className, expansion, pagination and footer props are not DataTableView APIs.
Feature Alert owns errors; separate compositions own pagination/footer.
Allowed/rejected API evidence: [DataTableView.type-test.tsx](../../components/core/DataTable/DataTableView.type-test.tsx).

## Click, keyboard and selection policy

Row-background clicks call rowInteraction.onClick first, then rowAction.onActivate unless canceled. Background modifier clicks retain this existing contract.
Native row links retain Ctrl/Meta/Shift/Alt and canceled-click URL intent without duplicate onActivate.
Checkbox/action cells stop propagation. Clicks inside custom native/ARIA controls or contenteditable do not activate the row.

Mobile rowInteraction rows are groups named by primary content. Their main command is a separate native button/link, with checkbox/menu outside that command. The group itself is not tabbable.
With rowAction, the existing native command is reused; with rowInteraction alone, a hidden button before primary content directly receives caller click/key handlers. This retains FileManager/Picker target===currentTarget key guards.
Its focus-visible state uses the existing [rowWithAction rule](../../components/core/DataTable/DataTableView.module.css) to outline the row. No visible labels were added. Actual browser focus/reading order remains a review item.

FileManager selects with modifier click/Space and opens with Enter. Picker distinguishes folder selection/opening and file selection/immediate confirmation using allowMultiple. Core does not change these domain policies. Table is not an arrow-key spreadsheet grid.

DataTableView select-all changes only selectable current-page keys and retains external-page keys.
[useCurrentPageRowSelection](../../components/core/DataTable/selection.ts) instead removes keys absent from rows; client/server bulk sections using it have page-scoped selection. Callers such as FileManager own persistent selection.
Checkbox checked uses selection keys; row highlight uses rowInteraction.isSelected. These are not automatically identical.
Disabled rows remain visible but block callbacks/checkboxes. Nonselectable folders remain navigable without checkboxes.

## Changes and verification evidence

- Reproduced and fixed contenteditable/combobox/switch cell clicks activating rows.
- Fixed mobile plain-cell activation blocked by the row's own role=button when rowInteraction and rowAction were combined.
- Made the actual horizontal-scroll wrapper tabbable; an existing collection name also names its region.
- Reproduced and fixed multiple aria-sort headers. Existing translated directions now reach hidden descriptions through the [view-model](../../features/data-table/content-view-model.ts) and client/server adapters.
- Replaced mobile button wrappers that obscured descendant controls with named groups and separate commands in all three layouts; checked event contracts.

Evidence: [Core view tests](../../components/core/DataTable/DataTableView.test.tsx),
[client content tests](../../features/data-table/DataTableContent.test.tsx),
[server content tests](../../features/data-table/ServerDataTable/ServerDataTableContent.test.tsx),
[selection tests](../../components/core/DataTable/selection.test.tsx),
[FileManager tests](../../features/file-manager/FileManagerView.test.tsx),
[Picker tests](../../features/editor/components/EditorFileLibraryPickerView.test.tsx).
Vitest verifies DOM/events, not actual Tab movement, native keyboard activation or AT reading.
The specified Core/adapters/bulk-selection/FileManager/Picker run passed 12 files / 91 tests. Core public typing and changed TS/TSX ESLint passed; colors/gaps/row heights received no visual approval.
The later full tsc --noEmit also failed. IconButton test overload issues were corrected; remaining diagnostics concern duplicate Next-generated .next/types/.next/dev/types and Storybook vendor types.
Full tsc was not rerun for that document update; do not record a full-app type pass.

Consumers: /admin/posts [PostsTableContent](../../features/admin/post/PostsTableContent.tsx), /admin/files and /files [FileManagerView](../../features/file-manager/FileManagerView.tsx), and [EditorFileLibraryPickerView](../../features/editor/components/EditorFileLibraryPickerView.tsx).
Comparison fixtures: [DataTableView stories](../../components/core/DataTable/DataTableView.stories.tsx), Populated/Empty/Loading/SelectableAndSortable/CompactList/InlineList/TruncatedNames/FooterBoundary.
Route/story presence is not evidence of browser success.

Current [Table.Tr](../../components/core/Display/Display.tsx) injects ToolbarDensityProvider='comfortable' without dragState. DataTableView density='compact' reduces cell padding independently of this inner control inheritance.
Measure cell padding, parent gap and inherited control height separately when reviewing table actions.

## Remaining checks

| Item                      | Required evidence / owner                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mobile / tablet / desktop | Actual Posts/FileManager/Picker at 320/390/834/1440px and around sm: cards viewport versus compact/inline container switching, long Korean/English names, visible actions and page overflow                   |
| Keyboard / AT             | Browser and actual AT evidence for scroll focus/horizontal movement, mobile main-trigger outline, checkbox → command → menu reading/Tab order, disabled/pending transitions and multi-sort direction/priority |
| Density / footer          | Display/Core measurements of three densities, long two-line rows, toolbar/action gap roles and one between/footer boundary                                                                                    |
| Caller data               | Runtime does not validate every duplicate/empty key, populated dataset without columns or missing checkbox/collection name; strengthen consumer specifications/fixtures                                       |
| Custom rendering          | Both desktop/mobile DOM are generated. Caller verifies no duplicate literal IDs or rendering side effects; Core does not normalize caller content                                                             |
| System adoption           | Update Core contract/Storybook/state examples, verify actual consuming screens and record adoption scope. Pending review is not design approval                                                               |

documents.title: Table of contents: reading rail and scrolling outline
documents.markdown:
# Table of contents: reading rail and scrolling outline

This is the contract for the Notion-based scrolling correction.
Executed automated and browser checks are recorded separately in the review evidence.

## Scope and ownership

This guide covers the page-side table of contents, especially long-list scrolling.
It does not replace the rest of the design system, page layout or authored document.
Core `TableOfContentsView` owns presentation, opening, focus, scrolling, scrubbing and the
inline space reserved for the outline beside a document, and publishes that space to document
chrome outside it (`tableOfContentsScope`).
The navigation Feature supplies translated UI copy.
Post, page, legal, changelog, work and event Views supply their actual heading IDs, text and levels
and pass their document as `children`. Since 2026-10-13 there is no standalone fixed rail: every
outline reserves its space beside the document it navigates.

## Reference evidence

| Reference                                          | Visually inspected                                                                                                                                                                           | Applicable behavior                                                                                                                   | Limits                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Notion desktop app, 2026-10-12                     | A real 26-heading document: compact rail, expanded outline, scrollbar track clicked to later entries, entry selected and highlighted in the document, outside area entered, outline reopened | Quiet right-side marks; an adjacent floating title list; indentation; current-section emphasis; a bounded list with its own scrollbar | Pure hover without clicking, wheel boundary behavior, physical touch, mobile Notion and native screen-reader behavior were not verified |
| User-supplied ChatGPT screenshot, 2026-10-12 14:56 | The actual image: thin marks, a longer current mark, a floating card containing a title and body excerpt                                                                                     | Low visual weight while reading; contextual information appears next to the rail                                                      | The image alone does not establish keyboard, scrolling or mobile behavior                                                               |

[Notion's official contents guide](https://www.notion.com/help/columns-headings-and-dividers#table-of-contents)
documents a page-side outline revealed on hover, heading hierarchy and navigation.
It supplements the directly inspected app. It does not substitute for visual inspection.
No other product is a reference for this change.

For Geul, use Notion's scrolling heading list as the navigation model.
The ChatGPT image informs the quiet rail and adjacent reveal, not a new search interface
or a claim that its conversation excerpts are document headings.
A body-excerpt card is outside this scrolling correction; do not fabricate summaries
or add another competing navigation surface.

### Direct mouse investigation

Each mouse action was followed by an actual screenshot. These findings concern the
observed desktop document only; they are not inferred from markup or source code.

| Step | Actual operation                                             | Visible result                                                                                                                       | Local evidence            |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| R1   | Click the compact rail with the mouse                        | A floating title list appears at the right; the article keeps its width                                                              | `01-open.png`             |
| R2   | Click the lower track of the outline scrollbar               | Later titles replace earlier titles inside the same surface; the article remains at its previous section                             | `02-inner-scroll.png`     |
| R3   | Click a later title in that list                             | The document moves to that heading; it is briefly highlighted; the selected outline entry is blue                                    | `03-selected-heading.png` |
| R4   | Move to and click the blank top toolbar, outside the outline | The title list closes and small marks return                                                                                         | `04-closed.png`           |
| R5   | Re-enter the rail by mouse click                             | The outline starts at its first entries even though the document is near its end; it does not automatically center the current entry | `05-reopened.png`         |

The list stayed open after R3 while the pointer remained inside it. Selecting a title
did not itself dismiss the surface. These findings replace the former draft's
immediate-close behavior and current-row centering.

Long titles in this Notion screen used multiple lines, with an ellipsis on an overlong
entry. Indentation expressed heading levels. No search field, separate list-icon
launcher, section-collapse chevrons or persistent count appeared in the inspected outline.

Evidence is local and ignored by Git, under
`.artifacts/design-system/references/notion-toc/`. It contains the user's workspace
screen and is not copied into the published Storybook bundle.
One attempted drag navigated the article instead of isolating list scroll; it is not
used as proof of independent scrolling. The scrollbar-track result is the positive
evidence. No claim is made about untested hover timing or overscroll behavior.

## Author visibility and document controls

Page and Post authors can turn the outline off in Options. The persisted shared document layout
uses `hideTableOfContents`; absent/false retains the existing automatic heading threshold. Hidden
outlines reserve no rail and provide no navigation targets. This setting does not change
the authored headings or the content language menu. The menu stays at the page frame’s inline end.
The comment setting is a separate Post-only feature.

## Presentation (2026-10-19 owner decision)

Every width uses one presentation: the quiet rail. It replaces the three presentations approved on
2026-10-13, which kept the title list open as a persistent column from `lg`. A long outline gave
that column a second scroll area beside the document, and the rail is more compact. The rail stays
in the Notion/ChatGPT interaction family: a quiet indicator and a revealed title list. No floating
launcher or search panel is added.

| Viewport (reserved layout) | Presentation                                                                                                            | Reserved inline space                                               |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Every width                | Quiet rail; hover, keyboard focus or a press reveals the bounded title list; touch, pen or a mouse drag scrubs the rail | Rail target width (28px; 44px on coarse pointers) at the inline end |

Every document starts at the frame's start edge and runs up to the reserve at the inline end (owner
decision 2026-10-18, replacing the balanced 2026-10-13 reserve that centered the reading column): the
title, hero text and running text share the start edge, and the rail sits at the inline end. The rail
is sticky inside the reserved track, below the site header, and stops at the end of the document box, so the footer boundary needs no measurement. The document
plays (`stories/public/fixtures/document-outline.ts`) assert that no reading block or reading chrome
reaches the outline (`assertOutlineClearance`) and that the first reading block starts where the title
starts.

The outline is never taller than the viewport below the sticky line. Until the document has
scrolled the outline up to that line (it starts below a title or hero), Core also subtracts the
remaining distance, so the revealed list fits the first screen with its own scroll
instead of running off its bottom (written per frame as a style property, no re-render). At the
document end the outline leaves with the document box like any sticky element.

### Placement

There is one placement: the document starts at the start edge and only the inline end is reserved.
Running text (posts, legal documents, the changelog) keeps the reading measure from that edge; CMS
pages and entity details keep their section composition. The `center` placement was removed on
2026-10-18.

### Chrome outside the outline layout

Titles, heroes and overlaid document controls are rendered by `ContentLayoutView` outside the outline
layout. Its root carries `tableOfContentsScope`; inside it `--_table-of-contents-inset-end` holds the
reserved inline space (0 without an outline and on paper). `ContentChrome measure="reading"` keeps the
reading measure on the start edge clear of that space, the post hero ends its title where the reading
measure ends, and `ContentLayoutView` anchors its page language controls at the frame's inline end.
The control row sits above the outline instead of inheriting the outline's horizontal reserve.
Every title keeps the first body line's start edge at every width.

Revealed list details: the `tableOfContents.title` copy names the landmark and the rail link
(`aria-label`). Rows are real links in a nested list, at the rail target height (28px; the shared
44px `interaction-minimum` on coarse pointers). The list scrolls independently and contains overscroll.

Reading and focus order: the outline precedes the document in the DOM (its track is out of flow,
so this does not change the layout). Tab reaches the rail right after the document chrome; focusing
the rail reveals the list and ArrowDown moves into its links. Tab then continues into the document,
as the rail is seen beside the document's first lines. Links follow authored document order and nesting.

### Rail scrubbing

Pressing the rail (touch, pen, or a mouse drag of more than a few pixels) opens the outline
and highlights the heading at the same proportional position as the pointer; the outline
scrolls (itself only) so that row sits level with the pointer, beside the finger rather than at
the list's lower edge under the hand, and the rail's current mark follows the pointer. Releasing
navigates exactly like link activation (focus moves to the heading, reduced motion respected)
and, for touch, closes the outline. `pointercancel`, Escape or moving sideways more than
three rail widths away cancels without navigating. The rail uses `touch-action: none` (the
page does not scroll while scrubbing), suppresses the link callout and selection, and the
click that follows a scrub is ignored. A plain mouse click keeps the hover outline behavior.
Scrubbing only previews: `aria-current` and announcements do not change until navigation.
Keyboard and screen-reader users keep the link list.

### Nested headings

The outline is a nested `ol` built from authored levels in document order (`tocOutline`).
A skipped level (h2 → h4) nests one step; a shallower heading closes deeper sections.
Rows indent one `md` step per outline level, capped at three visual levels so deep headings
neither drift nor squeeze their titles. Long titles wrap with a hanging indent and clamp at
three lines; the complete title remains the link's accessible name. The current row's
containing sections are shown in ink (`data-ancestor`) so the reader keeps the parent context.
The current row itself is ink at medium weight with a hairline underline in the revealed list.
Location never uses the accent color.
Rail marks encode depth by length on one end-aligned axis (`md`, `xs`, `xxs`).
Each title keeps its authored direction inside a `<bdi>` isolate while its row keeps the interface
alignment, so an English title in an Arabic interface reads left to right with its punctuation in
place and the list stays right-aligned. In that mixed case Chromium draws a clamped title's ellipsis at
the interface end of the third line (verified at 834 and 1440, ar).
Authored rich text has heading levels 1–3, so production outlines nest three deep at most; the
changelog uses levels 2–3. Core still handles h1–h6 (DeepNesting). Outline depth is the authored
level: under a document title the body's elements are one level lower (authored H1 renders `h2`, see
[authored heading semantics](token-contract.md#authored-heading-semantics)), but the builders read
the authored levels and the scroll spy follows ids, so the outline is unchanged. Review fixtures
author H1–H3 without skipped levels; their plays assert one `h1` and no skipped level on the page.

## Reading measure

Running text reads at the `contentWidth.reading` role (44rem, `--geul-content-width-reading`), one
width for every language and script (owner decision 2026-10-13; it was 36rem). At the md body size
(16px Noto Sans, line height `line-height-document` 1.7) a full line measures about 92 Latin, 60
Hangul and 120 Arabic characters, spaces included (`typography-audit.mjs measure`, `reading`). In
posts the plain header, running text, series and
comments share one column on the start edge; the hero image keeps its full width and its title starts
and ends with the same column. Legal documents (current, scheduled preview, history detail and share link), the
changelog and work/event details use the same composition: `ContentLayoutView` with
`ContentChrome measure="reading"` for their header (notices, title, metadata, document actions) and
`.prose[data-reading-measure]` (or `LayoutContainer size="reading"` for the changelog list) for the
body. A work featured-image header and an event poster header keep their full-width grids, like the
post hero. Their information order is unchanged; the header → body gap is the shared `md`
document relationship.

| Block (full preview width)                                             | Maximum width      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| Text, lists, quotes, callouts, math, dividers, audio, attachments      | `reading`          |
| Tables, code blocks, Mermaid diagrams                                  | `standard` (62rem) |
| Images, video, standalone external video, maps, p5/three/shader scenes | `wide` (75rem)     |

A block with an authored preview width below 100% stays in the reading column. Breakouts never
exceed the document box, which ends at the outline's reserve.
The measure applies on screen only; paper keeps the print stylesheet's page measure
(`LayoutContainer size="reading"` drops its maximum in print).

### CMS page sections

CMS pages keep their sections' authored widths (`full`, `container` 1200px, `narrow` 800px; an unset
width renders `full`). The reading measure is not a section width option: `narrow` serves bounded text
sections, and the page wire contract (`PageSectionSettings.MaxWidth`) is unchanged.

## Design rules

| Part             | Required behavior                                                                     | Avoid                                                                                              |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Closed rail      | Small neutral marks in the page margin; a distinct current mark                       | A list icon, a persistent title panel, counters or a second long page                              |
| Opening          | Pointer enters the rail; keyboard focus or activation reveals the same outline        | Hover-only access; a detached launcher or search dialog                                            |
| Floating outline | One surface next to the rail, overlaid without moving the article                     | Resizing the article, body scroll locks, modal semantics                                           |
| Long list        | Height limited by viewport and footer; scroll inside the outline                      | Expanding every item down the page; a scrollbar on a tiny closed rail                              |
| Title rows       | Authored text and document order; indentation from actual levels; wrap long titles    | Invented grouping, truncating the only destination name, changing row height on hover              |
| Current section  | Distinct mark and `aria-current="location"`; opening starts the list at the beginning | Automatically centering the current row; overriding manual list scroll                             |
| Closing          | Leave the shared rail/list area; provide keyboard dismissal separately                | Closing solely because a pointer selected a heading; closing between rail and list; trapping focus |
| Small screens    | Reserved layouts show the same rail in reserved space, scrubbable by touch            | A floating button, a bottom sheet or a rail that covers text                                       |

Colors, typography, spacing, boundary, surface, shadow and focus use existing Geul
semantic roles. There are no new palette or theme tokens.
The rail is decorative inside one named focusable entry. Dense documents bound only
the number of decorative marks (48); the current indicator uses full-document position.
Every source heading remains in the outline. Decorative marks are not tiny link targets.
The expanded rows keep the Core compact/coarse-pointer minimum.
The maximum 20rem rail and 28rem outline are component geometry, not external standards.

The Geul outline owns vertical scroll and contains overscroll. Wheel
containment is a Geul acceptance requirement, not a verified Notion finding. Its inner
padding keeps the first/last row and focus outline clear of the edge. Opening starts
the list at the beginning without moving the page. Subsequent page scroll updates
current meaning but must not override manual outline scrolling.

## Public contract and content

Props are `items: TocItem[]`, `title` and `children` (required: the document the outline navigates).
`outlinePresentation` was removed on 2026-10-19 with the persistent column.
`hasTableOfContents(items)` exposes the threshold and `tableOfContentsScope` marks the ancestor
that shares the reserved insets with outside chrome. Items remain `{ id, label, level }`. IDs must
match rendered headings in document order.
Keep the existing omission for three or fewer headings.
Do not pass a rail subset back to the document or change authored labels with the UI locale.
There are no arbitrary size, color, maximum-heading-count or style override props.

The outline contains native links. Modified activation preserves browser link behavior.
Selecting a target moves focus to its heading and scrolls with the reduced-motion preference.
A temporary tabindex is removed on blur. Missing targets do not shift current indices.
Heading lookups are cached. Active-section tracking uses a binary lookup in vertical
geometry order, refreshed on content resize. The visible outline retains authored
reading order, including headings in page columns.
At the document end the last heading becomes current even if its short section
cannot scroll all the way to the reading line.

The rail exposes its localized name, expanded state and controlled list.
Tab reaches the rail and reveals the list; ArrowDown/keyboard activation enters the first entry.
Tab navigates real links. Escape closes and returns focus to the rail.
Keyboard activation closes the list after moving focus to the heading. Pointer selection
keeps it open while the pointer remains inside. Keyboard focus can keep it open after
pointer exit so focused links are never hidden. These are Geul keyboard extensions;
native Notion keyboard behavior was not verified.
No menu roles, modal backdrop or focus trap are used.
Theme changes use the existing semantic roles. Heading language stays authored.

## User scenarios and acceptance

| ID     | Scenario                            | Steps                                                                 | Expected result                                                                                                                         | Story / consumer                                                              |
| ------ | ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| TOC-01 | Read without interruption           | Open a normal document; scroll the article                            | Only compact marks; current position changes; article width and scroll remain stable                                                    | Default; PostView/PageView                                                    |
| TOC-02 | Inspect destinations                | Enter rail, then move into floating list, then leave                  | One adjacent list; no hover gap; close only after leaving both                                                                          | Default                                                                       |
| TOC-03 | Browse a long outline               | Open 60/120 entries; scroll to the bottom                             | List stays within viewport; last entry reachable; article does not scroll; wheel does not chain into article                            | LongDocument; ManyTopLevelSections                                            |
| TOC-04 | Reopen after navigation             | Navigate to a middle section, leave and reopen                        | List begins at the start; current meaning preserved; no forced list movement while browsing                                             | LongDocument                                                                  |
| TOC-05 | Navigate to a distant section       | Select a late heading from the outline                                | Actual heading receives focus; pointer selection keeps the outline open while the pointer remains inside; reduced-motion respected      | LongDocument; post/page fixtures                                              |
| TOC-06 | Use keyboard only                   | Tab to rail; ArrowDown; Tab between entries; Enter; reopen and Escape | Visible focus and readable names; heading focus on selection; no focus trap; Escape returns to rail                                     | KeyboardNavigation                                                            |
| TOC-07 | Read long and nested titles         | Open a mixed H2/H3/H4 outline with a long name                        | Titles wrap; hierarchy remains based on levels; no horizontal scrollbar                                                                 | LongLabels                                                                    |
| TOC-08 | Change theme and UI language        | Select Korean/English and light/dark/custom themes                    | Rail, surface, text and focus use current theme; title stays authored; navigation name localized                                        | All examples                                                                  |
| TOC-09 | Reach footer / short viewport       | Open at the top; scroll to footer; inspect a short-height viewport    | The revealed list fits the first screen below the title; the outline ends with the document box; internal scrollbar exposes all entries | FooterBoundary; MouseNavigation                                               |
| TOC-10 | Use mobile/tablet page              | Inspect 390px and 834px                                               | The rail sits beside, never over, the text; no floating button                                                                          | PhoneRail; MediumRail                                                         |
| TOC-12 | Read on a wide screen               | Open a long post at 1280–1920; scroll                                 | The closed rail sits beside the reading column; the current mark and row follow the reading position; no second scroll area             | WideRail; PostLongDocument                                                    |
| TOC-13 | Scrub on a phone                    | Press the rail, drag vertically, release; repeat and drag sideways    | Highlighted heading follows the finger; release navigates and focuses the heading; sideways/cancel does not navigate                    | ScrubNavigation; PhoneRail                                                    |
| TOC-14 | Read nested sections                | Open an h2–h6 outline with long titles; scroll to a deep section      | Nested list; indentation capped at three steps; titles wrap/clamp; parents of the current row shown in ink                              | DeepNesting                                                                   |
| TOC-15 | Align document chrome               | Hero/plain post and untitled page with a language menu at 390–1920    | Title and first body line share a start edge; page language controls stay at the frame’s inline end, independently of the outline rail  | PostHeroLongDocument; PageLongDocumentUntitled                                |
| TOC-16 | Read legal, changelog, work, event  | Open each long document at 390–1920, light/dark, ar; print A4         | Reading column on the start edge, outline at the end, same header order; paper has no outline                                           | TermsLongDocument; ChangelogLongDocument; WorkLongDocument; EventLongDocument |
| TOC-11 | Document changes or IDs are missing | Replace items; supply a missing target                                | Three-or-fewer clears navigation; pending work cleaned up; remaining heading indices intact                                             | Core unit tests                                                               |

## Verification and migration

The rejected list-button/search/collapse-panel draft is superseded.
Existing Feature props, heading data and routes require no migration.
Pointer scrubbing returned on 2026-10-13 as an owner-approved enhancement of the rail only;
the revealed list still uses ordinary links. Do not treat condensed decorative marks as
independent touch targets: the whole rail is one target that maps position to heading.

Removing the standalone rail is a breaking Core change: `children` is required and `footerSelector`
is gone. Every consumer was migrated (see the changelog); a new consumer passes its document as
children. The legal editor
preview renders the body without an outline.

Run `node scripts/design-system/review.mjs run toc-navigation`.
Browser screenshots and observations must identify exact scenarios, viewport, theme,
locale and production View fixture. Automatic tests and visual checks are separate.
The review examples stay at their initial position for manual inspection. Dedicated
MouseNavigation, KeyboardNavigation, ScrubNavigation, WideRail and DeepNesting examples run
automated scenarios against the rail on the Storybook test runner's 1280px page (hover, keyboard,
scrubbing, fit to the first screen, aria-current). Touch scrubbing on devices is covered by the
390/834 review captures and by Core unit tests. LongDocument, ManyTopLevelSections, LongLabels, FooterBoundary, MediumRail and
PhoneRail are manual review surfaces; Storybook's viewport toolbar sets their width.
Production consumers are Pages / Public / Documents / PostLongDocument, PostHeroLongDocument,
PageLongDocument and PageLongDocumentUntitled; Pages / Legal / Public Document /
TermsLongDocument; Pages / Public / Utilities / ChangelogLongDocument; Pages / Public / Entity Detail /
WorkLongDocument and EventLongDocument. Review evidence (plans, before/after captures, A4 PDFs) is in
`.artifacts/design-system/reviews/toc-followups/`.
PageContentView now connects its rendered rich-text sections and nested columns to
the same navigation owner; that production connection was previously missing.
Those two examples include the production ShellView through its existing Storybook
harness, with local navigation and footer data. They do not call the server Shell controller.
Local fixtures establish Core/View behavior, not backend persistence, physical touch
or native VoiceOver/Orca acceptance. Read the recorded review for executed scope.

## Print omission

The rail is screen chrome. `TableOfContents.module.css` hides them, removes the
reserved inline space and sets the published insets to 0 under `@media print`, so chrome outside
the layout prints on the page measure too; global print styles (`lib/styles/print.css`) must not
select the generated CSS-module class (such as `TableOfContents_wrapper`) or reserved Core markers.

documents.title: Tables and collection toolbars
documents.markdown:
# Tables and collection toolbars

Core owns cell spacing, header/body alignment, control density, responsive switching and divider geometry. Features supply columns, records, localized labels and actions. Use existing space, type, control and border tokens; this consolidation introduces no new tokens.

## Shared toolbar ownership

[ToolbarLayout](../../components/core/Section/ToolbarLayout.tsx) owns collection search/filter/action geometry for file browsers and data tables. `SelectionToolbar`, `DataTableToolbar` and `DataTableSelectionToolbar` are adapters to this same owner; none keeps its own responsive CSS. The client and server DataTable families consume these adapters.

| Contract                       | Use                                                                   |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `arrangement="flow"`           | Existing child-based toolbar compositions; wrapping flex layout       |
| `arrangement="actions-end"`    | Search, filter/sort group and actions; optional leading location      |
| `arrangement="actions-inline"` | Location + view actions, then search/filter controls as width permits |
| `density="compact"` (default)  | Shared compact button scale and xs search/filter text                 |
| `inset="none\|content"`        | Plain table controls or content-aligned file browser inset            |
| `divider="none\|surface"`      | Exactly one explicitly owned boundary                                 |

Only Core owns container queries. Below `lg`, an inline collection toolbar places location/actions first and filters/search second. Below `sm`, location and view actions remain together; search and filters occupy their own rows. Ordinary table controls keep search/filter/actions on one row down to `xs`; below `xs`, search takes the first row and filter/actions share the second row, avoiding an isolated trailing action row. Slots have zero intrinsic minimum so long translations and inputs cannot widen the parent. Action groups use xxs spacing and wrap where appropriate. Search fields fill their allocated slot; client/server table searches have no feature-owned 400px width wrapper.

TextInput, Select, MultiSelect and NativeSelect inherit compact size/density from the toolbar provider; Select/MultiSelect portals retain that same scale. Standalone fields retain their existing named sizes. Core controls retain the interaction-minimum behavior for coarse pointers. Do not shrink targets through feature CSS or numeric icon sizes.

ToolbarLayout keeps ordinary Tab order and the native input/combobox arrow keys. Contextual editor commands continue to use `ToolbarSurface`, which owns command-arrow navigation. These are distinct interaction contracts: a search/filter form must not acquire command-navigation behavior merely because it looks like a toolbar. See the [WAI toolbar pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/).

## Tables

`DataTableView` defaults to compact density. Header and body checkbox cells use the same selection-control wrapper, middle alignment and reserved track. Consumer overrides for checkbox vertical alignment are removed. Single-selection and non-selectable rows omit controls while reserving the same leading track when the table supports selection.

Use `columnSizing="fixed"` where a flexible name/title track must truncate. Long text retains its full accessible value and title. Align numeric/size columns with `column.align="end"`, including their header. Header sort labels and indicators stay together and respect the column alignment; they do not occupy opposite ends of a wide name track. Do not hide columns with consumer CSS.

| Narrow presentation                      | Use                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mobileLayout="inline"`                  | One-line collections; flexible name, short trailing metadata, `mobileVisibility="hidden"` for secondary columns |
| `mobileLayout="compact"`                 | A primary line with concise secondary metadata where both are needed                                            |
| `mobileLayout="cards"`                   | Records whose named fields must remain available in a readable stack                                            |
| Native `Table` + `Table.ScrollContainer` | True comparisons/matrices where column relationships must be retained                                           |

File Manager and Editor File Library Picker share [FileBrowserListView](../../features/file-manager/ui/FileBrowserListView.tsx), plus one presentation adapter. File rows are always inline: checkbox, icon, filename, short lowercase extension and size. Below the container `sm` breakpoint, format/location are omitted and only size remains. Full MIME and richer administrative metadata remain in details. See [file-browser.md](./file-browser.md).

Use `rowDividers="between"` when a footer owns the final boundary. Do not combine a last-row rule with another footer rule or add an outer border/striping to an already separated compact table without a specific need. A standalone table owns its final rule.

Scroll containers need a localized region name and a keyboard focus target. Native tables retain `th`, `td`, scope and sorting state; responsive styling does not replace those relationships. See the [WAI table guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/tables/).

## Consumer review and corrections

| Family inspected                                                      | Result                                                                                                                                                     |
