| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Client/server DataTable                                               | Shared toolbar layout and control density; redundant top checkbox alignment removed; search width wrappers removed                                         |
| File Manager / Library Picker                                         | One shared list, trailing short format/size, inline mobile rows, current-folder-only narrow path, matching header/list insets and no duplicate status rule |
| Translation overview matrices                                         | Existing large-density/striping/outer-border combination replaced by compact rows and one row rule; shared labelled keyboard-scroll container              |
| Policy history                                                        | Shared labelled keyboard-scroll container protects date-range columns on narrow screens                                                                    |
| Form submissions, translation jobs, campaign analytics, public series | Already use Core Table scroll containers; retained existing domain-specific columns                                                                        |
| Release track credits and release associations                        | Existing responsive card/table or compact Core Table consumers; retained needed domain fields and reorder behavior                                         |

This is an ownership and source review of those families, not a claim that every application route has received visual approval. Verify representative Core stories and production-view stories at phone/tablet/desktop widths, in light/dark and more than one locale. Core typography/control/layout checks, runtime/type contracts and interaction tests accompany visual checks.

## Storybook and verification

Use Core / Layout / ToolbarLayout / Collection and Table Controls for slot reflow and inherited control scale. Composition / Data Table / Toolbars shows the compatibility adapters. Core / Data Display / DataTableView / Inline List shows truncation and secondary-field omission; existing cards/compact/sorting/loading stories cover the other contracts. File picker form stories verify actual selection, Add and Submit; the browser story contains no extra form.

Test that resizing does not change records or selection, checkbox/range input remains modifier-aware, search/combobox keys remain native, folder navigation respects the accessible root, and horizontal scrolling stays within the table region. Regenerate inventories after adding or moving system components.

# Design token audit

This report is generated from production source by `node scripts/design-system/check-tokens.mjs --report`. Regenerate after source changes. Current source findings do not certify every visual state.

## Current measured scope

- 2469 production CSS/TS/TSX files scanned under app, components, features and lib, plus the central theme.ts.
- 225 known semantic and font tokens in shared CSS definition files.
- 0 remaining interface/runtime literal color occurrences in 0 files, excluding central definitions and the authored-color exceptions below.
- 0 remaining authored editor palette literals in legacy variables.css. Their exact document colors belong to the shared authored palette source.
- 20 authored editor color definitions are owned by the shared token source and generated into the same durable document roles.
- 0 existing literal CSS spacing/typography occurrences covered by the migration baseline.
- 0 existing custom-property declarations/inline assignments outside central files (private `--_*` implementation variables are permitted).
- 174 literal CSS dimension occurrences in spacing, typography and geometry properties; 66 distinct values. These are audit findings, not blanket errors: canvas dimensions, geometry and responsive layouts require context.
- 223 CSS custom-property declarations, 83 distinct names, 51 names declared more than once. Theme/state/media overrides are expected; equal values alone do not establish semantic duplication.
- 0 findings match the reviewed migration baseline; 0 new violations; 0 obsolete baseline keys eligible for removal.

## Enforcement contract

Run `node scripts/design-system/check-tokens.mjs` (or `pnpm design-system:check`) in CI. New literal colors, CSS spacing/typography values and non-private custom-property definitions fail relative to an occurrence-count baseline. Adding another occurrence of an old color fails. Editing a literal color or spacing value in place also fails. Line movement does not change approval. Existing custom properties may change initializer to migrate to a semantic token; their file/name/occurrence count stays constrained. Unknown semantic/font variable references or literal-name runtime CSS setters and parse errors always fail and cannot be baselined. Missing baseline data fails closed.

Allowed central definition files:

- `node_modules/@echovisionlab/design-system/src/tokens.css`

Legacy definition files (existing definitions constrained by the baseline; new declarations are forbidden):

- `lib/styles/variables.css`

Legacy `variables.css` now consumes shared roles; its authored palettes, safe-area aliases and compatibility token definitions have been migrated. New design tokens belong in the TypeScript token source and its generated CSS. Private local variables use the `--_` prefix; they may compose semantic tokens for hover, selected and size states. Mantine `--mantine-*` overrides are upstream framework token assignments, not application token definitions. Runtime CSS setters may update registered semantic tokens or upstream/private variables; other literal names require an existing baseline allowance. The theme bridge may reference canonical tokens but cannot define another literal palette. The checker does not treat Mantine named palette props as literal colors because those are library token references.

`--write-baseline` is an explicit migration-maintenance operation. Review its diff; never run it as part of CI or to approve a new violation automatically. Existing debt is visible below. Removed debt is reported as stale and does not block migration; use `--prune-baseline --report` to remove only obsolete occurrences after review. Pruning cannot approve new findings.

## Remaining literal colors

| Source | Occurrences | Lines |
| ------ | ----------: | ----- |
| None   |           0 | —     |

## Remaining CSS spacing/typography literals

New nonzero px/rem/em values on padding, margin, gap, row-gap and column-gap fail (`raw-spacing`); zero, percentages, inherit, auto and token expressions are allowed, and spacing within explicit print media and page rules is classified as authored print geometry. Type sizes are stricter (`raw-font-size`): any literal unit (px, rem, em, pt, %, viewport units), font-size keywords and unitless line-height in `font-size`, `line-height` and `font` fail on screen and in print rules, because the token generator projects the paper scale onto the same roles. TS style objects, option objects, DOM style and canvas `font` assignments and `setProperty('font-size', …)` are checked the same way. Widths, heights, radii, viewport geometry and responsive breakpoints remain audit-only. Mantine named scale props in TS/TSX remain valid references. Initial spacing allowances were measured from git HEAD before this migration rather than approving the changed working tree.

| Source | Occurrences |
| ------ | ----------: |

Authored typography exceptions (artwork, not interface roles):

- `lib/utils/og-config.ts`: Generated share-image artwork defaults (pixel geometry rendered by Satori)
- `lib/utils/og-image.tsx`: Generated share-image artwork (pixel geometry from site settings)
- `features/page/blocks/immersive-scene/SceneRenderer.tsx`: Viewport-scaled immersive scene title artwork (clamp/vw geometry of the authored scene)
- `features/application-error/ErrorCodeParticles.tsx`: Canvas glyph mask sampled into the error-code particle artwork

| `--_document-layout-controls-space` |            2 | `features/document-layout/ui/ContentLayoutView.module.css`                                             |
| `--_map-callout-line-color`         |            2 | `features/map/ui/MapLibreMapView.css`                                                                  |
| `--_map-callout-current-text-color` |            2 | `features/map/ui/MapLibreMapView.css`                                                                  |
| `--_map-callout-current-desc-color` |            2 | `features/map/ui/MapLibreMapView.css`                                                                  |
| `--_map-callout-current-bg-color`   |            2 | `features/map/ui/MapLibreMapView.css`                                                                  |
| `--_map-callout-scale`              |            3 | `features/map/ui/MapLibreMapView.css`                                                                  |
| `--font-family-sans`                |            5 | `lib/styles/font-assignment.css`                                                                       |

## Authored-color exceptions

These sources contain provider identity colors or persisted/output artwork values. Their literal values remain separate from interface role tokens. Exceptions cover literal colors only; new custom-property declarations and unknown semantic references are still checked.

| Source                                                         | Reason                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `components/core/Social/brand-colors.ts`                       | Third-party identity palettes           |
| `lib/theme/site-brand.ts`                                      | Configurable site branding default      |
| `lib/types/map-theme/schema.ts`                                | User-authored map theme schema defaults |
| `lib/types/site-setting/config.ts`                             | User-authored site setting defaults     |
| `lib/utils/og-config.ts`                                       | Generated share-image palette           |
| `lib/utils/og-image.tsx`                                       | Generated share-image artwork           |
| `features/page/blocks/immersive-scene/schema.ts`               | User-authored scene defaults            |
| `features/page/blocks/immersive-scene/scene-renderer-model.ts` | User-authored 3D artwork                |
| `features/page/blocks/immersive-scene/settings-model.ts`       | User-authored 3D artwork defaults       |
| `features/map/hooks/useMap3DBuildings.ts`                      | Map artwork styling                     |
| `features/map/hooks/useMapLabels.ts`                           | Map artwork styling                     |

## Limits and interpretation

CSS uses a real PostCSS parser and TS/TSX uses the TypeScript compiler parser, so comments and regular expressions do not create false color findings. TS string values (including embedded HTML and templates) are inspected conservatively; persisted color defaults and graphic runtime strings outside explicit exception files may be baseline debt rather than interface styling. The audit does not infer intent from a matching color.

Generated/vendor sources, documentation, Storybook output, story fixtures, stories, tests, type declarations and fixtures are excluded. CSS selector/data-attribute custom-property references not expressed as semantic/font `var()` references, computed concatenated token names, dynamic numeric JS style values, user-uploaded styles and third-party runtime CSS are not validated. Literal CSS dimensions are counted only on the properties listed by the scanner. CSS spacing enforcement covers the explicit properties above; JavaScript numeric spacing props, private variable values and dynamically composed styles are not covered. Repeated declarations usually mean light/dark or state overrides; review their role and cascade before consolidating them.

documents.title: Design token contract
documents.markdown:
# Design token contract

The authority is `@echovisionlab/design-system/tokens`. App, Storybook, generated CSS and
JavaScript adapters consume this source. New UI must use Core's closed presentation APIs.
Feature-level numbers and local tokens cannot replace a shared presentation role.

## Foundations and roles

| Family           | Authority                                           | Usage                                                                |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Palette          | `primitiveTokens.colors`                            | Base theme assignments, preset overrides and authored color families |
| Spacing          | `primitiveTokens.spacing`                           | Named Core gaps, insets and padding                                  |
| Typography       | `fontSize`, `heading`, `fontWeight`, `lineHeight`   | Body, title and supporting text roles                                |
| Control geometry | `controlHeight`, `interaction`, `chrome`            | Closed control sizes, compact density and shared glyphs              |
| Composition      | `contentWidth`, `breakpoints`, `hierarchy`          | Content widths, responsive transitions and nesting                   |
| Surface behavior | `radius`, `border`, `opacity`, `layer`, `motion`    | Shared appearance and interaction feedback                           |
| Theme roles      | `semanticThemes`, `invariantTokens`, `themePresets` | Meaningful UI colors/effects; every preset shares role names         |

Spacing, font and control-height scales are defined once. Derived TypeScript roles read those
scales. `derivedTokenRoles` makes CSS aliases explicit; generated CSS references the foundation
instead of copying its current value. Changing a foundation therefore updates its dependents.

| Derived role                                                                                         | Foundation                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `spacing-role-control-label`, `spacing-role-action-group`                                            | `spacing-xs`                                            |
| `spacing-role-control-label-compact`, `spacing-role-toolbar-item`, `spacing-role-field-label`        | `spacing-xxs`                                           |
| `spacing-role-field-column`                                                                          | `spacing-sm`                                            |
| `spacing-role-section`                                                                               | `spacing-xl`                                            |
| `control-padding-compact`, `control-padding-xs`, `control-padding-standard`, `control-padding-large` | `spacing-xxs`, `spacing-sm`, `spacing-md`, `spacing-lg` |
| `chrome-font-size`                                                                                   | `font-size-xs`                                          |
| `chrome-row-height`                                                                                  | `control-height-chrome`                                 |
| `chrome-section-row-height`                                                                          | `control-height-compact`                                |
| `heading-h4`, `heading-h5`, `heading-h6`                                                             | `font-size-lg`, `font-size-md`, `font-size-sm`          |
| `text-control-padding-xs`, `text-control-padding-md`                                                 | `spacing-xxs`, `spacing-xs`                             |

`text-control-padding-sm` (0.375rem, 6px at a 16px root) is an explicit off-scale exception. It is
TextButton's middle block padding between the `xxs` (4px) and `xs` (8px) steps and has no derived
foundation. Do not copy 6px elsewhere or treat it as a spacing step.

Square chrome commands use `control-height-chrome` directly; there is no separate chrome action size.

Role names remain public so existing consumers keep their meaning. Icon geometry is owned by
`chrome-icon-size`; equal body-font and icon dimensions do not make them the same semantic role.
Button accessory SVGs, TextButton's Core indicator, IconButton glyphs and DropdownMenu command SVGs consume this
same role, including wrapped SVGs. Consumers supply an icon without a numeric size. Core owns
the rendered dimensions and vertical alignment; image/avatar accessories retain their media
geometry. Post, Page, Work and Policy header actions and table row menus follow this contract.
Menu row height is a distinct compact-menu contract, not an alias of a coincidentally equal
heading size. Application header heights use rem and share the same responsive scroll offset.

## Type scale, document title and paper

One heading scale serves interface and document headings. `primitiveTokens.heading` holds the
base (below `sm`) sizes; `responsiveTokens.sm` restores the wider steps and `printTokens`
replaces the type roles on paper. The generator emits both as media blocks (print last, because
printed pages are wider than `sm`), so Core `Heading`, `.prose` and the Tiptap editor read the
same role at the same width and on paper. Do not add per-consumer breakpoints for headings.

The responsive steps belong to the global heading roles rather than to a separate document
heading family: a second scale would make interface `h1`–`h3` and authored `h1`–`h3` diverge on
phones, duplicate every heading selector and let the editor drift from the published view. On
phones interface headings that use scale 1–3 therefore shrink by 2–6px with the documents. A
responsive `scale` object remains for changing the role itself per breakpoint.

| Role                                      | Below `sm`               | `sm`+ | Paper (A4/Letter)                     |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----- | ------------------------------------- |
| `heading-title` (Heading `scale="title"`) | 20px                     | 24px  | 15pt                                  |
| `heading-h1`                              | 16px                     | 18px  | 12pt                                  |
| `heading-h2`                              | 15px                     | 16px  | 11pt                                  |
| `heading-h3`                              | 14px                     | 14px  | 10pt                                  |
| `heading-h4` / `h5` / `h6`                | 13 / 12 / 11px           | same  | 9.5 / 9 / 8pt (follow `lg`/`md`/`sm`) |
| `font-size-xs/sm/md/lg/xl`                | 10 / 11 / 12 / 13 / 14px | same  | 7.5 / 8 / 9 / 9.5 / 10.5pt            |
| `heading-weight` (every heading)          | 500                      | 500   | 500                                   |
| `icon-size-xs/sm/md/lg/xl` (geometry)     | 12 / 14 / 16 / 18 / 20px | same  | same                                  |
| `line-height-md` (interface, dense text)  | 1.55                     | 1.55  | 1.5                                   |
| `line-height-document` (document text)    | 1.6                      | 1.6   | 1.6                                   |

`heading-title` is the document title role: Post (plain and hero), Page chrome and public
document details (Work, Event, Release, Artist, Label, Terms/Privacy and their history detail,
shared legal documents, Changelog) and the legal editor's title preview. It stays at least one
text-scale step (×1.125, ≥4px) above an authored body `h1` at every width and on paper;
`components/core/typography-scale.test.ts` enforces the order title > h1 > h2 > h3 > h4 > h5 > h6
and the published/editor heading parity, and the `PostHeadingHierarchy*`/`PageHeadingHierarchy`
stories assert it in the browser. Interface page titles keep `scale={2}`; they are not documents.

### Authored heading semantics

Size and outline depth follow the authored level; the rendered element follows the page outline.
A public document has one `h1`, its title, and no skipped levels. The document title layer owns the
offset: `ContentLayoutView` wraps its body in `DocumentHeadingScope` (`@/features/document-layout`)
with `parentLevel` 1 when it has chrome (the chrome renders the title `h1`) and 0 without. The
published renderers (`GeneratedRichTextBlockView`, `DefaultBlockView`) read the scope and render
authored H1 → `h2`, H2 → `h3`, H3 → `h4`, capped at `h6` (`documentHeadingTag`), with
`data-heading-level` carrying the authored level. Without a scope (an untitled CMS page, the
editor/published comparison) the authored element is kept, so the author's H1 is the page `h1`.
A body below a section label declares that label's level (Release/Label/Artist descriptions under
their `aria-level` 2 label: `parentLevel={2}`, H1 → `h3`); the legal editor preview declares 1 below
its title, and `policyTiptapDocumentToHtml(doc, { headingParentLevel })` does the same for its HTML.

`.prose` heading sizes key on `[data-heading-level]` and keep element-only fallbacks
(`.prose :where(h1:not([data-heading-level]))`, class-level specificity) for HTML without the attribute,
so a Core `Heading` inside `.prose` keeps its own role; no rule sizes a body heading
by its element alone (`typography-scale.test.ts`). Ids, the table of contents (authored levels),
the scroll spy (ids) and Markdown export (`#` per authored level) are unchanged. Screen (390, 834, 1440) and A4 sizes were measured identical before and after (typography audit `compare`).

Paper sizes are physical points so a printed document is 10.5pt running text with code, tables
and captions at 9pt (`sm`) and metadata at 8pt (`xs`). Feature and print CSS consume the same
role names (`var(--geul-font-size-sm)`), never a literal size. The token scanner reports
`raw-font-size` for literal `font-size`, `line-height` and `font` values in any unit (including
`pt`, `%`, viewport units and keywords), in print rules too, and for TS style/option objects,
DOM style and canvas `font` assignments. `authoredTypographyFiles` in
`scripts/design-system/token-policy.mjs` names the only exceptions: generated share-image
artwork, the immersive scene title artwork and the error-code particle canvas.

### Document leading and block rhythm

`line-height-document` (1.6, owner decision 2026-10-18; it was 1.7) is the leading of running text in document
bodies, one value for every language and script: published `.prose` paragraphs, list items and their
markers, quotes, callout copy and check-list items, the same Tiptap editor blocks, and Core
`List leading="document"` (changelog release notes). Interface text keeps `line-height-xs`–`xl`
paired with its size, dense document content (tables, code, captions) keeps its interface role, and
headings keep `heading-line-height`. Paper uses the same 1.6 at 9pt, above the dense 1.5 because the
A4 measure is long and Hangul glyphs fill the em box, so the return sweep needs the extra leading. A Core `Heading` inside a `.prose` region (for example the legal editor's preview title)
keeps its own role: the `.prose` heading element fallbacks have class-level specificity (`:where`).

Blocks of a document body are `spacing-md` (12px) apart: paragraph → paragraph, paragraph ↔ quote,
callout, list, media, table and code. Items of one list (the same list kind in a row) stay
`spacing-xs` (8px) apart. A heading that follows content opens `spacing-xl` (24px) above it and
keeps `spacing-xs` below. The heading step moved from `lg` with the paragraph gap: before, the
heading's 16px was twice the 8px block gap; against a 12px gap 16px would leave the heading almost
equidistant between two sections, so `xl` restores 2:1 above and keeps the heading closer to its
text than paragraphs are to each other. `lib/styles/document-content.css` owns the rules for
published blocks, materialized HTML, nested children and callout content, and Tiptap's block group
(its flex gap stays `xs`; margins add the difference), so the editor and the published view measure
equal (`typography-audit.mjs gaps`, and the `Feature/Editor/Public Block Comparison` plays).

`chrome-font-size` and `chrome-section-font-size` alias `font-size-sm` (11px) for navigation and section
overlines (SideNavigation, DropdownMenu), so chrome Hangul, Kana and Han never drop below 11px. The text
scale steps one pixel (owner decision 2026-10-18): `xs` (10px) is reserved for captions, badges and
field help, never for navigation or running text.
Geometry that sits beside text (icons, logo defaults, check-list boxes, emoji choices) uses `icon-size-*`,
so it keeps its size when the text scale changes. Coarse-pointer text fields keep 16px through
`interaction-text-minimum`.
Uppercase labels separate from running text by `letter-spacing-caps` (0.04em) and weight, not size.

## Content widths

`contentWidth` roles are content maximums, not breakpoints: `form` (28rem) single-column
account forms; `reading` (32rem) the running-prose measure of long documents; `compact`,
`standard` and `wide` (48/62/75rem) LayoutContainer surfaces and document breakout widths.
`reading` was added on 2026-10-13 for a repeated meaning: running text and the chrome that shares
its column. Posts, legal documents (current, preview, history, share), the changelog and work/event
detail pages read on it; CMS page sections keep their own widths and do not offer it (their
`narrow` width serves bounded text sections). One width serves every language and script (owner
decision 2026-10-18: it narrowed from 44rem with the 12px body): a full line measures about 85 Latin,
55 Hangul and 110 Arabic characters, spaces included.
CSS consumes `--geul-content-width-reading`; React
layout uses `LayoutContainer size="reading"` and `ContentChrome measure="reading"`. It is a screen
measure: `LayoutContainer size="reading"` drops its maximum on paper, where the print page measure
applies. Feature CSS must not copy the value.

## Layer scale

`primitiveTokens.layer` is the only stacking authority. Generated CSS exposes `--geul-layer-*`;
`components/core/layer-contract.ts` projects the same values as numbers (`overlayLayers`) for
React Aria portals and inline styles. Roles are listed in ascending order.

| Layer      | Value | Meaning and consumers                                                                         |
| ---------- | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sticky`   | 100   | Page-owned pinned surfaces under application chrome: TableOfContents, Post editor zen surface |
| `backdrop` | 200   | Modal underlay. ApplicationFrame header/navigation use `backdrop - 1`                         |
| `modal`    | 201   | Modal and drawer dialogs                                                                      |
| `banner`   | 250   | Viewport-pinned notices: cookie consent, draft-mode alert                                     |
| `floating` | 260   | Non-modal floating tools (FloatingPanel); their own popups and tooltips stay above            |
| `popup`    | 300   | Menus, popovers, listboxes, sortable previews                                                 |
| `toast`    | 400   | Notification toasts, above modals and popups, below tooltips                                  |
| `tooltip`  | 1000  | Tooltips                                                                                      |
| `progress` | 10000 | Route progress bar; always topmost                                                            |

Banner and floating sit above `modal` because ApplicationFrame chrome occupies the slot directly
below the backdrop and these surfaces must clear the fixed header and workspace navigation. Moving
them below modals requires ApplicationFrame to consume a lower named chrome layer first.
Local stacking inside a component or canvas (`z-index: 1`, media resize handles, map loading
surfaces) is not part of this scale and must not borrow a global layer.

Breakpoints are not emitted as CSS variables because media queries cannot read them. JavaScript
uses `primitiveTokens.breakpoints`; CSS media queries use the generated PostCSS projection
`@echovisionlab/design-system/breakpoints.json` (`$mantine-breakpoint-*`).

## Motion

`motion-fast` (100ms), `motion-normal` (140ms) and `motion-slow` (300ms) time state transitions with
`motion-easing`. `motion-spin` (1000ms) is the single loading-rotation period consumed by
`components/core/Spinner.module.css`; it is deliberately calm and is not a transition duration.
Reduced motion stops rotation and transitions at their owners.

## Theme selection

`lib/theme/themes.ts` defines the `ThemeId` registry: `light`, `dark`, `ocean-light`
and `ocean-dark`. Each preset chooses a base scheme and overrides existing semantic
roles with existing primitive colors. `getThemeTokens()` resolves the complete role
map; `themeVariables()` projects it to CSS. Presets do not add component tokens,
spacing scales or independent command/status meanings.

The shared `DesignSystemProvider` owns the document projection, including portaled
surfaces. `data-geul-theme` records the base scheme; `data-geul-theme-id` records the
selected preset. Storybook's theme toolbar passes `forceTheme` through this provider.
Preview changes do not read or write saved application preferences. Application
preferences remain light, dark and automatic system mode.

Add a recurring custom theme in this registry and verify its text, surface, command,
status, chart and focus combinations. A role name cannot change meaning between
presets. Components must read semantic roles rather than select a palette locally.

## 2026-10-12 consolidation and migration

Removed seven unused semantic roles from both base themes: `wave-progress-soft`,
`media-surface`, `media-control`, `track-muted`, `track-border`, `track-fill` and
`shadow-docked`. Their CSS variables and TypeScript semantic keys are removed together.
The source audit found no current production consumer, theme override, derived alias,
adapter lookup or test reference outside central definitions. Generated references and
historical review excerpts were not counted as consumers. This repository no longer
owns a DTCG export pipeline; no token exchange file requires a second update.

| Removed family            | Current production authority                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Wave progress             | `readWaveMediaColors` consumes `action-primary`; waveform and cursor retain their distinct `wave-muted` and `wave-cursor` roles.     |
| Media surface and command | `MediaAudioFrame` consumes the shared Section surface. `MediaTransport` commands consume Core Control state roles.                   |
| Legacy track colors       | The persisted timeline adapter consumes `border-strong` and `action-primary`. New player transport uses the shared waveform adapter. |
| Docked shadow             | No current docked-shadow consumer remains. Existing surfaces retain their own documented shadow roles.                               |

No in-repository consumer migration is needed. A copied stylesheet or external runtime
that names a removed variable must migrate to the current owner above before consuming
this source change. Do not add fallback aliases that preserve an unused parallel role.

The spacing cleanup reuses existing relationships: table command groups now use
`action-group` instead of a local `xxs` choice, so their gap changes from 4px to 8px at
a 16px root and retains wrapping. Media command clusters use `toolbar-item` (4px);
outer media groups and video settings commands use `action-group` (8px). Clock content
retains the `xxs` scale because its separators are content, not commands.

Equal values do not imply equal roles. `control-label` and `action-group` both resolve
to 8px but express internal accessory alignment and external command separation.
`field-label` resolved to 8px until 2026-10-13 and now resolves to 4px (`xxs`) so Core
Field and every Core Input share one stacked label–control–help rhythm. They remain
separate aliases even when their values coincide.
Palette grades, persisted document color names, menu row height and glyph/target roles
also retain their distinct contracts. No new roles or migration-baseline allowances
were added. The production spacing audit found no nonzero literal gap/padding/margin
debt within its declared CSS property scope; geometry and print exceptions remain explicit.

Review the actual examples in `Foundations / Spacing`, `Foundations / Iconography`,
`Composition / Table Toolbars / Action Group` and `Core / Media / MediaControls`.
Source and automated checks do not establish viewport or design approval.

## 2026-10-12 role cleanup and migration

| Removed or renamed                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Replacement                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--geul-action-hover`                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `--geul-surface-hover` (identical in all four presets)                  |
| `--geul-action-pressed`                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `--geul-surface-active` (identical in all four presets)                 |
| `--geul-chrome-action-size` / `primitiveTokens.chrome['action-size']`                                                                                                                                                                  | `--geul-control-height-chrome`                                          |
| `--geul-breakpoints-*`                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `primitiveTokens.breakpoints` (JS) or `$mantine-breakpoint-*` (PostCSS) |
| `text-image-chrome`, `shadow-image-chrome`, `paper-border-soft`, `overlay-muted`, `overlay-video-status`, `overlay-border-muted`, `overlay-caption`, `overlay-spinner-border`, `shadow-media`, `shadow-map-panel`, `shadow-image-text` | None; no consumer existed                                               |

`action-boundary` remains: it is the meaningful outline of an outlined command, distinct from
`border-strong` (input underline and control outline). Ocean Dark no longer repeats base-dark
values for `background` and `surface-hover`. In the light theme `action-warning`,
`-hover` and `-pressed` now use yellow 700/800/900 so pressed differs from hover, matching
the accent/positive/danger ramps; label contrast on the lightest fill is 4.72:1.

New layer roles `sticky`, `banner`, `floating`, `toast` and `progress` replace Core and
Feature numeric literals (100, 999/1000, 150, 1000, 10000). Toasts moved from `tooltip` to
`toast`. A copied stylesheet that names a removed variable must migrate to the replacement.

## Extension rules

1. Use an existing Core component and named role first. Adjust composition through Core Layout.
2. If the shared component cannot express a recurring requirement, extend its closed Core
   contract and update its consumers, stories and type/runtime checks together.
3. Add a token only for a reusable meaning that existing roles cannot express. A one-off value
   or another spelling of an existing role is insufficient.
4. Keep state/size calculations private (`--_...`) and derived from registered tokens. No
   additional public feature-level palette or spacing scale is permitted.
5. Authored documents, provider identities, canvas/map and physical print geometry have their
   documented owners. Their independent dimensions do not authorize arbitrary product chrome.

## Verification

`generate-tokens.mjs` rejects missing foundations, alias chains and differences between a derived
TypeScript role and its foundation. Generated CSS must match the authority. Projection tests
check both JavaScript values and CSS references.

Token, responsive, layout, framework and action checks enforce the existing presentation
boundaries. Type/runtime tests cover the affected Core APIs. Actual browser screenshots verify
alignment, themes, localized text and phone layouts. Passing a source scan alone is not visual
approval; untyped/dynamic composition still needs review.

Application type checks exclude the `stories` tree consistently in both the default and local
contract projects. `.storybook/tsconfig.json` owns story fixtures and interaction tests and must
also pass. The local contract project does not relax dependency declaration checking to absorb
Storybook-only declarations. The token audit counts authored color definitions by their durable
role names, whether their generated values are literals or references to shared palette tokens.
The shared Storybook fixture projector also localizes React elements/fragments in action slots
and action arrays; it preserves event handlers, identifiers and authored row values. Header and
toolbar previews must exercise these composed slots under the locale and theme toolbar.

Core EditorHeader's collaboration indicator is an example: its glyph consumes the shared icon
token, numeric size overrides are closed, and the status/title and action groups align centrally.
Post, Page, Work and Policy editors consume this owner rather than patching local margins.

documents.title: Toolbar API review
documents.markdown:
# Toolbar API review

Reviewed: 2026-10-12, following Field. Scope: Core and actual editor/translation consumer code.
Source/type/jsdom findings are separate from product browser review. Visual approval at 390/834/1440px and Light/Dark/locales, actual touch and screen-reader checks are separate.

## Owned contracts

| Owner          | API / layout / behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ToolbarLayout  | arrangement=flow/actions-end/actions-inline; density=compact/comfortable (default compact); justify=between/start/end/center; inset=none/content; divider=none/surface. Places search/filters/actions/optional leading. Preserves ordinary Tab flow and native input keys; does not automatically add role=toolbar or roving tabindex |
| ToolbarSurface | Requires label. wrap=wrap/nowrap (default wrap), width=content/full, appearance=floating/embedded/inline, density=comfortable/compact (default comfortable). Core owns surface/boundary/shadow/wrap/overflow and command ArrowLeft/Right/Home/End                                                                                     |
| ToolbarCommand | Requires label; presentation=label/icon/responsive (default label), icon required for icon/responsive. Consumes tone/emphasis/loading/disabled and native command semantics. Rejects size/children/leftSection/rightSection and visual overrides. Reuses Button/IconButton and Tooltip                                                |

ToolbarLayout flow uses children; slot arrangements use leading/search/filters/actions.
actions-inline DOM order is leading → search → filters → actions, while CSS places actions in the first visual row. The visual/Tab-order difference needs product browser review.
API types and ToolbarLayout runtime variant checks remain. Expanding unsupported-string runtime checks for ToolbarSurface was outside this correction.

## Actual keyboard and state implementation

### Contextual editor presentation

Text, map, external-video, code, table and executable selection menus consume the same Core
ToolbarSurface `density="compact"` and `wrap="nowrap"`. Core owns icon target size, glyph frame,
focus and overflow; Features supply domain commands. Width readouts are named passive status
outputs with resize instructions, centered alongside commands rather than placed in a private
fixed-height wrapper or adapted into focusable tooltip triggers.

Executable runtime/source commands remain on the executable's own surface. Its floating
selection menu contains only block alignment and deletion, avoiding a second run/stop/source
control set. Nested title inputs and Monaco temporarily suppress selection bubbles while
retaining document selection; returning focus to the document restores the eligible menu.
Escape dismissal, toolbar arrow navigation and Tab exit retain their separate behavior.

Review `Feature / Editor / Menus` (Formatting Bubble, Map Controls, External Video Controls,
Table Selection) and `Feature / Editor / Executables` (P 5, Three, Shader). These are production
adapters, including the actual editor-backed stories; they are not a Storybook-only UI.

ToolbarSurface currently uses div role=toolbar with its own keyboard handler; child Button/IconButton uses React Aria.
Installed React Aria Components 1.22.1 includes Toolbar/useToolbar, but Surface does not use that primitive.
Its installed capture handler changes nested Toolbar to group and owns Tab movement. Replacing Surface would also change native-input and editor-consumer capture-level roving contracts.

| Check                    | Result / limitation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Arrow / Home / End / RTL | Moves among the current toolbar's enabled visible commands; end arrows wrap. Computed CSS direction reverses RTL arrows. Home/End follow DOM first/last commands                                                                                                      |
| disabled / pending       | Excludes native disabled and aria-disabled commands. Pending activation blocking and aria-busy names/state were checked with the upstream shared Button correction                                                                                                    |
| Nested groups            | Candidates must have the same closest role=toolbar. Inner navigation does not join outer candidates. Inner density overrides parent density                                                                                                                           |
| Input / consumer keys    | Does not intercept input/textarea/select arrows or reprocess preventDefault keys. Does not duplicate editor onKeyDownCapture roving ownership                                                                                                                         |
| Tab                      | ToolbarLayout keeps ordinary native Tab order. Default Surface does not globally rewrite child tabIndex. Editor SelectionBubbleMenu uses separate useSelectionToolbarNavigation for single entry/Tab exit/restoration. Not every Surface provides single-entry roving |
| Responsive touch         | Below sm, responsive uses icons for fine pointers; any-pointer:coarse retains visible labels. Explicit icon stays icon on touch. Names/click behavior remain                                                                                                          |
| Long labels / themes     | Label presentation uses Button labelWrap=wrap and named xs targets. Shared Control and token/theme owners define touch targets/type/state colors/contrast. jsdom does not verify final wrapping/contrast                                                              |

## Reproduced correction

CSS display:none commands remained candidates, blocking arrows or moving focus incorrectly. The filter now excludes computed visibility and display:none from control through toolbar ancestors.
Native :disabled also excludes commands disabled by a parent fieldset. Existing hidden/inert/aria-hidden, aria-disabled, nested-owner filters and consumer key handlers remain.

Toolbar CSS has a separate owner. spacing-role-toolbar-item and spacing-role-action-group alias existing values; compact Surface gap/padding=0 is an explicit existing exception.
This keyboard correction did not change CSS/token values or product copy.

## Actual consumers and browser fixtures

| Consumer path                                                                   | Story / task to inspect                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| EntityTranslationsPanel → TranslationLocaleRow ToolbarSurface + ToolbarCommand  | feature-translation-localerows--expanded / --read-only / --phone / --tablet / --desktop: translation add/review/errors, long locales and responsive actions                                                 |
| SelectionBubbleMenu / selection navigation hook                                 | feature-editor-menus--formatting-bubble / --selection-bubble / --map-controls / --external-video-controls: capture-level roving, Tab exit, editor-focus return and retained selection                       |
| TiptapTableMenu / CodeBlockSurface                                              | feature-editor-menus--table-selection / --code-selection; feature-editor-source-editor--standard / --compact / --read-only: nested commands and native editor keys                                          |
| DataTableToolbar / DataTableSelectionToolbar / SelectionToolbar → ToolbarLayout | pages-admin-content-lists--posts, pages-admin-file-manager--browser: ordinary search/filter/selection/action Tab order and container layout                                                                 |
| New Core fixtures                                                               | core-layout-toolbarsurface--navigation-states: input/pending/disabled/hidden/nested density; core-actions-toolbarcommand--long-label: long translated commands, responsive, Light/Dark and pointer branches |

Sources: [ToolbarSurface](../../components/core/Section/ToolbarSurface.tsx), [ToolbarLayout](../../components/core/Section/ToolbarLayout.tsx),
[ToolbarCommand](../../components/core/Section/ToolbarCommand.tsx), [editor navigation](../../features/editor/tiptap/menus/useSelectionToolbarNavigation.ts) and [shared control context](../../components/core/control-context.tsx).

Checks passed: six test files / 45 tests covering ToolbarSurface/ToolbarLayout/ToolbarCommand, useSelectionToolbarNavigation, SelectionBubbleMenu and EntityTranslationsPanel.
Pending integration includes the upstream Button aria-busy correction. Core type-test and added-story scoped typing passed with skipLibCheck. Changed TSX lint/format were run separately.
jsdom logged unimplemented canvas getContext during execution, without test failures.
These Toolbar results do not establish completed Table or AppDialog changes/checks.

# Translation, site identity, avatar and legal history presentation

This contract records the adopted presentation changes and their source boundaries.
It does not establish complete browser, server or assistive technology verification.

## Translation languages and state

[TranslationLocaleRow](../../features/translation/TranslationLocaleRow.tsx) displays the language name once.
The locale code remains its data/selection identity and is not repeated as a visual EN/JA-style label.
[Panel locale options](../../features/translation/useTranslationPanelLabels.ts) also use names.
The shared [option formatter](../../features/translation/locale-option-format.ts) removes only a matching trailing code suffix;
meaningful qualifiers such as `Português (Brasil)` remain. Submitted locale values do not change.
Source options retain their translated source-language indication.
The shared [TranslationLocaleControl](../../features/translation/TranslationLocaleControl.tsx) also uses the language
name in menu triggers, including compact Page and Post editor headers. Compact density changes control geometry,
not the language's identity. The trigger shows `한국어`, `English`, `日本語` or the supplied language name;
matching code suffixes are removed, while regional qualifiers remain. Menu source options and the trigger's
accessible name retain their source-language context. Locale values and change callbacks remain unchanged.
[ContentLanguageMenu](../../features/translation/ContentLanguageMenu.tsx) applies the same name convention to public
content, using the native names from the supported locale registry. The current displayed language remains selected
even when the requested language falls back to the source.

[EntityTranslationsPanel](../../features/translation/EntityTranslationsPanel.tsx) no longer repeats Existing/Missing badges.
Missing targets retain their explanatory text. Updated-at context remains when available.
Queued/running summaries, actual job badges, cancellation, generation/regeneration, create/edit/preview/delete,
permissions, errors, notifications and save-before-mutation behavior remain intact.
The source-language field is the primary source indicator; there is no duplicated source row.
Collapsed/expanded behavior and live status relationships remain owned by the existing disclosure/row contracts.

Review [LocaleRows stories](../../features/translation/TranslationLocaleRow.stories.tsx) in Collapsed, Expanded,
ReadOnly and Active states, and the existing actual EntityTranslationsPanel fixtures.
The local row fixture does not submit a generation job; production mutation tests use mocked services.

## Site logo and title fallback

[SiteLogo](../../features/site/SiteLogo/SiteLogo.tsx) uses the configured theme asset as before.
[SiteLogoView](../../features/site/ui/SiteLogo/SiteLogoView.tsx) renders the site title when no asset exists or an asset fails.
If identity is absent, it displays `LOGO` rather than returning an empty slot or using the image's descriptive alt as identity.
A changed asset URL can render a new image after a failed source.

The optional `size` API is closed to existing Core Typography xs/sm/md/lg/xl roles, default md.
Fallback text uses that named role with medium weight; it does not introduce a separate font scale.
Without an explicit asset height, the image uses the corresponding existing font-size token.
Legacy numeric `height` and image `style` remain authored asset geometry; they do not override fallback typography.
The controller supplies configured site identity explicitly; direct View fixtures can use `fallbackText` or their identity alt.

Review Default, Missing, MissingXL, Unconfigured and UnavailableAsset in the
[SiteLogo stories](../../features/site/ui/SiteLogo/SiteLogoView.stories.tsx).
Image alt, theme-asset selection and CDN resolution retain their existing responsibilities.

## Avatar removal

[ProfileAvatarControl](../../features/user/ui/ProfileAvatarControl/ProfileAvatarControl.tsx) keeps removal as an actual Core IconButton.
Its existing compact density context selects the 28px fine-pointer target; the common coarse-pointer minimum remains 44px.
The glyph remains the original 16px Core icon frame, with no path cropping or new icon scale.

The approved avatar-specific treatment uses danger/strong, providing a red default fill from existing action roles.
[ImageUploadField](../../components/core/ImageUpload/ImageUploadField.tsx) exposes only `removeButtonEmphasis="medium"|"strong"`.
Its default remains medium, with existing danger tone and xs geometry for ordinary consumers.
The avatar consumes strong inside its compact context. The crop dialog is outside that context.
No public tone override, raw color, numeric action size or new token was added.

Removal names, pending/disabled restrictions, upload validation, crop cancellation/save, controller persistence,
notifications and session updates remain intact. Check Empty and WithImage in the
[avatar stories](../../features/user/ui/ProfileAvatarControl/ProfileAvatarControl.stories.tsx).

## Legal history status

Public terms and privacy headings use the localized document title in current, scheduled-preview and history-detail views.
The heading follows the displayed content language, including source-language fallback, and carries that language's
`lang` with `dir="auto"`. The surrounding notices and controls use the site UI language. The entity label is the
fallback when no document title is available. Core Heading owns the existing title typography; no new tokens or styles
are required. Review [Arabic privacy content](http://localhost:6010/?path=/story/pages-legal-public-document--arabic-privacy-content)
and SourceLanguageFallback in the [public legal stories](../../stories/pages/Legal.stories.tsx).

[LegalPolicyHistoryClient](../../features/policy/LegalPolicyHistoryClient.tsx) renders Current/Archived using sm Core Text.
These are plain status labels without a colored badge surface.
Version links, language query parameters, effective dates, table headers, server snapshots, loading and error behavior remain unchanged.
This presentation change does not alter legal content or policy lifecycle status.

Review [Legal History](../../stories/pages/LegalHistory.stories.tsx) for privacy/terms and archived/current rows.
History-detail rendering and server persistence are separate contracts.

## Verification scope

Relevant regressions check compact header/native and regional language names, source-aware accessible names,
displayed-language fallback selection, preserved missing/job actions and mutations,
site-title/LOGO/asset-error fallback, named-size types, ordinary upload defaults, avatar removal and legal table relationships.
Record browser theme, locale, viewport, pointer, focus and actual observed geometry separately.
Story existence, a prop marker or a DOM test does not prove all viewport layouts or assistive technology behavior.

documents.title: Version history
documents.markdown:
# Version history

Review earlier source checkpoints for a Post, Page or Work and restore one through an explicit confirmation.
The same production controller and View are used by the three editors.

## Ownership and layout

| Responsibility                                                                    | Owner                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Compact width, inset, fixed header, body scrolling and focus restoration          | Core `Drawer`, `density="compact"`, `size="compact"` |
| Title and metadata hierarchy                                                      | Core Typography and Layout                           |
| Automatic continuation, keyboard fallback, pending, error, retry and end feedback | Core `NearEndLoader`                                 |
| Numeric pagination, entity identity and loaded versions                           | `useVersionHistoryQuery`                             |
| Permission, restore request and source-locale warning                             | `VersionHistoryDrawer`                               |
| Final restore confirmation                                                        | Shared `ConfirmationDialog`, intent `restore`        |

Each row puts the title first, followed by version, source locale and time. Contributors follow as secondary text.
Restore is the rightmost row action and uses Core's ordinary neutral/medium treatment.
The list uses the Drawer body as its only scroll owner; it does not add a nested ScrollArea.
The Core loader finds the closest scrolling ancestor and loads automatically near the end.

The relative timestamp is passive text inside native `time` with its ISO `datetime`.
The localized absolute timestamp is always present and connected through `aria-describedby`; native `title`
provides supplementary pointer feedback. Timestamp metadata adds no keyboard stop.
Each Restore control describes the version, title, locale and absolute time.

## Pagination and storage evidence

The production web client requests 20 versions per page. The GET route accepts `page >= 1`,
`pageSize` from 1 through 100, and an offset no greater than 2,147,483,647.
The web server adapter translates pages into `(limit, offset)` and exposes the returned total.
The Post, Page and Work API handlers order by `version DESC`, count the stored rows, and return
`total`, `limit`, `offset` and `has_more`. The installed TypeScript contract uses int32 pagination fields.
The 100-row limit is a web request page-size limit, not a limit on the number of retained versions.

`useVersionHistoryQuery` requests consecutive pages until the latest total is reached.
It uses the requested page offset, rather than the number of deduplicated rows, to calculate continuation.
It removes repeated IDs caused by mutable offset boundaries while keeping the loaded order.
An empty response stops continuation. If total metadata is absent, only a full 20-row response continues.
Requests carry an AbortSignal, duplicate pending continuation requests share the same query, and errors
retain earlier rows. A failed page requires explicit retry; it does not start an automatic request loop.

Inspected local source on 2026-10-12:

- Client and route: `lib/client/version-history.ts`, `app/api/version-history/[entityType]/[entityId]/route.ts`,
  `lib/server/version-history.ts`.
- Contract: `geul-event-contracts/proto/api/common/v1/common.proto:31` and the Post/Page/Work version messages
  in `proto/api/manage/v1`.
- Listing: `geul-api/internal/post/versions.go:73`, `page/versions.go:26`, `work/versions.go:27`.
- Checkpoint creation compares the latest snapshot, skips identical content, and otherwise increments
  the version number and inserts a row: `post/internal_service.go:699`, `page/internal_service.go:760`,
  `work/internal_service.go:581`.
- Owner deletion removes its history: `post/service.go:615`, `page/service.go:522`, `work/service.go:693`.
  The corresponding schema foreign keys use `ON DELETE CASCADE` at `geul-schema/schema.sql:9341`, `9201`, `10237`.

No implemented per-history count or age cap was found in the inspected local API, schema, contracts and
deployment source. The audit included checkpoint creation, registered scheduler/worker jobs, version-table
deletion, retention, prune, TTL and maximum-history settings. Generated code, vendor code, tests and secret
configuration were excluded from that policy search. Live database jobs and external cleanup were not inspected.
Version counters and pagination metadata use int32/SQL integer fields. This is not a claim of unlimited
storage on the deployed server.

## States and review

| Story                                                                                                                                 | Task                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Populated](http://localhost:6010/?path=/story/feature-version-history-versionhistorydrawerview--populated)                           | Inspect metadata, select Restore, cancel and return focus to its row              |
| Empty                                                                                                                                 | Explain why no checkpoint exists                                                  |
| Loading / Initial Error                                                                                                               | Await the first page or retry its bounded failure                                 |
| [Automatic Continuation](http://localhost:6010/?path=/story/feature-version-history-versionhistorydrawerview--automatic-continuation) | Scroll through three fixture pages without a persistent load-more button          |
| Loading More / Page Error                                                                                                             | Keep loaded rows while the next page is pending or failed; retry that page        |
| Restore Locked                                                                                                                        | Read history while restoration is unavailable                                     |
| Restore Confirmation / Restoring                                                                                                      | Review the source-locale effect and keep the owned operation locked while pending |

The View stories simulate service data and restoration callbacks. Automatic Continuation uses the actual
View and Core loader with three 20-row fixture pages. Controller and query tests exercise the actual query
and HTTP client with controlled responses, including more than 100 retained rows, failure recovery,
entity isolation and request cancellation. These checks do not prove deployed permissions or a successful
live restore.

Review at mobile, tablet and desktop widths with every named theme and locale. Check that the header stays
visible while the body scrolls, titles can shrink beside the right action, metadata wraps without horizontal
overflow, and appended rows preserve earlier entries. Check automatic loading, end feedback and explicit retry.
Verify the restore warning, pending lock and focus return separately. Browser axe and manual keyboard results
must be recorded with their actual scope; no VoiceOver or Orca result is implied by unit tests.

## Source and compatibility

- Controller: [VersionHistoryDrawer](../../features/version-history/VersionHistoryDrawer.tsx).
- Query: [useVersionHistoryQuery](../../features/version-history/useVersionHistoryQuery.ts).
- View and fixtures: [VersionHistoryDrawerView](../../features/version-history/ui/VersionHistoryDrawerView.tsx)
  and [stories](../../features/version-history/ui/VersionHistoryDrawerView.stories.tsx).

The View now requires initial error/retry and pagination props. Pagination contains the entity context key,
next numeric page or null, pending/error state and an awaited loading callback. Labels include continuation,
bounded load failure, end and retry. Row models include the ISO timestamp alongside relative and absolute text.
The production controller and all shipped View fixtures migrate together. Restore payloads and permission
rules are unchanged. Regenerate the Storybook documentation through the shared design-system workflow.
